News.title: Huw Edwards reacts angrily when challenged over child abuse crimes in new documentary
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Disgraced newsreader Huw Edwards furiously snaps at a journalist when questioned about his crimes in a trailer for Channel 4’s interview of him, set to air next Tuesday.

Edwards, 65, resigned from his longstanding position at the BBC in 2024 after allegations of grooming surfaced; he was subsequently convicted of making indecent images of children, and received a six-month suspended prison sentence. Edwards was never charged with a criminal offence in relation to grooming.

Two years on, Edwards is being interviewed and profiled for the first time on TV since his criminal conviction in Channel 4 documentary Huw Edwards – Guilty. The channel describes the forthcoming film as “an uncomfortable portrayal of what happens when a previously beloved public figure betrays the trust of the people”, which asks “what accountability really means in the wake of a serious criminal conviction”.

A short trailer for the programme sees Edwards lose his temper with the journalist interviewing him, saying when asked about his crimes: “You want me to analyse what I was doing? I mean, seriously?”

“What do you think you were doing?” the journalist asks him in the clip, to which Edwards claims: “I’d lost the plot.” After the interviewer remarks, “Oh, come on,” a seething Edwards interrupts him to say: “No, not ‘come on’.”

Sacha Mirzoeff, Channel 4’s senior commissioning editor, said in a statement: “Channel 4 has an established reputation for tackling controversial subjects through exemplary filmmaking. Huw Edwards – Guilty is no exception in its quest for answers from a man who is trying to come to terms with his abuse of power.”

Director Patrick Forbes described it as “an important film to make”.

“It’s rare to find a subject that touches on so many significant contemporary issues – whether it’s celebrity culture or the power of the media – as well as enduring questions about crime and punishment,” he added.

Deadline reports that Edwards was not paid for his participation in the documentary, and was not given any editorial control.

Huw Edwards seen leaving court ( PA )

The programme will constitute Edwards’s first televised interview since his widely publicised fall from grace; he has previously addressed the scandal in his Substack newsletter.

Before his downfall, Edwards was one of the most respected figures in British journalism, having presented a number of series at the BBC over the course of four decades, including BBC News at Six, BBC News at One, and on BBC World News.

He was known for covering many of the biggest news events of the century, and announced the death of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022.

In court, Edwards admitted to possessing 41 indecent images of children, sent to him over WhatsApp by another man who police revealed to be a convicted paedophile.

Included in the count were seven Category A images, the most serious criminal classification, two of which featured a child aged between the age of seven and nine. Following his conviction, Edwards was placed on the sex offenders’ register.

The scandal was depicted in a Channel 5 drama earlier this year, titled Power: The Downfall of Huw Edwards, in which he was portrayed by Martin Clunes.

News.title: Milk of human kindness: How Brazil’s donor breastfeeding programme is being exported worldwide
News.content:
When baby Luis Miguel was born in Guarapuava, Brazil, in February, he was unresponsive.

He had inhaled meconium, a newborn’s first stool, during delivery. It then entered his lungs and blocked his airways. Doctors at Hospital de Caridade São Vicente de Paulo resuscitated and intubated the baby boy, saving his life. He spent the next three weeks in the hospital’s neonatal unit.

His mother, 25-year-old sales assistant Luany Thainara Machado, could not produce enough breast milk and so hers was supplemented with that of a woman she had never met.

“While it might not make much sense for a mother to do this under normal circumstances it becomes very important when the need arises,” she said.

Nine months later, Luis Miguel is healthy and Machado is grateful that donor milk was able to support her son when he needed it most; so much so that today she donates 2.5 litres of her now plentiful supply every week. “Being able to help other mothers and other babies today, it feels really good,” she told The Telegraph, bouncing Luis Miguel on her knee as she spoke.

News.title: One person had a worse night than United keeper – the wretched referee
News.content:
Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

The manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

United are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Sporting are well-placed after three wins from four, but their Champions League schedule is rather one-sided: in their final three matches they travel to Roma, before playing Barcelona and Manchester City. They reached the quarter-finals of the competition last season, losing narrowly to Arsenal over two legs.

They are third in their league, having been weakened by the summer sales of Geovany Quenda (to Chelsea), Morten Hjulmand (to Atletico Madrid) and Ousmane Diomande (to Nottingham Forest). The vast majority of goals are scored by Colombian striker Luis Suárez.

Bruno Fernandes, United’s captain, returns to his former club tonight and there is hope Luke Shaw could be back at left-back. Pochettino must decide whether or not to stick with Matthijs de Ligt, who was extremely rusty at Anfield but may need the minutes.

Yoro’s one-game suspension was overturned by the FA, and he would have been available for this one in any case.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Wirtz follows rich Liverpool heritage with star showing in win over Brugge
News.content:
“A knock on the knee and we have to test it,” Iraola said. “That was the worst part of the night. It is very early to tell but it was very painful at that moment. He was better after the game.”

So, too, was Iraola, who was especially pleased that Liverpool recorded their first Champions League clean sheet of the season and, in the process, stopped Brugge – who had scored in 19 consecutive games – from finding a way through.

There were several reasons this was the case: Jérémy Jacquet, for instance, never put a foot wrong – what a smart signing he has proved to be. He more than did his bit to retain order in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, who was given the chance to catch his breath before the Merseyside derby.

It was tough for Liverpool in the second period, as Brugge attacked the end of the stadium where their noisy ultras created a cacophony. Yet they handled the situation well, even if Iraola looked ready to combust at one stage, receiving a yellow card for protesting too much to the officials.

“I saw the referee beforehand, I know him from Spain and I knew this was coming,” Iraola said.

Perhaps his ire was fuelled by Liverpool squandering a fabulous chance on the hour to kill things off. A move that featured Wirtz and Isak exchanging passes with pinball precision ended with Szoboszlai bearing down on Sommer, but his shot was too close to the veteran.

He had to score and the grimace that followed had nothing to do with heavy strapping the Hungarian had on supporting his right knee. That miss would have been exacerbated in the 69th minute had Alisson Becker not made a superb save to deny Félix Lemaréchal, plunging to avert the danger.

News.title: ‘It blocks out the sun’: The toxic dust storms choking Uzbekistan
News.content:
In the early hours of the morning last June, Gulbara Aminova woke up with a violent fit of coughing. The 39-year-old got up to shut her bedroom windows. But as she did, she saw something disturbing outside.

“My car was covered in powder,” says Aminova, a resident of the town of Moynaq in western Uzbekistan. “It was like it had been snowing. But it was the summer.”

The fine dust on her car was far from a picturesque snow scene: it was in fact a toxic mix of salt and sand laced with pesticides and other chemicals, blown in by strong winds during the night. The dirty air had been making it difficult for Aminova and her three children to breathe at night.

For the residents of Moynaq, a former fishing town on the edge of the Aral Sea, these storms have become a public health emergency, with fears that they are behind not only air pollution spikes but high rates of cancer, tuberculosis and other diseases.

“Two of my daughters have asthma,” says Aminova. “I lost my father and my aunt to cancer. There is a lot of sickness here. I think it’s because of the dust.”

Today, sand and dust storms strike as many as a 100 times a year in Uzbekistan, many of them originating in the desiccated wastelands that decades ago were home to the world’s fourth-largest lake.

News.title: Mick Harford: ‘My prostate cancer diagnosis was a shock. As a footballer, I’d felt bulletproof’
News.content:
However, an MRI scan and a PSMA PET scan at UCLH, where I had been referred, showed only a little bit of growth on my prostate, and I was told I would be fine. But, while I was symptomless at the time, within around eight months I was getting up three or four times in the night to go to the toilet, and then feeling the urge to go back again only two minutes later. I instinctively knew something was wrong.

Upon my return to UCLH in December, I was told my PSA was now “very high”, at around 48 ng/mL – far more elevated than the 4.5 ng/mL considered healthy for my age group. Advanced prostate cancer was then confirmed with a biopsy. The first person I told was my son, William, in a phone call from the car at the hospital. It was horrible – it was not just me who would suffer, but my family too. I also needed to tell Luton Town, who were amazing and gave me as much time off work as I needed from my role as assistant manager.

Facing the opponent

My brilliant oncology team immediately had a plan for me. They got me on a course of hormone therapy medications called Enzalutamide and Zoladex, in preparation for me to begin radiation treatment from mid-August. I had 49 sessions over the space of about eight weeks, and it was daunting each time I travelled into London on the train from my home in Harpenden to go underground to the hospital’s Radiotherapy Department.

But I got through it, even with a bit of collateral damage. While my ongoing symptoms are not a pleasant conversation, it’s an important one, because it has affected my life in so many ways. My sleep is disrupted because I still need to get up multiple times during the night to go to the toilet so I can avoid an accident in bed. I also have to wear a nappy every day in case of leakage, and need to be careful when I’m out to ensure I’m close to a toilet.

I’m still on a hormone therapy called Triptorelin to block my testosterone, which feeds the cancer, and takes the form of an injection every six months. As a result, I’m going through the “male menopause”, which is not very nice and can cause tiredness, sleep issues and brain fog. It has given me lots of sympathy for women of my generation.

However, as I approach six years since my diagnosis, I’ve tried to stay proactive as much as possible. The discipline and drive instilled in me as a footballer have come in handy. To be a successful player, you need to stick to a routine. In the same way that I worked hard to ensure my teammates and coaches respected me on the pitch, so I’ve adhered to what all the doctors have advised – including trying to be diligent in terms of lifestyle.

News.title: Underperforming Manchester City are an accident waiting to happen
News.content:
Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

Maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

News.title: Arsenal get the best and worst of Gyokeres on frustrating night for Arteta
News.content:
Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

News.title: Emery unhappy with ‘unfair’ referee but Aston Villa are toothless
News.content:
Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”

Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Reason Amar Dedic had bow and arrow revealed after police scrambled HELICOPTER to pursue Newcastle star
Sports.content:
Next

AMAR DEDIC and a pal were firing arrows at a tree before being stopped by cops earlier this month, according to reports.

The Newcastle star, 24, inadvertently sparked a police manhunt after being spotted with a bow and arrow in Northumberland.



A concerned member of the public dialled law enforcement after thinking they’d just spotted someone with a “crossbow”.

Six cop cars subsequently chased Dedic, before a HELICOPTER was even deployed.



The Bosnian was eventually found with a friend around seven miles from the Darras Hall estate on the outskirts of the city.

When it was determined that he posed no threat to public safety, the full-back was allowed to go – although his archery equipment was confiscated.

According to the Mail, Dedic and his friend had merely been trying to hit a tree with their archery equipment.

They were NOT hunting animals or people, rather just attempting to get their arrows into the trunk.

Dedic’s Toon team-mate Mark Gillespie and ex-Newcastle defender Paul Dummett happened to be in the area by chance.

And the duo were on hand to help Dedic as he was quizzed by cops.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The summer signing from Benfica did not initially comment on the incident.

But after Newcastle posted on Instagram that he’d received an international call-up, Dedic poked fun at what had happened.

He playfully commented on the post with a picture of Legolas from Lord of the Rings clutching his own bow and arrow.

Dedic did not miss any matches following the incident.

The defender has so far played 12 times for the Magpies, most recently in their 2-2 draw with Arsenal last weekend.



Newcastle return to action on Sunday as they travel to high-flying Brighton.

Sports.title: Man Utd claimed Alexander Isak was too slow to get ball with expert analysis to get Leny Yoro red card overturned
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER United claimed Alexander Isak would have been six feet short of reaching the ball before keeper Senne Lammens in their successful appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card.

The written reasons for the three man commission overturning Yoro’s one man ban has been published by the FA.



United boss Mauricio Pochettino slammed ref Sam Barrott, VAR John Brooks over the call and then criticised ProRef boss Howard Webb for backing the decision in his side’s 4-0 loss to Liverpool.

Top flight officials are understood to be perplexed at the disciplinary escape, with a widespread belief that there was no “clear and obvious” reason for the initial onfield call to be overturned.



But the commission, headed by former England winger Stuart Ripley, “unanimously” accepted United’s case of “wrongful dismissal”, freeing Yoro to play against Brentford on Saturday.

Their report discloses that United argued their analytical evidence proved Isak would not have beaten Lammens – who was moving backwards when the Swedish striker was bundled over – to the ball.



The reasons stated: “The club letter (from United) included technical analysis calculating whether or not, Isak, had he maintained his speed and direction from the point of first contact, would have been able to reach the ball before it was gathered by the goalkeeper.

“The conclusion of this analysis was that Isak would have been, at best, 1.8m short of reaching the ball.

“It should be noted that the Commission had no way of testing the validity of this analysis undertaken by the Club and as such the evidence was viewed with caution and allocated weight accordingly.”

United also cited the decision to overturn a red card awarded – after a VAR intervention – to Brighton’s Pascal Struijk in their win at Sunderland.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And all three panel members – it was completed by ex-Sheffield United striker Tony Agana and former Walsall and Ireland goalkeeper Mick Kearns – backed United’s case.

The report added: “The Commission viewed the available footage of the incident on numerous occasions and considered carefully the written submissions from the club.

“Members unanimously considered there to have been a foul committed by Yoro but that Isak would not have had an obvious goal-scoring opportunity.

“Despite the fact that Isak had reached the ball initially, his touch was heavy to the extent that he had in fact lost control of the ball.

“That control had, in effect, passed to the advancing goalkeeper who in the view of the Commission would have been able to gather or smother the ball before Isak could get to it and shoot at goal.”



It is understood that, despite the commission verdict, the Prem’s Key Match Incident panel of former players, refs and coaches has backed both Barrott’s on-field call and Brooks’ decision not to intervene.

Sports.title: Premier League star Sven Botman BANNED from driving for six months after being caught using phone at the wheel
Sports.content:
Next

PREMIER LEAGUE star Sven Botman has been banned from driving after a cyclist filmed him using his phone while stuck in traffic.

The Newcastle United ace was spotted with both hands on his mobile when he was behind the wheel of his £90,000 Range Rover



The cyclist sent the footage to cops and the Dutch centre-half was hauled before the courts.

He had been due to stand trial but changed his plea to guilty.



He was already on nine points and was given another six after admitting the offence in his absence, resulting in a six-month ban.

The cyclist had peered through the footballer’s car window in South Gosforth, Newcastle, on September 17 last year.



Prosecutor Ruth Forster told Newcastle JPs that Botman, 26, was “in a queue of traffic” and his car was stationary.

David Forrester, mitigating, said: “This case is unfortunate because there is a limited level of risk to what Mr Botman was doing.

“At the time, he was in traffic.

“It is unfortunate people think it is appropriate to peer into cars but the law is the law.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

District Judge Paul Currer also handed Botman, who pleaded guilty to using a handheld mobile phone while driving, a £900 fine and ordered him to pay a surcharge of £360 and costs of £400, totalling £1,660.

Botman began his career in the Netherlands before moving to Lille in France.

Eddie Howe signed him for Newcastle in 2022.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans fume ‘they sold our best centre-back and left us with garbage’ as Chalobah’s incredible Como stats revealed

THE answer to Chelsea’s defensive woes may have been allowed to walk out of the door in August.

Xabi Alonso‘s reign has been blighted by issues at centre-back, with the Blues conceding 20 goals in 11 Premier League outings — six more than any other team in the top half of the table.



Summer signing Maxence Lacroix is in the treatment room, while Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill were bullied by Leeds target man Dominic Calvert-Lewin in a humbling 4-1 defeat at Stamford Bridge.

Meanwhile, academy graduate Trevoh Chalobah, 27, is starring in Serie A and Europe for Cesc Fabregas‘ Como.



WhoScored riled up the Blues faithful in a post on X which revealed that the former Chelsea defender has the best pass accuracy (97.1 percent) of any Champions League player to manage over 250 minutes this season.

Supporters are fuming that not only are their side not involved, they now have to watch the man who left for £26million enjoying himself on the biggest stage.



They took out their anger in posts aimed at Clearlake Capital Group, who own Chelsea, while others suggested that fans should have appreciated the CB more last season.

One wrote: “They sold our best CB for pure profit and left us with garbage. #ClearlakeOut.”

Another blasted: “CLOWNLAKE OUT.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That point was backed up as a fellow supporter added: “You can’t blame his sale on anyone but Chelsea fans, they drove him out the club as much as they can, he wanted to stay.”



Whoever is to blame, it is obvious to anybody with eyes that central defence is a weakness for Alonso’s side.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher thinks a lack of size is an issue, using the example of his time at Liverpool when 6ft 4in giant Sami Hyypia came in and instantly made an impact.

It is not an easy task to pick up big men who are also capable of playing the technical football Alonso demands.

Sports.title: ‘From Upton Park to this’ – West Ham fans rage as club introduce POTTED PLANTS to London Stadium stands
Sports.content:

WEST HAM fans are up in arms after the club introduced potted plants behind one of their goals.

The Hammers have had a torrid time in the Championship of late and remain winless in their last six, including a 1-0 defeat away to Portsmouth this week.

The club sit 13th in the league and are set to host high-flying Stoke City on Saturday.



Following their relegation from the Premier League last season, the mood around the London Stadium has been far from positive.



And the addition of some pot plants between the lower and upper tiers behind one goal has made it worse.

Moving from the beloved Upton Park to the London Stadium was already judged as a questionable decision by fans.

Fans of other clubs took the West Ham uproar as a chance to remind the suffering supporters of their current issues on the pitch.

Sports.title: Fifa reveals it has been HACKED after ‘criminal cyber attack’ as reports claim financial records were accessed
Sports.content:
Next

FIFA has revealed that it was cyber attacked by criminal hackers.

World football‘s governing body is now working with authorities following the major data breach.



Hackers are said to have gained access to confidential information by impersonating and taking advantage of Fifa staff – with no tech failure at fault.

Fifa bosses say that “personal and business information” was stolen.



Credit for the cyber attack appears to have been claimed by a group of hackers calling themselves the “Handsome Boy Hacking Club”.

They claim to have stolen more than 12 gigabytes of confidential Fifa info.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyber-attack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.

“FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.

“FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data.

“Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has seen his authority severely challenged since the World Cup last summer.

The Swiss, 56, saw his hated Fifa Forward Enterprise – which would have seen stakes in the World Cup sold to private investors – fall apart.

Infantino is also set to be challenged in the next Fifa presidential election in March by Philippe Diallo and Kohzo Tashima.

SunSport understands that the recent data breach does not include any data pertaining to the Fifa Forward Enterprise.



Fifa believes that less than 0.1 per cent of the data at their disposal was breached in the attack.

Football’s global governing body was ordered to hand over all documents relating to the failed World Cup sell-off plot following a legal challenge by Uefa.

Bosses from Uefa claim that the Fifa Forward Enterprise plan was initially hatched by Joshua Kushner – brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared – and had been discussed with Infantino for “nearly a year”.

Fifa lawyers then claimed that Uefa was attempting to usurp Infantino through a campaign of “misinformation”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Judge Jeanette Vargas dismissed Fifa’s argument, ruling that intervention would “unduly prejudice” Uefa if full disclosure was delayed.



That cleared the way for a final judgement on Uefa’s behalf, likely to have hugely embarrassed Fifa and Infantino.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich legend Joshua Kimmich slams OWN CLUB over ‘unacceptable’ treatment of Jamal Musiala amid medical condition

BAYERN MUNICH icon Joshua Kimmich has blasted his own club for its recent handling of contract talks with Jamal Musiala.

Musiala, 23, has been battling physical injury and a neurological condition which saw him collapse twice on the pitch with seizures in the summer, terrifying fans before he disclosed his illness in a statement.



Bayern Munich were aware of the ‘neurological dysfunction’ and are helping him treat and manage his health while assisting him in maintaining his playing career, where he is currently on around £18million-per-year.

But Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge opened the door to contract pressure and even the prospect of a pay cut for the German international as a result of his absence from the pitch.



He suggested: “We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible.

“I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.”

But Musiala’s team-mate and makeshift Bayern captain Kimmich has blasted the “absolute no-go” of airing out the contract situation in the media.

He told media after Bayern’s shock 2-1 loss to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday: “What happened now is something that simply must never happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.

“I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal’s agent or with Jamal himself. And I think the other side is open to that as well.

“I believe I’ve also read that they’ve met and are supposed to issue a statement. What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated publicly.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“It must never happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it.

“Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than us as players, but it’s not bigger than the person. And that’s an absolute no-go.

“It’s also not Bayern-like. Especially at this particular time, when I’ve often emphasised how special this club is.

“Even in my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out.”

Bayern released a statement on Wednesday confirming that talks between Musiala and the club are ongoing.



The statement read: “A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala.

“For both sides, the player’s health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back.

Sports.title: Wrong calls and bad results: Are refs making Man Utd's problems worse?
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino will need more than just good performances to turn Manchester United’s season around – refereeing decisions will have to go their way too.

Pochettino's first two games in charge have been plagued by controversial moments, following a similar pattern during the club's dreadful start, which has left them 19th, inside the Premier League relegation zone and out of the Carabao Cup.

United's luck appeared to be changing when Bruno Fernandes' shot was deflected in off a divot against Sporting on Wednesday, but the officials in Lisbon left Pochettino furious again as Amad Diallo's equaliser late in the first half was harshly ruled out for Youri Tielemans' foul in the build-up.

"It's difficult to answer as everyone saw it was impossible [to award a foul]," said Pochettino. "It's difficult to understand why that happened on the field."

Szymon Marciniak, referee in the 2022 World Cup final, had also already blown his whistle before Amad scored despite the forward being through on goal. Tielemans was booked for the tackle and the midfielder was later sent off after receiving a second yellow.

There was more controversy when United's third goal, and what they thought could be the winner, was ruled out following a VAR check. Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched the ball into his own net at a corner, although it was disallowed for Patrick Dorgu's foul.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino insists it's 'difficult to understand' why Amad Diallo's goal was ruled out for a foul on Sporting Lisbon keeper Kaique

Pochettino had already been complaining about officials this week with Leny Yoro's one-match suspension overturned on Tuesday after the defender was shown a straight red card with the score at 0-0 in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Yoro was dismissed for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity, although it appeared striker Alexander Isak wouldn't have reached the ball had the defender not fouled him.

Refereeing chief Howard Webb still backed the officials' process on Match Officials Mic'd Up, although he was non-committal when sharing his own verdict on the incident.

Pochettino also felt Liverpool's opening goal, scored by Dominik Szoboszlai from the free-kick conceded by Yoro, should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola was standing next to the Man Utd wall when the ball was struck.

Barcola appeared to be pushed towards the United defenders by Bruno Fernandes, revealing a grey area in the laws of the game, as they do not explain that type of incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Leny Yoro's overturned red card for Manchester United during their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino questioned VAR's involvement in the Frenchman's dismissal

What else has gone against Man Utd?

The most significant incident of United's season came prior to Pochettino's arrival when United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner in Manchester City's 1-0 win in September which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu, but Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland, and Webb acknowledged the error.

In the same game, Man Utd benefited from Man City's Phil Foden being sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, a decision only narrowly backed 3-2 by the Key Match Incidents panel, while the United captain wrongly avoided a yellow card despite initiating the incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Match Officials Mic'd Up, Pro Ref chief Howard Webb says that there will be a review into how the VAR process decided to allow Erling Haaland's goal for Manchester City against Manchester United to stand

Yoro's red card against Liverpool wasn't the first time he has been harshly sent off for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity this season.

The defender was shown a straight red card when United trailed 1-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last month and then lost 2-0.

Yoro brought down Atletico's Jonathan David, who was heading away from goal, after the pair came together just inside United's half. "It is soft! No way, that should not be a red," said Sky Sports' Clinton Morrison.

But surely they've had some decisions?

United have had some good fortune. In their only Premier League win of the season, Harry Maguire escaped punishment for a handball to put his side ahead against Ipswich.

Had the defender's shot gone straight into the net, it would have been disallowed, but because Jacob Greaves diverted the attempt in, it was allowed to stand.

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa was fined £25,000 last month over his post-match comments following their draw with United. Arbeloa felt Maguire had committed a foul shortly before United's late equaliser and that the officials had favoured the away side.

"All fouls for them," he said. "You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, it's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here."

And then, in a similar incident to United's third goal against Sporting, Dorgu's dramatic equaliser in United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa earlier this month was allowed to stand despite Man Utd goalkeeper Senne Lammens appearing to impede Villa keeper Zion Suzuki, who flapped at the corner and missed the ball.

Sports.title: Yoro red card: Written reasons for overturned decision revealed
Sports.content:
The Football Association has released the written reasons why Leny Yoro's red card for Manchester United at Liverpool was overturned - even though refereeing body Pro Ref said the on-field decision was correct.

Yoro was sent off for bringing down Liverpool striker Alexander Isak as the last defender outside the penalty area, with referee Sam Barrott sending him off for a denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO), with VAR John Brooks agreeing with the call.

United went on to concede four goals in the heavy defeat to Liverpool - and despite Pro Ref chief Howard Webb indicating that no clear mistake was made, the FA still decided to overturn the red card for an "obvious error" by the officials, as Isak was not in possession of the ball when he was fouled.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News’ Kaveh Solhekol explains Manchester United's successful appeal process for Yoro's red card

In the written reasons, the three-person panel - consisting of three former professional footballers, including one goalkeeper - said Isak had taken a heavy touch "to the extent he had in fact lost control of the ball" - which under the rules, says Yoro should not have been sent off.

Who was in the three-person FA panel? Stuart Ripley - Chairman FA's Judicial Panel, former Premier League winger and winner with Blackburn

Mick Kearns - former First Division goalkeeper

Tony Agana - former First Division striker with Notts County and Leeds

They were advised on the Laws of the Game by former referee Eddie Wolstenholme.

"The Commission members were unanimous that, taking the foul committed by Yoro out of the scenario, Isak would not have had an obvious goal-scoring opportunity," the statement read.

"Despite the fact that Isak had reached the ball initially, his touch was heavy to the extent that he had in fact lost control of the ball - that control had, in effect, passed to the advancing MUFC goalkeeper who in the view of the Commission would have been able to gather or smother the ball before AI [Alexander Isak] could get to it and shoot at goal.

"To the mind of the Commission, the referee had made an 'obvious error' in deciding that AI would have had an obvious goal-scoring opportunity."

The written reasons also said United provided extensive 'evidence' to say why Yoro should not have been sent off. As well as providing three separate angles of the incident, they also provided clips of Pascal Struijk's red card for Brighton against Sunderland - which was later overturned.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Yoro's overturned red card for Manchester United during their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino questioned VAR's involvement in the Frenchman's dismissal

United's analysis also claimed that Isak was, "at best 1.8m short of reaching the ball". The FA said there was no way of determining that analysis themselves, so it was "viewed with caution and allocated weight accordingly".

Why Webb felt the decision was correct

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'D Up, Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Webb backed the process of his officials although was non-committal when sharing his own verdict on the incident.

"By and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," said Webb.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

Audio from the officials revealed the VAR Brooks, who backed referee Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.

Why the Struijk footage helped Man Utd

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Premier League referee Mike Dean reacts as Brighton defender Pascal Struijk was controversially sent off against Sunderland

This is not the first time this season that a DOGSO red card has created division within the football authorities.

In October, two independent panels disagreed over whether Brighton's Struijk deserved to be sent off at Sunderland, an event which United used in their evidence to get Yoro's red card overturned.

Struijk was dismissed for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity in the second half when he was adjudged to have fouled Sunderland striker Wilson Isidor as he tried to latch on to a pass that ran through to goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Neither referee Thomas Bramall nor his assistant gave a foul, but VAR Neil Davies intervened and recommended an on-field review. Bramall watched several replays before changing his decision and dismissing Struijk.

However, Brighton appealed and an independent regulatory commission, which is convened through the FA to consider disciplinary matters, overturned the red card and subsequent one-match ban.

But disagreements over the decision continued after the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel - another independent panel who determine the validity of refereeing decisions - voted 3-2 that the VAR intervention was correct.

The KMI panel ruled that Struijk committed a "cynical foul clearly impacting the attacker's ability to gain possession of the ball which should have been penalised by the referee".

Sports.title: Delap's chance at redemption against toothless Chelsea
Sports.content:
When Liam Delap joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he probably had ambitions of cementing himself as an elite Premier League No 9. Perhaps even positioning himself to be the heir to Harry Kane's throne for England.

Less than a month later, Joao Pedro made the move to Stamford Bridge and suddenly, the landscape changed. He was not the first-choice striker at the club.

What followed was an arduous campaign that brought three goals in 47 games and saw Delap succumb to what is now the fabled curse of the Chelsea No 9 shirt.

A club-record move to Nottingham Forest in August has yet to truly revitalise his career either. But Oliver Glasner does have faith that there's a 20-goal-a-season striker hiding in the 23-year-old. What better time to showcase it than against his former employer?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Clinton Morrison said earlier this season that Nottingham Forest suits Liam Delap's play

This isn't just an opportunity for Delap to prove a point, mind. If anything, this game comes at the most opportune time to show Xabi Alonso exactly what he is missing at this very moment.

Since Joao Pedro has been on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Chelsea's devastating attack has often looked tame. Without the Brazilian as a focal point, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer have struggled to hit the same heights. As Paul Merson playfully put it: "if you had The Three Musketeers but took one of them out, you'd struggle to sell a film."

Joao Pedro has not played since the 2-0 win on October 17 against Everton. In the four Premier League matches since, Chelsea have lost three and won once against 10-man Manchester United. In those games, they scored three goals. They managed more than that in wins over Bournemouth and Brighton prior alone.

Nottingham Forest

Chelsea Friday 27th November 7:15pm Kick off 8:00pm

Alonso has tried all sorts to combat the loss. They played without a recognised striker against Tottenham and got ripped apart. The same approach was used in the defeat to Sunderland. Against United, Willian Estevao tended to operate centrally while Emmanuel Emegha was finally given the chance against Leeds. He scored but also had the fewest touches of any starter that day, being the only one to remain in single digits.

Danny Welbeck would appear to be the most obvious option, but Alonso appears reluctant to use his very own Benjamin Button from the off. That makes Emegha the only natural choice.

It's difficult to compare Delap and Emegha from last term for different reasons. The former was often watching from the bench while the latter was out from December to April with injury at Strasbourg. The season before, though, indicates that perhaps Delap could offer a little more with his all-round game.

What makes Joao Pedro so unique to Chelsea is not purely his scoring numbers. It is the fact that he is a consistent top-10 performer among all Premier League strikers with his link-up play.

While Emegha's data shows him to be more prolific in front of goal, the Englishman is far closer to Joao Pedro in build-up play than his Dutch counterpart. There is still a gulf in quality as you'd expect, but it certainly shows that the former Ipswich man was probably more suited to filling in when the Brazilian is unavailable.

That was the case two seasons ago and is even more so since he has joined Forest. The indication being that even in a period that hasn't been so fruitful, he has still been able to develop.

Delap has shown he can thrive when he has a chip on his shoulder. His brace against Manchester City was as great an example as you could find to show that. Against another former club, with his team struggling to get results and fans fans beginning to grow frustrated.

That was the night he announced himself to the City Ground faithful. On Friday, it will be an opportunity to announce himself to the travelling supporters, something he'd have wished to have done by this time last year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Nottingham Forest and Manchester City

He may even be further buoyed by the fact that his former side are struggling just as much at the back as they are in attack. Chelsea have the fifth-worst defensive record in the Premier League from the first 11 games.

That is a mouth-watering fact for any striker, let alone one who has no excuse but to have the bit between his teeth. It feels as though the cards have fallen as perfectly as they possibly could for Delap to have his say.

No one will ever know if there's a scenario where Delap staying could have been beneficial for his career. But Friday Night Football is his platform show it would have been beneficial for the Blues.

Watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Premier League and Main Event on Friday Night Football; kick-off 8pm.

Sports.title: Collins: I got choked up before I came on for my Wales debut!
Sports.content:
On Friday November 6, Aaron Collins was notified by the FAW that he was on the standby list for Wales' Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal.

He knew it was a step in the right direction, but his form - 17 goals and three assists in 16 games in all competitions at the time - seemed more than worthy of an official call-up.

A first chance for the MK Dons striker to represent his country since an U19 friendly defeat to Germany in April 2015 was tantalisingly close, yet just out of reach.

Until November 10, that was.

Wrexham's Kieffer Moore withdrew from Craig Bellamy's squad and Collins was called up to take his place.

"That was a call I've been waiting for for a long time," Collins tells Sky Sports.

"I don't score goals to be like: 'I'm going to get called up now', because I know the level I'm at, and I've got to prove a lot to get that chance.

"But after being a pro for 12 years, I did think the older I was getting, the less chance I was going to get. Of course that crossed my mind.

Image: The 29-year-old came on after 63 minutes at the Cardiff City Stadium

"It was a shock to finally receive the call and know I was going to represent my country at international level."

In Oslo, Collins was an unused substitute as Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Erling Haaland, Martin Odegaard and co.

Hearing 'Land of My Fathers' for the first time stirred something inside.

"It really choked me up. I grew up watching the rugby team and the football team singing it and you get goosebumps then. But to be able to stand there and sing that national anthem as a proud Welshman, as one of the players, was something that I would have never even thought I'd be able to do."

Back in Cardiff against Portugal, Bellamy told him at half-time to make sure he was ready to go if called upon.

After 63 minutes, he came on alongside Brennan Johnson to make his senior debut.

"I got choked up again then!" Collins says.

"To actually be able to achieve that and have the honour of having a Welsh badge on my chest entering the pitch was just crazy.

"I enjoyed it and I just played with no fear, like I had nothing to lose. I did what the manager wanted from me; I didn't manage to get any real chances, but you're at the elite level and it's not going to be as easy."

Having not played against Norway, he did not go searching for a shirt swap "out of respect for the lads who played".

But against Portugal "I was walking down the tunnel I saw Diogo Dalot and I got myself a shirt to treasure along with my debut shirt".

Those two shirts are not the only new additions to the room where Collins puts his accolades on display.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet League One match between MK Dons and Doncaster

In the last league game he played before his Wales adventure, on October 31, he scored four in MK Dons' 6-1 demolition of Doncaster.

That mammoth effort earned him another match ball for the collection - the second of the season and fourth of his career - as well as the Compare the Market Goal Hero of the Month award.

Image: Collins won the Compare the Market Goal Hero of the Month award for October

"I'd never scored four in a game before - that's a new achievement ticked off!"

"The only thing I can put my form down to is confidence. Any attacker knows that when you're in your flow, you're in your flow, and when you're scoring and assisting, there's that feeling where you feel like you're not going to miss.

"I'm in hot form and I do expect everything that I hit to go in. It's a feeling I need to cherish and try and make last as long as possible."

Collins' hot streak comes after a turbulent 2025/26 season, during which he helped Paul Warne's side to promotion from Sky Bet League Two, but suffered three significant injuries that greatly reduced his playing time after a reported £800,000 move from Bolton.

That misfortune is fuelling him.

"Coming into this season, I had this different kind of hunger to make up for last season where I came in as, maybe you could say the marquee signing, and didn't really get to live up to that," he adds.

"Being fit and ready to kick on - and to start of the season the way I have - has been a real achievement. Now I can show why I've been signed, and hopefully fans can go, 'Aaron Collins was a good signing!'

"To get to 17 in 17 games is a huge achievement so far, and there's plenty more games to come. My goal is to get to that 20 mark as early as possible, and even get to that 20 mark in the league as early as possible, and carry on kicking on."

If Collins carries on in this fashion, he might be a shoo-in for another Wales call-up in March.

Created by Compare the Market, ​in partnership with​​ the EFL, the Goal Hero of the Month award celebrates the most memorable and impactful goals from across the Championship, League One and League Two.

It aims to shine a spotlight on the stories behind them and what they mean to the clubs, players and supporters involved.

Sports.title: FIFA hit by cyberattack with 'personal and business information' stolen - including immigration documents and financial records - after hackers 'impersonated staff'
Sports.content:
FIFA hit by cyberattack with 'personal and business information' stolen - including immigration documents and financial records - after hackers 'impersonated staff'

Personal information, immigration documents and financial records have been stolen from FIFA in a cyberattack.

Football's governing body confirmed that a hacking group 'impersonated staff' to gain access to their system before taking the sensitive files.

In total, more than 12 gigabytes of data has been stolen and a group called Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) shared a screenshot of FIFA documents on X last week, claiming credit for the theft and finding access through FIFA’s Microsoft app portal.

They are understood to have then published the stolen files on a forum on the dark web, writing 'more leaks soon'.

A FIFA spokesperson said: 'FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyber-attack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.

'FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.

FIFA were hacked and had sensitive documents stolen - pictured, FIFA president Gianni Infantino

Handsome Boy Hacking Club took credit for the hack and shared this screenshot on X

'FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data.

'Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.'

According to the Athletic, immigration, financial and personal documents were stolen by the hackers impersonating staff but did not include the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a plan to effectively sell off the World Cup that collapsed and piled pressure on president Gianni Infantino.

The FFE plan first became public knowledge in July. Infantino sought to create a company to manage the commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions, including the World Cup, but wanted a minority stake to be made available to private investors.

The lead investor was set to be Thrive, a company founded by President Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, Josh Kushner, but the plan was abandoned on August 1 after three continental confederations rejected it.

It remains to be seen whether files relating to Infantino himself were taken by the hackers.

The 56-year-old is currently running for reelection against Kohzo Tashima of Japan and France football federation president Philippe Diallo.

He remains the strong favorite to win FIFA's election is held on March 18 and has already served three terms.

FIFA are the latest football-related body to have fallen victim to cyber crime, with LaLiga targeted earlier this month.

Spanish police are still investigating but LaLiga confirmed their security teams identified the source and stopped the hacker from stealing more data.

Sports.title: Female reporter protected by Jude Bellingham reveals how classy England star stood up for her in 'intimidating' Madrid press scrum - leading to viral moment
Sports.content:
The female reporter Jude Bellingham defended during an 'intimidating' post-match interview has praised the England star for being 'respectful' and 'well-mannered' as she opened up on the viral incident. BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway was speaking to Bellingham after Real Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday when another journalist interrupted her as she posed a follow-up question, threatening to cut her interview short. But the midfielder, 23, refused to answer the interferer and instead told him: 'Sorry, she's got one more [question].' Bellingham, who scored a sensational long-range goal on the hour mark to put Real Madrid ahead in the Champions League clash, was widely praised after footage of the incident went viral on social media, with fans applauding him as a 'class act' and 'role model for young men'. Now Conway has added to the praise, stating the experience 'added a whole new layer to the love people have for Jude'. Conway had been waiting to speak to the England star in the 'mixed zone' after the match – an area where journalists line up behind a barrier to interview players. Jude Bellingham has won praise for his 'respectful' and 'classy' treatment of a female reporter BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_ 'It is utter carnage,' she told BBC Radio WM, opening up on the incident at the Bernabeu. 'Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust. 'Jude very rarely gives interviews, especially in the mixed zone. It is chaos... It's kind of every person out for themselves. 'You've got elbows, you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you. 'I'm one of very, very few female reporters and one of very, very few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so important.' Conway admitted the mixed zone can be an 'intimidating' environment and being interrupted is unfortunately a routine part of being a post-match interviewer. Admitting it was 'so nice' that Bellingham stepped in to stand up for her, she added: 'It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.' Conway, originally from Solihull, specialises in Spanish football and is based in Madrid, according to her Instagram, where she has more than 12,000 followers. She had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort at the Bernabeu. 'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham said. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through. 'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it. It was a nice goal and important for the team being the second goal and gave us control.' The England superstar (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on Tuesday night

Your browser does not support iframes.

After being interrupted and encouraged by Bellingham to pose her second question, Conway asked whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country. 'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter,' Bellingham added. 'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.' Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment. Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.' The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe. Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances. Bellingham has previously earned plaudits for his treatment of the media, having stopped to speak to a disabled reporter during the World Cup when several of his England team-mates had walked past, taking the time to answer his questions in Spanish.

Sports.title: How Man United's data gurus got Leny Yoro off the hook: Stats analysis from ex-Formula One boffin proved Alexander Isak had NO chance of reaching the ball before red card - in appeal win that has left refs fuming
Sports.content:
Manchester United turned to its data gurus in a bid to categorically prove Alexander Isak had no chance of reaching the ball as part of its evidence to overturn Leny Yoro’s red card. Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United’s trip to Anfield for a last-man foul on Isak, which referee Sam Barrott determined fit the criteria for Denial Of A Goalscoring Opportunity (DOGSO). The young United centre-back was shown a straight red card after VAR doubled down on the day, insisting that no ‘clear and obvious error’ had been made. United successfully appealed the decision through an independent panel and the lengths they went to for their evidence submission has now come to light. Bosses at United included three high-definition video clips of the incident in question, which used multiple different angles as well as speeds in slow-motion and in real time for the panel to consider. United also submitted video evidence of a DOGSO sending off earlier this season for Brighton’s Pascal Struijk against Sunderland, which was also overturned on appeal. Leny Yoro was sent off for Man United against Liverpool but the red card was later rescinded United showed that Isak would not have reached the ball if he'd have stayed on his feet The most fascinating element of United’s detailed evidence pack came via its data department, led by ex-Formula One guru Michael Sansoni. United outlined in a letter to the appeal panel that a technical analysis of the incident saw boffins at Carrington calculate the probability of Isak reaching the ball following his heavy touch prior to contact from Yoro. The data allowed for the possibility that Isak maintained his speed and direction from the moment his legs first made contact with Yoro to assess whether he would have got to the ball before United goalkeeper Senne Lammens. United’s analysis concluded that Isak would have been 1.8 metres shy of reaching the ball even if all optimal speed and directional factors had been achieved. The appeals commission, however, told United that that data, however detailed, was not verifiable and so had to be treated with ‘caution’. Considering all the elements of United’s submission, the panel unanimously agreed that it was not a red card offence and did not meet the threshold for DOGSO, immediately overturning the decision and withdrawing all punishment against Yoro. ‘We can accept referee can make a mistake. But we have VAR. What were they doing?’ a fuming Mauricio Pochettino said on Tuesday of the original Yoro decision. ‘We are going to repeat the game? Play similar tools the game XI v XI? We have an unbelievable car but we have to be at the level to drive. We accept the technology.’
