Sports.title: Melbourne boxer's career in turmoil after Australian Idol star exposes his vile private messages - as Anthony Mundine vows to 'teach him a lesson'
Sports.content:
Melbourne boxer Tommy Pedis has been dumped from Victoria's boxing team days before the national championships after sending vile messages to Australian Idol contestant Majeda Beatty.

Beatty went public on Monday with screenshots and a video she said the Craigieburn boxer had sent her directly.

In the video, Pedis used a racist slur, called Indigenous Australians 'petrol sniffers' and told them to 'leave our country'.

Beatty, who competed on Australian Idol in 2025, said the experience had been 'incredibly upsetting, confronting and honestly exhausting'.

'I've been riddled with anxiety today. It's one thing to experience racism, but it's another to have someone deliberately direct it towards you, continue to antagonise you and make you feel as though you're powerless to do anything about it,' she said.

'I never intended to spend my day having to defend my existence, my identity or my people. I'm proud to be Aboriginal, proud of my heritage and proud of the communities I come from. I will not be intimidated into silence or made to feel ashamed of who I am.

'Racism isn't banter, it isn't a joke and it certainly isn't something we should have to tolerate. Boxing is a sport that brings people together from all walks of life, and there should be absolutely no room for racism within it.'

Pedis claimed his remarks had been 'meant to be a joke' and acknowledged that his language was racist, saying he took full responsibility.

Melbourne boxer Tommy Pedis as been booted off the state team just days before the national championships after racist remarks he directed at a former Australian Idol contestant emerged online

He later issued an apology for the vile messages after Majeda outed him online

Majeda publicly exposed him on social media for making the vile comments

'I understand that people are disappointed and angry at me. I don't blame them,' he said.

'I can see my action, what I've done was wrong, it has hurt certain people, and in future I would not do that again.

'My comments were completely unacceptable, and I take full responsibility for what I said.

'There is no excuse for my behaviour, and I deeply regret the hurt and offence I have caused.'

On Tuesday, the VABL and ANABA suspended Pedis from all their events with immediate effect and until further notice, and dropped him from Team Victoria for the national championships.

Former world boxing champion Anthony Mundine challenged Pedis to get in the ring with him.

'This is the s*** I fought against my whole life,' Mundine said.

'Get in touch with me brah, and I'm going to teach you a lesson.

'I don't want to be a bully, but you need to be put in line.'

Sports.title: Huge crowd gathers for funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves after he passed away following knockout in the ring and three-month coma
Sports.content:
Huge crowds have gathered today for the funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves who died this week.

The 31-year-old died in hospital on Monday after being placed in a medically induced coma following a fight in August.

After being knocked down twice in the 10th round, the Irish southpaw was carried from the ring on a stretcher following his defeat to fellow countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital.

His promoters, Queensberry, later revealed he was in a 'critical but stable' condition before undergoing surgery.

Reeves was then placed in an induced coma, where he remained until his death three months later, surrounded by his family.

Along with being a professional boxer, Reeves was a serving member of the 12th Infantry Battalion out of Sarsfield Barracks, an ambassador for Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention and a model.

A large crowd gathered at the Church of Our Lady, Queen of Peace for the funeral mass in Roxboro, Limerick, on Friday, with thousands also tuning in to a livestream of the service.

Dreams by The Cranberries played in the church as the coffin carrying Reeves' body, draped in the Irish tricolour, was carried inside.

Irish boxer Lee Reeves died on Monday after spending three months in a medically-induced coma

Family members accompanied the hearse carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours on Friday

Members of the Irish Defence Forces carry the coffin of boxer Reeves out of Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

It had been brought to the church on an adapted gun carriage, as part of the military honours for the service.

His Defence Forces cap was also placed on the coffin.

Reeves' boxing gloves and belt, his Bible, and a pizza box were among items placed at the altar to represent his interests including his love of his religion – along with photographs of the Limerick-born boxer.

The mass heard tributes from some of his four sisters: Louise, Shannon, Jodie and Jessie, who described him as 'one of the greatest men on this earth' and 'an inspiration to everyone he met'.

Jodie told the funeral mass that Reeves was a family man who 'did everything' for his sisters.

'He was my mother's whole life, and she was his. He dedicated every fight to her, and no doubt made her proud.

'She was his number one supporter from day one.

'You were a father to us all, and that even includes Dad.'

She added: 'Nothing is going to be the same without you around, but I promise you'll never be forgotten.'

Jodie, also reading a tribute from Reeves' father, said: 'You had a heart and a presence that touched so many lives.'

Continuing that tribute, she added: 'God knows how much we will miss you, and how much of a piece of our hearts will go with you. Rest easy, son.'

Reeves had been carried out of the ring on a stretcher after his defeat to his countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital (Source: Instagram/Lee Reeves)

A car is pictured following the funeral cortege of Reeves as it leaves Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, after his funeral mass on Friday

Wreaths and tributes are seen on display before the funeral of boxer Lee Reeves at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick,on Friday

Shannon said: 'I will miss you every day that I'm on this earth.'

She added: 'You never deserved this, brother, but it's not the end.

'Your story will live on, and your legacy will live on.'

Outside, a large screen and several framed photographs depicted images of Reeves and his loved ones as well as his boxing gloves.

The images carried captions such as 'brother', 'son', 'nephew', 'uncle' and 'pride of Limerick'.

Attendees included Mayor of Limerick John Horan as well as Defence Forces colleagues including the General Officer Commanding 1 Brigade, Brigadier General Caimin Keogh and Officer Commanding 12th Infantry Battalion, Lieutenant Colonel Ian Harrington.

Reeves was placed in a medically-induced coma and had emergency surgery after a junior welterweight fight in Dublin on August 1.

He had won 16 of his 18 bouts after turning professional in 2018, with several of his fights in Canada and Colombia.

The hearse is pictured carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours, on Friday

Family members stand behind as soldiers from the Irish Defence Forces place the coffin of boxer and serving soldier Reeves on an adapted gun carriage at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

Reeves' August clash with final opponent Gary Cully saw the 31-year-old knocked down twice in the 10th round

He was also a contestant on BBC reality show, Survivor, in 2023.

Defence Forces head chaplain Fr Paschal Hanrahan said Reeves showed physical courage in the boxing ring but also moral, courage and integrity in his mental health advocacy.

'We hold in our prayers today his colleagues serving overseas at this time with the 128th Infantry Battalion in Unifil, along with their chaplain Fr Piotr, who I know are gathered at this very moment in prayer for Lee.

'With all the agility and dexterity of a professional boxer, Lee moves seamlessly from being a model to being a role model in the Defence Forces.

'And those who served with him in Sarsfield Barracks saw our Defence Forces values in the way that he lived.'

He added: 'They saw his respect in the way he treated people, his loyalty in the way he stood by his comrades, and his selflessness in the time he gave to those who needed encouragement.'

Reeves, who was nicknamed 'El Champo', had won 16 of his 18 professional bouts since turning professional in 2018, and had been challenging Cully for the vacant BUI Celtic light-welterweight title.

He had been knocked down twice in the 10th round against Cully before being taken out of the ring, and in his tribute message for his opponent, Cully admitted that he was still in shock at how their match had ended.

Members of the Irish Defence Forces walked in procession alongside the coffin of boxer and soldier Reeves on an adapted gun carriage at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

'I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals, the weight above me, and (I would) always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear,' Cully wrote.

'What a character and a gent. It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'

Sports.title: 'It's amazing that Scotland now has TWO world champions'... Meet the Kilmarnock kid who idolises Prince Naseem Hamed and is part of the Scottish boxing boom with Willy Hutchinson
Sports.content:
'It's amazing that Scotland now has TWO world champions'... Meet the Kilmarnock kid who idolises Prince Naseem Hamed and is part of the Scottish boxing boom with Willy Hutchinson

Only last month, the mutterings were about where Scottish boxing goes from here, three years after Tartan Tornado Josh Taylor was toppled and with doubts mounting about the health of the sport’s grass roots.

Three weeks on, seemingly from nowhere, the nation has not one but two new world champions.

Willy Hutchinson claimed the WBC light heavyweight belt in a tussle with Joshua Buatsi earlier this month in the full glare of the television cameras. But slipping beneath the radar were the achievements of Aaron Sarwar, who was anointed the under-19 world flyweight champion in Montenegro on October 27.

Both men sobbed in the ring and fell to their knees as the simple raising of a referee’s hand detonated identical emotional explosions in them – sudden vindication of years of grinding roadwork, gruelling gymwork and grafting ringwork.

With beautiful symmetry, the only other Scot to have won a world amateur title was Hutchinson himself, in Russia in 2016. Now his ascent to the top of the pro game has lit the path for Sarwar to follow. And if there are still mutterings, they are that this kid from Kilmarnock could be the real deal.

Compared with big-ticket bouts, youth boxing’s short contests can appear cagey and sterile – but it’s hard to peel your eyes off Sarwar’s compelling repertoire of shots, defence, switches and occasional showboating.

Kilmarnock fighter Aaron Sarwar with his trophy for winning the Under-19 world championship

Those who know him best say his most remarkable asset is an iron psyche that, even at such a tender age, has created a machine-like drive to reach whatever peak is placed in front of him.

Having become a world junior karate champion and double black belt by the age of 11, the ring became his home during the Covid-19 pandemic as he looked for a fresh challenge.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport, Sarwar insists he has already set off on a mission for another Montenegro moment.

He said: ‘People ask me about that feeling. It’s indescribable. I wish I could go back and relive that ten, 15 seconds of getting my hand raised because I don’t think anything will come close to it again.

‘But I’ll be chasing it. I want to make my mum and dad proud again. I watch [the video of] it every day. I get goosebumps every time.

‘I’d spoken to Willy before, but we met at a boxing show this week and had a good chat about what’s next for us.

Sarwar admits he still struggles to describe the euphoria he felt on being crowned the winner

‘It’s amazing that in the space of two weeks, Scotland’s got two new world champions. It’s crazy.’

Sarwar turned to boxing when lockdown meant karate was reduced to online seminars. He stumbled across a basic gym with punchbags behind the shop from where he’d buy lunch on school breaks – and from there he joined the local club.

The 18-year-old was back to his roots this week at the Northwest ABC in Onthank, the estate made infamous by the BBC Scotland fly-on-the-wall documentary The Scheme.

Hitting our screens in 2010, the series won a Bafta award but also stood accused of creating a ‘poverty safari’ for the chattering classes and creating dubious celebrities out of light-fingered drug addict Marvin Baird and his dog Bullet.

Northwest ABC was feted and funded for being a beacon among the anti-social behaviour, even receiving a personal visit from Justice Secretary Kenny MacAskill. Now Graeme Marshall’s committed coaching team has helped create a new poster boy for The Scheme.

Down at the club, they are proud of their prodigy, but the mood is more about hope than hype. They remorselessly tease Sarwar about his fussy fringe and point out, to rein in expectations, that he’s still so young he’s yet to even fight without a headguard.

Sarwar bumped into his fellow world title holder Willy Hutchinson during a boxing show

But Marshall – who Sarwar refers to as akin to a second father – is in no doubt about their boy’s freakish potential.

He said: ‘When he asked to come to the club after lockdown, it was Aaron himself who called up, which was unusual for a 12-year-old.

‘We knew straight away there was a talent there — he’s fast and strong and dedicated. After a few months, we entered him for the Scottish championships. It was his first fight, but he went and won the tournament.

‘Second season, he won the GB championships. I took him all over to fight. In Sweden, he stopped the Swedish champion, and when you see him beating Irish boys in Ireland, you know you’re dealing with something special.

‘He’ll turn professional at some point; it’s every young boy’s dream. And there’s no reason why he can’t go on and match what Willy Hutchinson’s done and become a world champion.’

The calls have started coming from managers testing the water about going pro – as Hutchinson did immediately after winning amateur gold – and McBookie are already offering odds of 8/1 that he goes right to the top.

Hutchinson brought Scottish boxing out of the doldrums with his defeat of Joshua Buatsi

But, for now at least, Sarwar – who ditched his engineering college course to concentrate on the sport – remains focused on fighting for Scotland at the 2030 Commonwealth Games in India.

He said: ‘I’ve got all the time in the world. I’ve opened myself a lot of doors now. I’ll speak to my coaches and mum and dad about what they think is best for me. But I know what I can achieve off the back of this now.

‘For karate, I was dedicated and hard-working but I didn’t have that same passion. Boxing, it’s all I do. I’ve left all my education to box full time. It’s all my eggs in one basket so there’s no choice, I have to do it. It’s boxing or nothing.’

Sarwar names his inspiration as Prince Naseem Hamed, the flamboyant featherweight world champion from the 1990s, for ‘his style, his flashiness, his power’. He added: ‘I’ve got that flashy side too, but if they get serious, I’ll stand toe to toe. I can box, I can fight, I can do it all.’

Despite training solely with Boxing Scotland now, Sarwar can’t keep away from his home club. He added: ‘I try to carry myself well all the time and inspire the young ones to come to the gym and train that bit harder, and it’s good to be around the coaches all the time.

Sarwar is in no rush to turn professional and is eyeing the 2030 Commonwealth Games in India

‘The support they’ve given me over the years has been second to none, I can’t thank them enough. There’ll be no way I can ever repay them the sacrifices they’ve made [for me].’

Meanwhile, in the ring at the Northwest, a small boy’s fists are a deadly blur, thwacking the pads held out by his coach with awesome efficiency. To misquote Muhammad Ali, he has the legs of a sparrow but the sting of a bee.

Aidan Sarwar – 12 years old – is already part of the Scotland set-up.

It was a Glasgow music hall crowd that first memorably coined the heckle, ‘Oh no, there’s two of them’ when English comedian Bernie Winters joined his brother Mike on stage. Boxers across the land may soon empathise.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua becomes a father for the second time: Boxing star welcomes baby girl in secret with mother of his son - but won't meet her until after his fight with Tyson Fury on December 11
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua becomes a father for the second time: Boxing star welcomes baby girl in secret with mother of his son - but won't meet her until after his fight with Tyson Fury on December 11

Anthony Joshua has revealed he is a father again, welcoming a new baby girl into the world with Nicole Osbourne.

Former heavyweight world champion Joshua, who is gearing up to fight long-term rival Tyson Fury at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, already has a son with Osbourne called JJ, aged 11.

Now JJ is a big brother, with Joshua deliberately not finding out the sex of his newborn during pregnancy. His daughter is yet to be named but was born on November 14, weighing 5.5lb.

Joshua is yet to meet his daughter as he is in Marbella preparing for his long-awaited showdown with Fury in the early hours of December 12, but will meet and hold his newborn after the fight. In the meantime, there have been FaceTime calls with Osbourne to see their daughter.

'It's been amazing, a big blessing, and I can't believe I'm a girl dad. I didn't want to find the sex out during the pregnancy,' the 37-year-old told The Sun.

'I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, "No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!".

Anthony Joshua has announced that he is a father again, welcoming a baby girl into the world

The ex-heavyweight world champion already has a son called JJ who is now 11 (duo in 2021)

'I'm going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll's playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know? I will change nappies, I've gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!

'Now I've got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive.

'My daughter will give me a first-hand experience of the power of a woman - I've spoken to all the women in my family, and it's amazing the amount of support that women give each other.'

Joshua, who almost lost his life in a devastating car crash in Nigeria that killed two of his best friends last year, said the ordeal has taught him not to take life for granted.

'This past year has been incredibly tough, I realised how precious life is, and how short it can be. I’m just going to live my life by duty, and even having a baby girl was part of my duty. I wanted to bring life in, it was a conscious decision, 100 per cent. If something happened to me, I didn’t want JJ to be out here alone,' he added.

The wholesome news comes less than a year after Joshua was devastated by the loss of his best friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele last December, after the trio were involved in a car crash near Lagos.

Joshua has been deeply affected by the death of his friends and surviving the fatal crash himself, with the accident coming just ten days after he took down YouTuber-turned-boxing star Jake Paul.

Upon his return to the ring in late July with his fight against Kristian Prenga, Joshua broke down during his post-fight interview as he credited Ayodele and Ghami for getting him through a tough first round.

The 37-year-old is preparing to fight long-term British rival Tyson Fury in Cardiff next month

'I don't want to talk about it anymore,' Joshua had said quietly as he let out his emotions.

Earlier in the evening he had stepped into the ring wearing his friends' names on pennants pinned to his chest and had admitted before the fight that he had spent months suppressing the pain of their loss.

Joshua was being driven along one of Nigeria's deadliest roads in December when his SUV crashed into a stationary truck on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

He is thought to have narrowly escaped major injury or worse after having switched to sit behind the driver in the back seat on the left-hand side of the car.

Joshua was admitted to hospital with 'minor injuries' after being pulled from the wreckage of the crash.

In February, Joshua added the names of 'LATZ' and 'SINA' to the tattoo outline of Africa he sports on his bicep.

Sports.title: Tragic boxer's heartbroken final opponent pays tribute to 31-year-old rival in emotional Instagram statement after Irish fighter lost his life following three-month coma
Sports.content:
Tragic boxer's heartbroken final opponent pays tribute to 31-year-old rival in emotional Instagram statement after Irish fighter lost his life following three-month coma

The final opponent of boxer Lee Reeves has paid an emotional tribute following the death of the man he shared a ring with in August.

Gary Cully, 30, knocked Reeves down in the bout and his fellow Irishman was in a coma for three months before tragically losing his life on Monday.

The 31-year-old Reeves, who was nicknamed 'El Champo', had been challenging Cully for the vacant BUI Celtic light-welterweight title and was sent to the canvas twice in the tenth round before being taken out of the ring on a stretcher and rushed to hospital.

Cully shared his shock and grief at Reeves's death on Instagram, writing: 'We shared the ring back in August but we been going back for years.

'I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals the weight above me and always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear myself and Luke Thomas used to plague him to spit us out an MC when we were staying in Dublin on training camp and they’d always be fire.

'What a character and a gent. It’s never been nothing love between us champ can’t really believe I’m writing this but RIP brother.'

Lee Reeves died on Monday having been in a coma for three months after fighting Gary Cully

The 31-year-old (right) was knocked down twice in the 10th round and Cully (left) shared an emotional tribute

Cully shared a number of pictures from their fight and also screenshots of messages between them from the last few years.

In one, Reeves wrote: 'Take a bow son! Fantastic win well done champ!' Cully replied: 'Thank you bro, congrats on your two also.'

Limerick-born Reeves spent time away from the ring as a competitor on BBC reality show Survivor in 2023, and served as an ambassador for Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention group.

The fighter, the oldest of four siblings, lost his mother Cathy to suicide in 2015.

Reeves had initially been declared as in a critical but stable condition in hospital when he was placed into a medically-induced coma.

But the grim news was announced on Monday by his friend and coach Jonathan O'Brien, who paid tribute to Reeves in a poignant statement on social media.

'Goodbye son, sleep tight, you fought so hard till the end,' O'Brien wrote. 'We love you so much, rest in peace with your mam and brother waiting at the heavenly gates.

'Look over your sisters and your father, give them the strength to get through this. We love you Lee.'

'Limerick is a very dark place tonight with the loss of Lee Reeves. Lee was not just a boxer that excelled in his career - he was a mental health advocate who highlighted mental health and how it can affect young people,' Limerick City councillor and Reeves' family friend Catherine Slattery said in her tribute.

Cully shared screenshots of messages between him and Reeves over the years

Reeves (second from right) was described as a 'character and a gent' by his last opponent Cully (centre)

'Lee was a very proud Limerick man, he loved Limerick and its people and any chance he got to promote Limerick, he took it.

'Lee loved his family. He was very proud of his dad, Tony, and he adored his sisters and his nieces and nephews and they, in return, adored him.

'Lee had great faith in God and the only (consolation) is that Lee's mam and brother are embracing him in their arms in heaven.

'The loss of Lee will be felt in Limerick for a long time to come and I am heartbroken for Lee that he lost his fight.

'Rest in peace El Champ - you will be missed by us all.'

Queensberry also shared a statement after news broke, writing: 'Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to learn of the passing of Lee Reeves.

'Lee was an immensely talented boxer, as well as a true role model and inspiration to his community.

'Our deepest condolences go to Lee's family, friends and all those who loved him. We ask that their privacy be respected at this incredibly difficult time. Rest in peace, Lee.'

Sports.title: Boxer Lee Reeves dies, aged 31, after three months in a coma - having been knocked out in the ring

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr in talks to fight Kell Brook in first bout since Conor Benn loss - with 'Special K' to come out of retirement
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr is in talks to fight Kell Brook in his return to the ring.

Brook, 40, has not fought since beating Amir Khan in 2022, but has emerged as a potential option to fight Eubank in his first fight since losing to Conor Benn late last year.

According to Elliott Amoakoh, the executive director of Eubank Jr's management team, Nova Sport LLC, any agreement is still a way away.

He told Sky Sports: 'Talks are ongoing but the date, purse and location are yet to be confirmed.'

Ben Shalom, however, who has represented both fighters in the past, told talkSPORT: 'It's a fight that we have been trying to make for a couple of months.

'They have pretty much agreed terms on both sides, there is just some final bits to go. It is one of the biggest fights in British boxing. I think you are right on February and in Manchester.'

Chris Eubank Jr (pictured) is in talks with Kell Brook to face off in his return to the ring

Brook (pictured) hasn't fought since 2022 and retired after beating long-term rival Amir Khan

Brook retired after beating long-time rival Khan in Manchester, having been linked with a fight with Eubank in the aftermath.

Brook has seemed almost certain to return to the ring, having revealed his return fight would be 'announced soon'.

He retired with 40 wins from 43 fights, and is a former International Boxing Federation welterweight champion.

Having debuted as a professional in 2004, he didn't lose until September 2016, when he was stopped in the fifth round by Gennady Golovkin.

Eubank Jr, meanwhile, had faced questions over retirement following his defeat by Benn but has refused to call it quits on his 15-year career.

He had claimed to have major fights scheduled for 2026, but has taken a whole year out of action.

Sports.title: F1 2027 grid: Who will be racing and where?
Sports.content:
The 2027 Formula 1 grid is now complete following the announcement from Haas that it has retained star youngster Oliver Bearman.

But the American squad is also the only team that is altering its driver pairing for next season, as many potentially enthralling storylines failed to materialise.

So, here’s a look at the situation.

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Hector Vivas / Formula 1 via Getty Images

The 2026 season has witnessed a significant shift in the dynamic down at Mercedes between Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, as the latter headed into the year as the heavy title favourite - only to fall flat early on.

It came after Russell finished 169 points ahead of Antonelli last season in what was a very up-and-down rookie campaign for the Italian, while the Briton arguably delivered his best yet. So, with Mercedes expected to master the regulation switch, which it did, Russell was the natural favourite yet Antonelli learned his lessons impressively fast to vastly improve upon 2025.

This eventually led to the 20-year-old becoming F1’s youngest ever world champion by securing his maiden title at the Mexico Grand Prix, with four rounds still to play at the time. Although this came as a surprise to many, Mercedes would have argued that his performances had been as forecast when it plucked him from karting and into its junior programme.

Read Also: Formula 1 How Antonelli rose so rapidly to become F1 world champion

As for Russell, his season has been a “complete disaster” - per Max Verstappen - and with two grands prix left in 2026, he sits fourth in the standings and could easily drop to fifth as he is level on points with 2025 world champion Lando Norris.

Nevertheless, he will remain with Mercedes for 2027 with his and Antonelli’s fate known for quite some time.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

Ferrari and Charles Leclerc agreed upon a new deal earlier in 2026 - announced in June - meaning the 29-year-old is continuing his length association with the Italian outfit. Leclerc joined its junior programme in 2016, made his F1 debut with customer squad Alfa Romeo Sauber in 2018 before moving to the works’ outfit in 2019.

The Monegasque has won nine grands prix in that time, which can be seen as a disappointment considering the promise displayed early on. But with Ferrari’s improved performance in 2026, jumping from fourth to second in the championship, Leclerc’s hope is that the team can press on and finally deliver a championship-winning car having signed a multi-year contract.

But he will have Lewis Hamilton to worry about in the neighbouring garage, as the seven-time world champion is understood to be under contract until the end of 2027 after joining in 2025. Last year was a disappointment for the Briton, finishing 86 points behind Leclerc, but he’s strengthened in 2026 with a 17-point advantage over his team-mate.

Tensions have also been high recently, with the two colliding on various occasions, most notably Monza, Mexico and Las Vegas, so that is a dynamic Ferrari must manage heading into 2027.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

It was known that at one stage Verstappen held some level of talks with McLaren when his Red Bull future was up in the air. Though this simply may have been a tactic to secure a more lucrative deal with the Austrian outfit, which is something he eventually earned, so McLaren is remaining with Norris and Oscar Piastri.

The Briton seems content with being a one-team man for the time being, staying with McLaren since his debut in 2019, and why not? Norris has secured that world title he so strived for and has been impressive in 2026 with three victories, even if the car hasn’t been quite there on several occasions.

As for Piastri, what happens with him is an on-and-off talking point given the Australian would have likely been the man to move had Verstappen joined. This year has been a disappointment for him, continuing on from his late title collapse in 2025, as he is seventh in the standings and 97 points behind Norris. His most recent victory was Zandvoort in August last year.

But he is on a “multi-year contract”, signed in 2025, and looks set to stay for now.

Red Bull: Max Verstappen, Isack Hadjar

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Manuel Eletto

The 2026 season has been quite similar to 2025 for Red Bull, having started quite slowly before a late rejuvenation with Verstappen enjoying four wins and nine podiums since this year’s summer break.

That has vaulted him into second in the drivers’ standings and should he carry such momentum into 2027, then a fifth world title could easily be on the way for the Dutchman. That would put him one short of Hamilton’s record for the most championships with one team - he achieved six at Mercedes - as Verstappen signed a bumper deal until at least 2030 this year.

It will see him start a second season alongside Isack Hadjar, who has had a solid first campaign at Red Bull and gave the team no reason to replace him. Perhaps the team now has its ideal number two driver to assist Verstappen in his title charge next year.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

The situation down at Red Bull’s sister outfit was one of the biggest sources of uncertainty, given it was only in November that Racing Bulls confirmed its pairing for 2027. It will be an unchanged duo, however, as Arvid Lindblad will return for his second season in F1 alongside Liam Lawson, whose seat was in doubt despite his best year yet.

Lawson is on course for a career-best ninth in the standings with 89 points, securing a top 10 finish at all but six grands prix, which in itself is enough for the Faenza outfit to secure its highest-ever constructors’ championship finish of fifth.

But Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov has impressed as an F2 rookie this year, sitting second to Rafael Camara, and historically Racing Bulls doesn’t keep drivers for long if a promotion to the main squad isn’t on the cards.

With 2027 going to be Lawson’s third proper season at Racing Bulls, historically the team may have dropped him in favour of its next protege. Tsolov, however, will have to settle for a reserve driver role in 2027 while Lindblad continues to perform, taking 38 points from his rookie year so far and 11th in the standings.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

Pierre Gasly signed a contract extension with Alpine last year, demonstrating his commitment to the cause despite the team being adrift at the back of the constructors' order across 2025. The arrival of Flavio Briatore, Steve Nielsen, and Mercedes has put the team back into the midfield battle, and the Frenchman is hoping that the Enstone squad can deliver a car worthy of his immense - and oft-underrated - talent.

Gasly is 10th in the 2026 standings with 52 points, helping Alpine sit sixth in the constructors’ championship and although he’s the French outfit’s clear number one driver, Franco Colapinto has still made a considerable step.

The Argentine has taken 35 points in 2026, compared to zero last year, and that earned him a new deal in August for 2027.

Haas: Oliver Bearman, Rafael Camara

Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team, Rafael Camara, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Bryn Lennon / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Haas is another squad to have endured serious question marks surrounding its driver pairing for next year. The first concerned Esteban Ocon, who just couldn’t make things click ever since he joined the American outfit from Alpine for 2025.

At the time he was seen as a real coup, the first grand prix winner to drive for Haas, but instead he was consistently outperformed by his much more inexperienced team-mate - Bearman - across both last year and 2026.

In the end things turned quite ugly and after it being confirmed that the 198-time grand prix starter wouldn’t continue into 2027, he was dismissed by Haas with five rounds still to play in the season.

His replacement is F2 championship leader Camara, who has signed a “multi-year” deal and given up his title ambitions in the feeder series to finish the season in F1 before his first, full campaign in 2027.

That will come alongside Bearman, who has mightily impressed in his time at Haas so far. Although the Briton was all but certain to continue with Haas into 2027, his announcement came rather late as Bearman's camp was looking for long-term assurances ahead of his third season at Haas on loan from Ferrari.

Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi F1 Team, Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Audi F1 boss Mattia Binotto confirmed in September that it will retain Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto for the 2027 season. At the time it didn’t really cause any particular conversations because the announcement came as little surprise, considering how well both drivers have done - thus giving Audi no reason to change its line-up.

The German marque, which made his F1 debut in 2026 after taking over from Sauber, has the perfect blend of youth and experience, plus a harmonious relationship between the pair.

Bortoleto is set for his third season in the championship, compared to Hulkenberg’s 16th, and both drivers have scored 14 points this year to give Audi eighth in the standings.

Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Peter Fox / Getty Images

Williams' decision to lock in Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz for at least another year demonstrates the buy-in for its long-term ambitions from both drivers, even if this season has presented a step back in fortunes. Some might uncharitably suggest that there was nowhere else for either driver to go, which is probably also true, but the retention of both drivers is a significant boost for the team.

Had Sainz decided to do something else, Williams is said to have hedged its bets and had spoken to the management of Sergio Perez and Colapinto for 2027, while Luke Browning has also impressed in his FP1 outings with the team.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

The situation at Aston Martin was another which promised potential drama for 2027 but failed to materialise as such. That is because for months the questions surrounding Fernando Alonso’s future were strife, considering he is 45 years old, driving for a backmarker and heavily dislikes the current regulations with his previous contract expiring at the end of 2026.

But all speculation stopped in September when the two-time champion announced his extension with Aston Martin into 2027. It is believed that him not publicly committing to F1 through the summer months was partly an effort to put pressure on the series to make changes.

As for team-mate Lance Stroll, his extension into 2027 arrived on the same day as Alonso, but was far from the same talking point considering father Lawrence owns the team. So, the 28-year-old Canadian, who next season will have had a decade in F1, effectively has a contract for as long as he likes.

Cadillac: Sergio Perez, Valtteri Bottas

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac, Sergio Perez, Cadillac Photo by: Bryn Lennon / Formula 1 via Getty Images

F1 newcomer Cadillac was the final squad to hold intrigue surrounding its driver pairing for 2027. Said intrigue didn’t really concern Sergio Perez, who in October signed a multi-year extension, but more Valtteri Bottas.

The 10-time grand prix winner has been outperformed by Perez this year, with a losing 16-10 head-to-head record in qualifying (including sprints), causing his seat to be thrown in doubt. Team management refused to publicly commit to him for some time as it weighed up the possibility of promoting reserve driver Colton Herta, given its desire to have an American driver racing for an American team.

One sticking point for Herta was his lack of an FIA Superlicence - required to compete in F1 - despite winning nine races in IndyCar. But he eventually obtained one via six FP1 appearances this year, yet that still wasn’t enough to grab an F1 seat with his highly disappointing F2 season, sitting 19th in the standings, in mind.

So, in November Cadillac announced its decision to stick with Bottas for 2027.

F1 2027 grid

Team Driver Driver Mercedes Kimi Antonelli George Russell Ferrari Lewis Hamilton Charles Leclerc McLaren Lando Norris Oscar Piastri Red Bull Max Verstappen Isack Hadjar Racing Bulls Liam Lawson Arvid Lindblad Alpine Pierre Gasly Franco Colapinto Haas Oliver Bearman Rafael Camara Audi Nico Hulkenberg Gabriel Bortoleto Williams Carlos Sainz Alex Albon Aston Martin Fernando Alonso Lance Stroll Cadillac Sergio Perez Valtteri Bottas

Sports.title: Alonso to not let his age determine F1 retirement
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso says he will quit Formula 1 when he feels slow and he doesn’t need to be as fit as a football player to be competitive.

Alonso is the most experienced driver in F1’s history, having competed in 23 seasons from 2001 to 2026, and the two-time champion has maintained his involvement well beyond his peers’ retirement age despite his current 245-race winless streak.

“Motorsport is a very unique sport in that regard,” the 45-year-old said. “You don't rely so much on your fitness to perform at the highest level. You are not a tennis or football player where you need to run all the time. You rely a lot on your technical environment.

“Of course, you still need to be fit and motivated, but at the end of the day I don't see anyone superior on the track. I don't feel that I've lost speed, or lost my reflexes at a race start, or lost motivation to come to the next grand prix.

“Some people say that the younger generation need a spot in F1 and drivers like myself and Lewis [Hamilton] need to move on because we've been on the grid so long, but motorsport doesn't work like that. I will stop when I feel slow, not when my passport says I'm this age or that age.”

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Alonso did clarify that he definitely wouldn’t be around when V8 engines return in 2030, and this may not be unrelated to his new role as a parent.

“That's been the toughest thing,” he said of spending so much time away from home. “Many nights this year, I've found myself wondering if I'm missing important moments.

“I think about the race team, too. My number-one mechanic and his partner had a boy three years ago, and they will have another child soon.

“Before I became a father, I probably didn't fully understand how much it meant to those who have children and how difficult it was to be away from them so often, but now I completely understand.

“And I think about them because they work harder than me. They spend more hours than I do at the circuit. They travel one or two days earlier than me, they travel one or two days after me back home, but they're always working hard, still motivated.

“Seeing that has helped me understand I'm a privileged part of the team and makes me want to work even harder together with them.”

Sports.title: Haas finally announces Bearman for F1 2027
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman will officially stay at Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season after he and the team finally put pen to paper on a new deal.

The American squad announced the renewal on Thursday, meaning the 21-year-old Briton will partner Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara at Haas next season.

It means the 2027 grid is now complete ahead of the final two rounds of the 2026 campaign, one in which Bearman has shone with 23 of Haas' 31 points.

Team boss Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us.

"We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track.

"He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward.

Ayao Komatsu, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

"TGR Haas F1 Team has one of the most exciting driver pairings on the grid, and I look forward to seeing Ollie flourish further with this incredible team."

Next season will be Bearman's third, full campaign in F1, although he did make three appearances in 2024 - his debut for Ferrari in Jeddah, before outings in Baku and Sao Paulo for Haas.

"It’s no secret that I’m delighted to be continuing with TGR Haas F1 Team into 2027," said Bearman.

"This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here.

"We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business."

Although this news comes late into the season, the Ferrari protege was always going to stay with Haas, which has loaned him from the Scuderia since his rookie year.

Oliver Bearman, Haas Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

But as he is entering year three with the American squad, Bearman's camp also wanted assurances about his long-term future - with driving for Ferrari being his ultimate goal.

Bearman's camp is also believed to have been looking for a significant pay increase, considering he's become Haas' lead driver after outperforming the now ousted Esteban Ocon.

At last week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman admitted he was "quite disappointed" that "I'm sitting here at round 20 without a contract signed for next year. It's been a strange situation, but we're getting there."

He now heads into Qatar this weekend with that new deal ahead of the Abu Dhabi finale, as Haas attempts to hold off Audi in the battle for seventh with three points separating them.

Sports.title: Williams breaches F1 2025 cost cap, Alpine guilty of procedural violation
Sports.content:
Williams and Alpine have fallen foul of Formula 1's 2025 cost cap, reaching an Accepted Breach Agreement with the FIA, with Williams incurring a sporting penalty for overspending and Alpine handed a fine.

The FIA announced on Wednesday that Williams overspent the 2025 cost cap by £627,000 or 0.48%. The overspend was found to be unintentional through the way the team interpreted the financial regulations, which meant it had committed what is called a "Minor Overspend Breach and a Procedural Breach".

The FIA's cost cap administration offered Williams an Accepted Breach Agreement (ABA), which the team accepted. The governing body noted the team "acted cooperatively and in good faith" and concluded that Williams did not attempt to seek a sporting advantage.

Nevertheless, the FIA handed Williams both a financial and sporting penalty. Alongside paying the FIA an undisclosed fine and reimbursing the cost cap administration expenses, Williams will be docked 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing over the next 12 months.

In a statement the team explained it had made an error while reorganising its team structure, believing some of its administrative costs fell outside the cost cap.

"The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. We believed these costs fell outside of the cap," a Williams spokesperson said. "Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process.

"Integrity is central to what Williams stands for, and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future. We have always been and will continue to be strong supporters of the Cost Cap, which naturally requires accurate policing to be effective."

Autosport understands Williams will receive a 1.5% hit on the maximum number of wind tunnel runs and CFD hours allowed across the second half of this season and the first half of 2027. That's against a 105% baseline for the current period, based on the team being eighth in the championship at the previous measuring point, and a 1.5% ATR hit against a 110% baseline for the following period, assuming Williams stays ninth in the standings until Abu Dhabi.

It means the Grove team respectively sees its number of wind tunnel hours reduced from 336 to 331 for the remainder of the current period, and from 352 to 347 for the first half of next year.

Alpine handed fine for procedural breach

Alpine was fined for a "Procedural Breach", which meant it did not actually overspend the 2025 cap but included a number of inaccuracies in its financial reporting.

Alpine wrongly excluded a number of non-sporting costs, including marketing and HR costs.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

As a result, Alpine will also be handed a fine while reimbursing the cost cap administration expenses. As is the case with Williams, the size of Alpine's fine was not disclosed, although similar offences are usually thought to be fined somewhere between $300,000 and $500,000.

"BWT Alpine Formula One Team acknowledges and accepts the findings of the Cost Cap Administration (CCA) for the 2025 Reporting Period," the team stated. "The team accepts that it unknowingly committed a Procedural Breach, which is a result of inaccuracies in the Full Year Reporting Documentation for costs related to exclusions and adjustments.

"The errors and inaccuracies in the reporting were specifically related to non-sporting and operational costs which the CCA recognised didn’t give the team any performance advantage, such as Marketing Activities, non-F1 Activities, HR Activities, Employee’s Bonus Costs, Offsetting of Costs, and Costs of Inventories.

"The team would also like to express its thanks to both the CCA and FIA, for its diligence and understanding throughout the entire process. The Financial Regulations are still relatively new, constantly evolving and complex, with some exclusions and adjustments being open to each team’s interpretation. The team acknowledges the collective efforts it needs to make across the business and recognises where improvements can be made in future."

Sports.title: Alonso: “We can't be competitive with the power unit we have”
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso says Honda is “a very long way behind” its Formula 1 rivals and Aston Martin therefore “can’t be competitive” with the Japanese engine, albeit expressing hope for the future.

As F1 switched to power units featuring 47% electrical energy, Honda’s new powertrain has been lacking both power and reliability. The ADUO upgrade introduced by the manufacturer at the Dutch Grand Prix improved its horsepower output at the expense of driveability, which had been a problem from the start with what Alonso described as “random downshifts”.

Lance Stroll suffered his 13th race retirement of the season in Brazil due to an ERS issue, with the situation so dire that Honda saw the near double finish in Las Vegas – Alonso retired before the last lap – as encouraging, despite the green cars only leading Valtteri Bottas’ Cadillac at the end of the race.

The high-speed layout didn’t help as Honda remains noticeably down on power, with the AMR26 33km/h slower than the fastest car in qualifying, while its straightline deficit was 27km/h in the race.

“On the engine side, we are a very long way behind and we can't be competitive with the power unit we have,” Alonso admitted on the Aston Martin website.

“There are some circuits like Las Vegas where we are losing more than two seconds a lap on the straights alone, and the reliability is not where it needs to be. No one is happy with how things are going on the PU side of things, but we know Honda is working hard to improve the situation.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Seeing the work and commitment going on behind the scenes gives me confidence for next year.”

On the chassis side however, progress meant Alonso managed to finish ninth on the winding Zandvoort track and eighth in Sepang’s wet conditions – two contexts in which the power deficit wasn’t as impactful.

“The Budapest chassis upgrade was supposed to deliver a certain lap time, and it delivered that lap time,” Alonso said. “We were competitive in Budapest and we scored points in Zandvoort and Malaysia.

“We've got into the midfield pack with only one large update to the chassis this season, so that has given me the confidence that we know the direction we're heading in and the belief that it's only a matter of time until we have a very good car.”

Sports.title: What's next for Herta after F1 2027 snub?
Sports.content:
Cadillac's decision to stick with veteran incumbent Valtteri Bottas to partner Sergio Perez is a choice for continuity and stability after a debut campaign plagued with issues for Formula 1's 11th team in 2026. It also raises key questions over what's next for Colton Herta.

With Cadillac's majority owner TWG enamoured with the prospect of having an American driver in one of its cars before too long, the team spared no expense on bringing Herta over, leaving the comfort of his IndyCar seat with sister team Andretti Global for a now-or-never shot at making it to F1.

Herta, a nine-time IndyCar race winner and the youngest to ever do so, faced a tricky challenge of adjusting to European racing in Formula 2, including mastering the peculiar Pirelli tyres that he would also find in F1.

That was dovetailed with private testing - Cadillac has no previous cars, so it rented a test from Alpine - and a number of grand prix FP1 sessions to boost his number of superlicence points to the critical number of 40.

After his sixth such test of the year in Brazil, Herta finally got to the magic number. But around that time, Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss and team principal Marcin Budkowski started aligning on the idea of retaining Bottas, deploying Herta as the official reserve driver for 2027, ready to step in if Bottas couldn't raise his performance ceiling over the first part of the season.

What Cadillac perhaps wasn't factoring in, is how Herta took the news of being snubbed. It is understood that the 26-year-old American has turned down the reserve role for now and has also decided against finishing his troubled F2 campaign with Hitech, forfeiting the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing, Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

While that decision may be clouded by his initial disappointment at missing out and Herta is desperate to keep racing competitively, rather than sit on the sidelines, it's a somewhat surprising position to hold. Being Cadillac's third driver behind 37-year-old Bottas still appears to be the position with the best odds of F1 promotion across the entire paddock, whether over the course of 2027 or in 2028.

"We've offered him a reserve position," Towriss said in Las Vegas. "The seat's open for ’28, so there are options on the table for Colton. There are options in other sports as well. I think he's decided on a direction, but we're still in conversations on that and look forward to seeing what Colton wants to do.

"It was definitely a tough decision, a tough discussion with Colton. I think he was disappointed. There was a lot of work, a lot of a build-up [that went] into this. I know Colton was very brave in even taking on this risk, going into F2 and trying to cram all this learning in."

The role, which is understood to be rather lucrative for a reserve driver, could also be paired with a one-off Indy 500 outing when the grid expands to 33 entries.

Why 2028 is a make-or-break year

Herta is now facing a career defining decision because of what's at stake in 2028. That is now the earliest he can get onto the F1 grid full-time if he makes a good enough impression to replace Bottas. It is likely also the last opportunity to do so, given how quickly reserve drivers tend to lose career momentum.

At the same time, his old home is also due a major renovation. For the first time in over 16 years, IndyCar will introduce an all-new car in 2028, the Dallara IR-28 which debuted to rave reviews in testing and is armed with a beefier 2.4l twin-turbo V6 engine.

Dallara IR-28 Photo by: Joey Barnes

With no full-time opportunities in IndyCar left for 2027 at this stage of the silly season, if Herta is deciding to call time on his F1 dream, then he needs to reposition himself as soon as possible to land a competitive seat for IndyCar 2028's season, whether that be with TWG or elsewhere. Returning in 2028, when the new chassis offers a blank slate, would be the most desirable timing from a competitive standpoint.

In any case, Herta has a decision to make as 2028 will be his make-or-break year. Either he swallows his pride and gives his F1 dream one last shot with Cadillac, or he abandons that dream prematurely and starts working on returning to a competitive IndyCar seat.

That process starts with his next move - right here, right now.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen considering 2027 Daytona 24 Hours entry
Sports.content:
Ahead of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Max Verstappen first paid a visit to Daytona.

The Dutchman said he was primarily there to film content with Red Bull, but the visit also raises the question of whether he is seriously considering taking part in the Rolex 24, the endurance race held on the road course of Daytona International Speedway.

When Autosport put that question to him during the Dutch media session in Las Vegas, Verstappen revealed that an appearance on the grid next winter has not been ruled out.

"We're looking into it, whether that's possible, but for now the visit was more about filming things with Red Bull."

Daytona is one of the endurance races high on the four-time F1 world champion's wish list. "That's definitely one that I want to do, yes," Verstappen confirmed.

It is also one of the races Verstappen could already contest during his F1 career, as the event takes place during the winter break. The 65th edition of the Daytona 24 Hours is scheduled for the weekend of 28-31 January 2027.

"Yes, that race is definitely possible already during my F1 career, so I hope so. But we'll have to wait a little longer [for news]. We still have some time for that as well."

Race start Photo by: Art Fleischmann

Verstappen made it clear that he would contest that race in a GT3 car, which at Daytona would mean competing in the GTD Pro category.

Following his adventures on the Nürburgring Nordschleife and the guest appearance for his own racing team at Portimao, it would mark Verstappen's first GT racing outing on American soil.

As for the Le Mans 24 Hours, Verstappen has already indicated that he will not compete there next year. The Dutchman only wants to race at the Circuit de la Sarthe with very thorough preparation, but he explained that Daytona is a different story.

"I really only want to do Le Mans in a hypercar. And then you have to think carefully about how you want to approach it. Do you want to do it yourself, or do you want to do it with a factory team? I still have time to figure that out as well.

"If I want to race at Daytona, or on the Nordschleife, that would be in a GT3 car. I don't want to say that's easier, but it is a little easier to organise than with a hypercar."

When it was pointed out that Verstappen would at least be giving motorsport fans something to look forward to during the F1 winter break – just as Fernando Alonso will do with the Dakar Rally – he laughed: "That's nice, isn't it? I always enjoy seeing drivers doing other things outside F1 and also getting enjoyment out of other racing series.

"The F1 season is already long enough, of course, but if I can combine it with bringing the family along, for example, then I'll still try to take part in other events."

That will most likely also apply to the Nürburgring 24 Hours in 2027, although the preparatory NLS races clash with F1 Grands Prix. Verstappen laughed, however: "Luckily, I already know that track!"

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon Photo by: ADAC Motorsport

He is still considering arranging a test day with his team as part of the preparations for the 24-hour race in the Eifel region.

"Yes, but of course you also have to look at that with the track, to see which days are possible. But we're going to see whether we can schedule another test day, because that's what every good team competing there does. So yes, that's definitely something we're going to look into as well."

Sports.title: Was the Las Vegas GP best race of the year - or too fake?
Sports.content:
The nature of the Las Vegas Grand Prix divided opinion in Formula 1's fanbase, and these opposing views were shared across the grid as the myriad overlapping passes were lauded and derided in equal measure.

Among the numerous changes for the lead, as Max Verstappen had to bat away passes from George Russell, Kimi Antonelli, and Lando Norris at various intervals throughout, the race was characterised by further chopping and changing in the overall order throughout.

Turn 14 was the most favoured overtaking zone, as the drivers used a combination of a powerful slipstream and overtake mode to make passes, but these were often temporary overtakes as the previous defending driver could often supply a riposte on the corner exit and reclaim position.

As such, although gaining position was simple enough, it required a lot more effort to retain it - even if a driver could build a gap, the slipstream-overtake combination could quickly close this down.

Across the range of opinions across the grid, Lewis Hamilton stated that it was a "great race" and found the style of racing on show exciting, and Mercedes CEO Toto Wolff agreed that it was "different" and "entertaining" - and more like a combination of oval races blended with modern-day F1.

"I thought it was a really great race. We knew that we have a pace deficit on the straights, but we weren't expecting it to be so brutal here with these long straights. It was important always to make sure you're behind the car and trying to move forwards," Hamilton said.

"You always have to make sure you're in a tow. Otherwise, you're just a sitting duck to people around. The Mercedes and the Red Bull, their power on the straight line is impressive, really impressive. My engine was on the limit. There was nothing else coming out.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I was pressing the button as hard as I could to make moves. I thought this race was one of the most interesting and most exciting. The car felt great today. Apart from the straight line, it felt great otherwise."

Wolff remarked that: "I guess you will have many people that will say, well, that's not racing.

"Personally, we need to be open-minded. Susie was in paddock club and she said that 90 minutes, people screaming with the overtakes. You were not quite sure whether you had the position or not.

"The instant feedback I got from friends watching, our sponsors, that was awesome. Stefano [Domenicali, F1 CEO] liked it very much. I think that's not going to happen everywhere.

"In a way, it's fitting that that was the Las Vegas race, like NASCAR and Indy 500 all together. To be honest, I don't know how long the race was, 90 minutes. For me, it was like 20 minutes. Because it was so different and so entertaining to watch."

Haas' Ollie Bearman took a slightly more dim view, stating that it was a fun race but rued that drivers were "penalised for passing" due to the chance for the following driver to supply an attack into the following corner.

He also disliked the "joke" slipstream tactics seen in qualifying, with cars jostling for position in the final runs to make the best use of the tow effect along the straight. He noted that the race had taken an unexpected path as the simulations conducted by the team had shown the overtake mode would only have a small effect.

Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi F1 Team, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

However, the power of the slipstream changed the dynamic of the race and retaining the tow was important to stay in the race. For Bearman, who had spent his afternoon battling the Audi pair, his slim chance of points had ebbed away when his pack dropped away from the top 10 and were unable to catch up having lost the slipstream to the cars ahead.

"It was definitely fun, I would say. It's a bit strange because you almost get penalised for passing, because you then lose the overtake. To be honest, I was just trying to stay in the race," Bearman said.

"I spent a lot of time sandwiched between the two Audis and I had a lot of opportunities to pass, but I opted just to stay behind, because I knew that if I go in front I would lose the overtake and lose a lot of race time.

"I was just trying to do my best race possible, knowing that the Audis were quicker than us and it was almost just a matter of time that they come past, but trying to delay it as much as possible.

"From simulations the overtake effect is very small, but then of course you have the slipstream effect as well, which is incredibly big. If I'm honest, it's a bit disappointing that we're doing these types of races, because even when you lose the slipstream, you lose so much time every lap, that you lose a lot of race time just from being alone on track.

"You saw it in quali yesterday, everyone coming out together like go-carts to take the slipstream. It's a bit of a joke, really."

Alpine's Pierre Gasly took a more cautious view, likening the Las Vegas spectacle to the Tour de France in choosing when to attack and when to be more conservative.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Although he also derived general enjoyment from the race, he noted that he would not want a full season of 'peloton-style' races.

"I mean, if you're leading, you can drive as fast as you can, you're not going to pull away. At some point in the race, I was like, this feels a bit like Tour de France," he said.

"You've got to be in the peloton and save your legs. Basically, that's what we did. We were saving our legs for the last sprint when we were managing the engine for the last few laps.

"It was fun but I don't want to see 24 races like that. I'm sure from the fans' point of view, it was incredible. I just don't feel it rewards all the driving in the corner because it's mainly a tow game. It was definitely very, very enjoyable."

Additional reporting by Filip Cleeren, Ronald Vording, and Cihangir Perperik

Sports.title: Haas finally confirms Bearman’s new contract for 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman will continue to drive for Haas in 2027, the team has confirmed.

Haas has not indicated Bearman’s new deal will last beyond next season.

The Ferrari junior driver will spend a third consecutive season at the team. Haas is a Ferrari power unit customer and Bearman’s team mate will be Rafael Camara, who is also part of the Italian manufacturer’s young driver programme.

Bearman said last week he was “disappointed” the team hadn’t clarified his situation for next year. He said some team members had been “questioning why [I] haven’t been announced yet.”

Team principal Ayao Komatsu said it had been “a natural decision” to retain Bearman. He has become the team’s most senior driver following its split from Esteban Ocon. Beraman’s former team mate was already due to leave the team at the end of the year, then was unexpectedly dropped mid-way through the Mexican Grand Prix weekend.

Komatsu said Bearman is clearly ready to lead Haas. “We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track,” he said. “He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward.”

Bearman said he is pleased to continue driving for Haas. “This team has played an integral role in my development and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here,” he said.

Haas’s announcement means the 2027 Formula 1 grid is complete. Haas will be the only team to start next season with a different driver line-up to the start of this year.

Sports.title: Williams given aero test reduction and fine for cost cap breach, Alpine also fined | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced two Formula 1 teams failed to comply with the cost cap regulations during the 2025 season.

Williams committed a “minor overspend breach and procedural breach”, said the governing body. Alpine was found to have committed a procedural breach only.

Both teams have been fined by the FIA and ordered to pay the costs incurred by the Cost Cap Administration panel. Williams has also been given a “minor sporting penalty” in the form of a reduction in the amount of aerodynamic testing it may conduct.

This is the second time each team has been fined for a breach of the cost cap. Williams was fined $25,000 in 2022 for submitting its paperwork late. Alpine paid $400,000 two years ago due to inaccuracies in its submissions.

In a departure from past practice, the FIA has not confirmed the size of the teams’ fines. Past penalties for cost cap breaches include Red Bull’s $7 million fine in 2022, the second-highest fine ever imposed on a Formula 1 team, for over-spending by £1.864 million (1.6% of the cap).

All nine other chassis constructors and F1’s five power unit manufacturers were found to have complied with the cost cap during 2025.

Williams acknowledged it had “unintentionally” exceeded the cost cap by £627,000. “The FIA has determined that the team committed a minor overspend breach and an accompanying procedural breach, unintentionally exceeding the cap by £627,000 – 0.48% over the 2025 cost cap,” it said in a statement.

“The agreed outcome is a financial penalty and a 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing over the next 12 months.

“The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap.

“The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process.

Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future.”

Williams team principal James Vowles has recently called for changes to F1’s cost cap rules which he claims makes it harder for smaller teams to invest in their facilities. “We have always been and will continue to be strong supporters of the Cost Cap, which naturally requires accurate policing to be effective,” Williams’s statement concluded.

Alpine also said it “acknowledges and accepts” the Cost Cap Administration’s findings.

“The errors and inaccuracies in the reporting were specifically related to non-sporting and operational costs which the CCA recognised didn’t give the team any performance advantage, such as marketing activities, non-F1 activities, HR activities, employee’s [sic] bonus costs, offsetting of costs, and costs of inventories.



“The team would also like to express its thanks to both the CCA and FIA, for its diligence and understanding throughout the entire process. The Financial Regulations are still relatively new, constantly evolving and complex, with some exclusions and adjustments being open to each team’s interpretation. The team acknowledges the collective efforts it needs to make across the business and recognises where improvements can be made in future.”

The FIA F1 Financial Regulations for F1 Teams, Issue 25, dated 31 July 2025 (“Financial Regulations”), govern the substantive breaches and applicable sanctions for the 2025 Reporting Period, whereas the applicable procedural provisions of the 2026 FIA F1 Regulations govern the resolution of this matter, subject to Article A9.8.2 of Section A thereof. The FIA F1 Financial Regulations, as applicable, are issued by the FIA and form part of the terms and conditions of participation in the FIA Formula One World Championship. The Cost Cap Administration recognised that: – WGPE has acted cooperatively and in a spirit of good faith throughout the review process and has provided additional information and evidence, both voluntarily and when requested, in a comprehensive and timely manner; – there is no accusation or evidence that WGPE sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the Cost Cap Administration; – the Financial Regulations are complex, and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted by WGPE in good faith; WGPE has accepted the FIA’s interpretation and the resulting breaches; – there is no evidence that WGPE gained or sought to gain any advantage (sporting or otherwise) from the identified breaches; and – the Minor Overspend Breach amounts to £627k and therefore, with 0.48% over the 2025 Cost Cap, falls at the lower end of the [less than] 5% minor overspend range. The Cost Cap Administration considered it appropriate, in these circumstances, to offer WGPE an ABA to resolve this matter, taking into account the unintentional and limited nature and extent of the Minor Overspend Breach and of the Procedural Breach in issue, and WGPE’s willingness to accept the breach and to cooperate with the Cost Cap Administration. That offer was accepted by WGPE. The ABA concerns: – a Procedural Breach committed by WGPE under Article 8.1, within the meaning of Article 8.2(e), of the Financial Regulations, due to WGPE’s failure to file accurate Full Year Reporting Documentation in respect of the 2025 Reporting Period, as a result of errors in the exclusion and adjustment of costs in the calculation of WGPE’s Relevant Costs, and – consequently, a Minor Overspend Breach under Article 8.10(b) of the Financial Regulations, as WGPE’s Relevant Costs exceeded the 2025 Cost Cap by less than 5%, namely by £627k (i.e., 0.48%), Summary of ABA terms and sanctions: In accordance with the Cost Cap Administration’s Final Findings, WGPE has acknowledged that its Full Year Reporting Documentation in respect of the 2025 Reporting Period contained inaccuracies relating, in particular, to the following most relevant exclusions and adjustments: – exclusion of costs pursuant to Article 3.1(i) of the Financial Regulations (concerning costs of HR, Legal and Finance Activities); – adjustment of costs pursuant to Article 4.1(f)(iii) of the Financial Regulations (concerning Redundant Inventories); WGPE has accepted that, through adopting an interpretation in good faith of the Financial Regulations, it has unintentionally committed a Minor Overspend Breach under Article 8.10(b) of the Financial Regulations by exceeding the 2025 Cost Cap by £627k (0.48%) and a Procedural Breach under Article 8.1, within the meaning of Article 8.2(e), of the Financial Regulations by submitting inaccurate Full Year Reporting Documentation in respect of the 2025 Reporting Period, as explained above. On that basis, WGPE has accepted the imposition of the following sanctions in full and final settlement of the Minor Overspend Breach and of the Procedural Breach: – WGPE must pay a Financial Penalty to the FIA within 30 days of the date of execution of the ABA (Article 9.5 of the Financial Regulations); and – WGPE receives a Minor Sporting Penalty in the form of a limitation of WGPE’s ability to conduct aerodynamic Testing during a period of 12 months from the date of execution of the ABA through the application of a subtraction of 1.5% of the Coefficient C used to calculate the individual Restricted Wind Tunnel Testing (RWTT) and Restricted Computational Fluid Dynamics (RCFD) limits applicable to WGPE as set out in Article F4.6 of 2026 FIA F1 Regulations – Section F [Operational Regulations], Issue 11, dated 1 October 2026 (“Section F”). For example, if the Coefficient C, based on WGPE’s championship position is 90%, the effective new value of C will be: CNEW=90% – 1.5% = 88.5%. – WGPE bears the costs incurred by the Cost Cap Administration in connection with its investigation of WGPE’s Minor Overspend Breach and Procedural Breach and the preparation of the ABA (Article D8.10.2.b of Section D). The Cost Cap Administration’s decision to enter into the ABA constitutes its final decision resolving this matter and is not subject to appeal. If WGPE fails to comply with the ABA, the Cost Cap Administration shall refer the matter to the Cost Cap Adjudication Panel in accordance with the applicable provisions of Section D. Such non-compliance would constitute a distinct Procedural Breach.
