Sports.title: F1 returns to the track its tyres can’t cope with: Seven Qatar GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Doubt hung over the Qatar Grand Prix for months as Formula 1 made contingency plans to relocate its final two rounds of the world championship.

However, despite ongoing concerns over the safety of travelling to the Middle East due to the war in Iran, F1 has decided to go ahead with the race.

Meanwhile, F1’s official tyre supplier Pirelli has been forced to admit its rubber cannot last the distance at this track. It will therefore once again enforce limits on how far each driver may run on a set of tyres.

Here are the talking points for this weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix.

Visit Qatar?

When Liberty Media’s other motorsport championship visited Qatar three weeks ago, not all of the teams accompanied them. Moto GP manufacturer Yamaha chose to steer clear of the region as it was not prepared to accept the risks of travelling there.

Several broadcasters also stayed away from Moto GP’s Qatar round. That will also be the case for this weekend’s F1 event – Sky Germany’s crew is reportedly not attending – but no F1 teams have indicated they will not participate.

Clearly, different groups have different assessments of how wise it is to travel to the region. Hopefully all involved stay safe, but when alternative venues were available it does not seem like a risk worth taking – regardless of whether the championships were already decided.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Pirelli’s impossible challenge

F1 embarks on its fifth event at the Losail International Circuit still without tyres that are up to racing on it. For the third time, Pirelli has told teams it cannot risk letting them run up to 56 laps on a single set of tyres and has imposed a maximum limit of less than half that – just 27.

This may be an increase over previous limits (18 in 2023, 25 last year) but Losail remains unique among F1 venues as being the only place where Pirelli imposes such a restriction. This will force teams to make two pit stops, reducing their strategic options.

But F1 appears uninterested in fixing the problem: earlier this year it extended Pirelli’s contract again.

More friction at Ferrari

The tension at Ferrari hit new heights last weekend after Charles Leclerc knocked Lewis Hamilton into a spin mid-race. Team principal Frederic Vasseur made it clear he agreed with the stewards’ view that Leclerc was “wholly” to blame for the collision.

It was the second time in three events the Ferrari drivers have badly compromised each other’s race. Whatever Vasseur has done up until now to contain the rivalry appears not to be working.

What can he do to prevent the pair costing each other points again – particularly on a track which should suit the SF-25 better than the last one?

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Another round of Russell versus Verstappen

Max Verstappen was pitiless in his response to George Russell’s criticism of him during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend. “He’s so far below my level,” remarked Verstappen in the press conference following his victory.

The pair have clashed several times before and the Losail track was the scene of one of their bitterest fall-outs two years ago. Verstappen accused his rival of “lying” when they met the stewards; Russell said the Red Bull driver told him “I’m going to purposefully crash into you, I’m going to put you on your fucking head in the wall.”

Despite all that, during last week’s race Russell also made a bizarre offer to co-operate with Verstappen so they could pull away from their pursuers. It’s hard to imagine him saying the same again following Verstappen’s latest comments.

Verstappen’s real new rival?

While Verstappen’s rivalry with Russell has grabbed the headlines, is the other Mercedes driver the one he should really pay attention to? Andrea Kimi Antonelli may have clinched this year’s world championship but Verstappen has out-scored him (and everyone else) over the past 15 rounds stretching back to the Monaco Grand Prix.

Just 12 months ago at this very race the Verstappen camp was accusing Antonelli of trying to thwart his bid to win the world championship. Verstappen’s race engineer at the time, Gianpiero Lambiase, and former Red Bull consultant Helmut Marko both claimed Antonelli deliberately let Lando Norris past in the closing stages of last year’s race.

Antonelli, of course, had done nothing of the sort, but the damage had been done and the vitriol he faced on social media was horrific.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Curb your enthusiasm

The combination of the kerbs at the Losail track and the high speeds at which F1 cars hit them mean drivers must take care to avoid damaging their cars this weekend. With several teams getting low on parts as the end of the season draws near, some drivers may have to curb their kerb use.

One-off format switch

After three years hosting sprint races, the Qatar Grand Prix reverts to the traditional format this weekend with three practice sessions. Unfortunately, it’s just a one-off: this will be one of 10 sprint events on the 2027 F1 calendar.

Sports.title: Stats: Mercedes have disappeared from the podium since their championship win | 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen scored the 75th victory of his career in last weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, meaning he is three-quarters of the way towards reaching a century of victories.

Back when he scored his first win just over 10 years ago at the age of 18, we polled RaceFans readers on whether he would reach 100 grand prix wins. Even at that early stage 17% of you predicted he would – a figure which might look a lot higher if we repeated the poll today.

Verstappen also claims his 51st pole position – Andrea Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying, but his penalty left him fifth on the grid.

Together, Verstappen and Red Bull have now won three of the four races on the Las Vegas Strip Circuit since it joined the calendar.

However Verstappen was beaten to fastest lap by another driver from the Red Bull stable – Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson, who had little else to do as he started a lap down and was still well behind the field after the Safety Car restart.

This was Lawson’s first fastest lap of his career. He became the 142nd different driver to achieve a fastest lap and the first driver from New Zealand to do so in over 50 years. He follows Denny Hulme, who took his ninth and final fastest lap in the 1974 Belgian Grand Prix at Nivelles, for McLaren.

McLaren enjoyed by far their best result at Las Vegas, having never previously scored a top-five finish at the track. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri took second and fifth respectively last year before they were both disqualified. Norris got to keep his second place this time, while Piastri took third after an impressive climb from 17th on the grid.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

However one team was conspicuously absent from the podium for the second race weekend in a row.

Mercedes got at least one of their cars on the podium at every race from the beginning of the season. That run ended in Brazil, where they clinched the constructors’ championship. They missed the podium again in Las Vegas as Andrea Kimi Antonelli sank from second to fourth at the end of the race.

Pierre Gasly rebounded from a frustrating first stint, during which he exchanged sharp words with his race engineer, to score fifth place. That was Alpine’s best result since the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, where Gasly produced the same result. With Franco Colapinto following him home, Alpine took their largest points score since their double podium finish at the Brazilian Grand Prix that same year.

Alpine’s haul of 18 points increased their total to 87, which is exactly what they scored in the previous two seasons combined. However they need to do as well over the final races to beat their 2023 score, and much better to equal their 2021 or 2022 totals.

Carlos Sainz Jnr brought Williams some cheer by equalling their best result of the season with eighth place. However Audi once again narrowly missed out on points: Nico Hulkenberg recorded their 11th finish in 11th place this year.

Over to you

Sports.title: ‘Maybe I’m delusional but I genuinely feel like a podium was possible’ – Lindblad | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Arvid Lindblad says he and Racing Bulls are still seeking an explanation for the spin which put him out of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

He was running sixth behind the Safety Car when he lost control and spun to a stop. He was then unable to select reverse and rejoin.

In a social media post two days after the race, Lindblad said he remained “absolutely devastated” by the result.

“For the first time in my career [I was] fighting in the top five with a genuine chance of a special result. To end it in the way it did, losing the car under SC, is just incredibly hard to take.

“No words to describe how I’m feeling right now. We work for years, our whole lives, for these moments and opportunities. In a midfield car, they come very rarely, and when they do, you need to grab them with both hands. The pain of missing out on something like this, and the endless thoughts of what could have been, will always hurt.”

Lindblad said he experienced something strange before his spin and the team still does not understand what caused it.

“Naturally, as the driver, you blame yourself in these moments,” he said. “Honestly, I still don’t really understand what happened.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I experienced a terrible shift, something very abnormal, and the team are working hard to understand why. I don’t know whether there was anything I could have done differently or if it’s just one of those things but it’s hard not to question yourself.

“Regardless, that doesn’t change the missed opportunity or how much it hurts right now.”

He had just gained a position from Andrea Kimi Antonelli during the pit stops when he spun out. Antonelli started the penultimate lap in second place and Lindblad believes he could have been in contention at the front.

“Maybe I’m delusional, but I genuinely feel like a podium was possible,” he said. “It felt like one of those special days, a different type of race where opportunities rarely present themselves, and we were right there to take advantage.

“Luckily we’re racing again in a few days, but it’ll take much longer than that for the pain of this one to settle.”

Sports.title: Joseph Parker Ready To Break Daniel Dubois Will Again
Sports.content:
Could Daniel Dubois quit if Joseph Parker takes him into the later rounds and he feels the fight slipping away? Dubois has proven to be a royal basket case when the going gets tough in fights. He’s fine when things are going well, but he goes to pieces when dealing with adversity.

We may see that happen before our eyes on January 30 when he defends his WBO heavyweight title against the experienced veteran Parker at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England. Parker is accustomed to war in the trenches and thrives on conflict. You can’t say the same thing about Dubois.

Queensberry Promotions is trying to sell this thing as unfinished business from February 2025 in Riyadh, where Dubois pulled out during fight week sick, and Parker knocked out an out-of-shape Martin Bakole in two rounds. Plenty of boxing fans still think Dubois got cold feet back then rather than being ill.

All I can say is he didn’t look thrilled sitting across from Parker on DAZN. He had fear in his eyes, being stared down by Parker. From that brief meeting, it’s easy to believe he pulled out of the fight because of stage fright.

Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) will be favored to win, yet his reckless style leaves him wide open for a fast veteran counterpuncher. He marches forward behind a hard jab, which worked well for him against Jarrell Miller and Anthony Joshua. It’s going to take more than a jab to defeat Parker because he’s well equipped to neutralize that weapon.

If Parker gets inside and forces Dubois onto his back foot, Dubois tends to mentally crumble fast. Once Dubois hits the deck, he appears to give up on himself, looking at his corner for help.

Dubois has been through a lot of brutal fights since 2022, and we’ve all seen his chin give out when somebody survives his early bum rush and hits him flush, just like Oleksandr Usyk and Kevin Lerena did. You could see the look of resignation on Dubois’ face in those fights. He got lucky against Lerena when his opponent gassed out.

Parker (36-4, 24 KOs) is coming back after a year out since Fabio Wardley stopped him in the eleventh round in October 2025. He served a suspension, but chose not to take a tune-up. It makes sense because he wasn’t going to pass up this golden opportunity to relieve a vulnerable champion of his WBO belt,

“I almost feel like there’s a bit of me that thinks Joseph deserves it,” said Ade Oladipo on his YouTube channel.

It makes sense why Frank Warren is making this fight. He also promotes WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and IBF belt holder Filip Hrgovic. Matching the aging, soon-to-be 35-year-old Parker against Dubois removes the risk that would be there if he put him in against Kabayel or Hrgovic. Parker is a safer opponent on paper, and even if there is an upset, the WBO title still stays with Queensberry. Although Dubois did beat Hrgovic in the past, it would be risky putting him in with him now after Hrgovic’s win over Moses Itauma. The last thing Warren needs is for Hrgovic to beat Dubois.

Parker’s hunger still makes him a real threat to beat Dubois. If Parker is still standing past the midpoint of the fight, he could break Dubois down and make him quit like he did against Usyk and Joe Joyce. As the saying goes, once a quitter, always a quitter.

Sports.title: British Fans Rip Weak Fury vs. Joshua Undercard Lineup
Sports.content:
Turki Alalshikh revealed the full card for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua event on December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and the fan reaction has been negative, particularly among Brits.

With the Fury vs. Joshua fight being billed as the biggest domestic heavyweight bout in years in the main event, fans are hopping mad that the undercard looks like it’s been thrown together without any care about quality.

Fans are finally realizing they’re basically paying for the Fury vs. Joshua fight and getting nothing else worth watching.

Virtually all the undercard bouts, including the co-feature pitting Deontay Wilder vs. Martin Bakole, have been bashed as pure 100% garbage. Fans who subscribed to Netflix just to see the event aren’t happy about it. I’m not surprised.

We saw the same thing with Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao and Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford. All the effort and dough went into the main events for those two mega-events, and man, did the undercards look like junk of the highest kind.

Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn got one of his fighters, former two-time super featherweight champion Joe Cordina, onto the card. The kicker is that Cordina, 35, has been placed on the preliminary portion of the card, fighting Mauricio Lara, out of sight, out of mind.

If Hearn thought this was Cordina’s big chance to win back the fans he lost when he was knocked out by Anthony Cacace in the eighth round in May 2024, he can forget it.

“What about Joe Cordina?” Hearn said when discussing the lineup. “What about a two-time world champion from Wales? Absolutely mental.”

Hearn had been banging the drum about wanting Cordina to fight on the main card against Manny Pacquiao, WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason, or Sam Noakes. Instead of fighting one of them in a highly visible fight, Cordina will be hidden away on the prelim card that will be shown on Netflix, TikTok, and The Ring social channels.

Hearn has got to be hopping mad, seeing his fighter fail to make the grade for the main card. I can totally understand the organizers’ decision to place the Cordina vs. Lara fight on the prelim card. Neither of these two fighters has beaten anyone halfway decent since losing. Cordina beat a fringe contender in Gabriel Flores Jr. and a lower-level fighter in Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz since losing to Cacace.

As for Lara, he’s won his last five fights against obscure opposition in confidence builders after fighting to a draw against Daniel Lugo in February 2024 and losing to Leigh Wood by a 12-round unanimous decision in May 2023.

The main card is just as abysmal, with Deontay Wilder facing replacement opponent Martin Bakole in the chief support bout after Jai Opetaia’s injury pullout, Zuffa heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter battling Michael Essomba, and Moses Jolly fighting Igor Adiel Macedo.

Hearn blasted Zuffa promoter Dana White and Zuffa’s influence for the poor undercard, and British fans are replying in droves to Turki’s undercard lineup, echoing Hearn’s thoughts. The people who paid good cash for tickets to see the event live in Cardiff are harping about the scarcity of UK fighters, the 1:30 a.m. local start time for the headliner, and the lack of quality fights beyond the Joshua vs. Fury fight.

The rest of the preliminary lineup is filled with obscure prospects and names that even hardcore boxing fans won’t recognize, aside from Tyson’s younger brother Roman Fury. If you’re tuning in on December 11, you don’t need to set your alarm until right before the main event.

Sports.title: WBA Sets 75-25 Split for Teofimo Lopez Against Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
It’s not looking good for Teofimo Lopez to dodge his mandatory obligations at welterweight. Today, the WBA called a purse bid for December 4 in Cypress, Texas, for a fight between WBA welterweight Super Champion Teofimo and Jack Catterall with a slanted 75/25 purse split.

Financially, that should make Teofimo happy. Even with three-quarters of the money guaranteed, he’s shown no eagerness to sign to fight the mandatory he inherited after his win over WBA champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero by majority decision on August 22. Lopez needs a special permit from the WBA to avoid Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs), but he may not get his wish. It’s understandable why Teofimo doesn’t want to fight Catterall. It’s a style that he’s struggled with, and it’s unlikely he would win.

Teofimo (23-2, 13 KOs) wants to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in what would be a lucrative unification, where even if he loses, he’d still do well financially. He needs the WBA title for purse negotiations more so than it being a valuable chip to create more interest in a fight with Ryan.

Teofimo’s title isn’t why fans are interested in seeing the fight. For him, it’s just a negotiation tool to get a better deal, because he lacks Ryan’s popularity to get an even split. Even with a title, you can argue that Teofimo doesn’t rate a 50/50 purse split.

Catterall Risk Explains Lopez Delay

If this were an easy mark, Lopez would be overjoyed at receiving a 75/25 gift split from the WBA. Catterall’s style is similar to Shakur Stevenson’s, which left Teofimo baffled and helpless in a unanimous decision loss over 12 rounds earlier this year at Madison Square Garden on January 31. Teofimo looked embarrassingly bad in that fight. The judges scored it 119 to 109 on all three cards, and he was outlanded 165 to 72.

Defensively, Catterall isn’t as sharp as Shakur, but he’s close enough to be the same kind of nightmare for Teofimo. On offense, Catterall is superior to Shakur, and coupled with his defensive ability, he would be a difficult problem for Teofimo to try and figure out. Besides all that, the pressure that Teofimo would be under would be severe if he needs to defeat Catterall to get to the lucrative payday fight against Ryan Garcia.

If he gets beaten by Catterall, he can forget about fighting Ryan for the time being. Unlike his loss to Shakur, Teofimo wouldn’t be given a straight title shot immediately after. He’d have to rebuild and get in line, which is what he should have had to do after losing to Stevenson instead of being given a crack at Rolly’s WBA title.

Catterall captured his WBA regular welterweight title by beating former mandatory Shakhram Giyasov by a wide 12-round unanimous decision last May. Giyasov was the mandatory challenger that Rolly was avoiding. Now, we’re seeing the new WBA champion Teofimo trying to give Catterall similar treatment. The WBA can stop this cycle by rejecting Teofimo’s request for a special permit.

It’s easy to predict what Lopez’s next move will be if the WBA rejects his appeal. Vacating the WBA belt will be the easiest way of getting Catterall out of his path to a fight with Ryan. Teofimo will still get a nice payday against Ryan, but probably not as nice as it would be if he still had his WBA title.

Sports.title: Brian Mendoza Replaces Keith Thurman in Weak Vergil Ortiz Jr. Co-Feature
Sports.content:
PBC and Golden Boy Promotions made it official today with Brian Mendoza replacing Keith Thurman as Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s opponent for his 10-round co-feature middleweight bout on December 5 at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona.

Ortiz Jr. and Mendoza will be fighting on the undercard of WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion David Benavidez’s unification bout against WBC champion Michal Cieslak on DAZN PPV and Prime Video.

The addition of Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) has received mixed views from fans. Many of them view the 32-year-old as a poor replacement, given his 1-3 record in his last four fights. That’s not exactly top shelf unless losing is the benchmark requirement used to get enlisted as a fill-in opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.

Back in Mediocrity Since Fundora

What Mendoza has got going for him is that he knocked out Sebastian Fundora in the seventh round in April 2023 in a huge upset at the time. Fundora was beating the living daylights out of Mendoza for the first six rounds until he got careless in the seventh and got clipped. Since then, Mendoza’s career has slipped back to what it was before that win. That was his textbook Cinderella night, where he got lucky in a fight that he was getting beaten up in.

What’s interesting is that fans online see this as an upgrade over 38-year-old Thurman, just because of his win over Fundora. If you look at Mendoza’s results since that upset, he’s a major downgrade, and that’s saying a lot because Thurman was not a great opponent. He’s not a middleweight, and definitely not young.

Tim Tszyu beat Mendoza by a wide 12-round unanimous decision in October 2023. That fight was an example of Mendoza being brought back down to earth. It wasn’t even slightly a close fight. It looked like Mendoza wandered into the ring from the crowd, and Tszyu took advantage by beating the stuffing out of him. Serhii Bohachuk did the same thing to Mendoza in a clash for the interim WBC junior middleweight title in March 2024.

The only win for Mendoza in the last three years came against journeyman Jesus Antonio Rojas (12-11-2, 10 KOs). It took that level of opponent for Mendoza to snap his two-fight losing streak. In Mendoza’s last fight, he returned to his losing ways, getting trounced by Yoenis Tellez by a one-sided 10-round unanimous decision in March 2026.

Basically, what we’re seeing here is not a dangerous threat being used as a replacement opponent for Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs), who recently looked like pure gold in wins over Israil Madrimov, Bohachuk, and Erickson Lubin.

A Cheap Showcase for Ortiz Jr.

Yanking Mendoza out of his fight with Eric Priest enabled Sampson Boxing, TGB Promotions, and Golden Boy Promotions to save money on finding a quality opponent. It’s a showcase fight for Ortiz Jr. Ideally, they should have spent some money to enlist a quality middleweight contender like Yoenli Hernandez to put Ortiz Jr. in a sink-or-swim fight.

What Mendoza does have going for him is a strong chin, as he’s never been knocked out in his career. So if the idea is for Ortiz Jr. to get some rounds in to sharpen up after a year on the shelf, Mendoza is the guy for the job. However, the referee may step in and halt this fight anyway because of the likely one-sided nature of it.

Entertainment-wise, Mendoza eating hard shots from Ortiz Jr. is not fun to watch in a PPV co-feature slot. Fans want competitive fights, not slaughters.

Ortiz Jr. is 28 years old, making the move up to middleweight, and has still accomplished little in his career. It’s got to bug him that he sees fighters like Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis taking the express route to superstardom, leaving him behind. The difference is, Ennis has been a risk-taker from day one, hasn’t feasted on weak opposition, and has stayed active. In contrast, Ortiz Jr. hasn’t fought the best, and he’s missed a lot of time in his career due to health and promotional issues.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Gets Worst Possible Replacement In Martin Bakole
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder is facing the worst possible replacement opponent for him in his December 11th fight in Cardiff against the heavy-handed Martin Bakole. It’s not the type of opponent that the 41-year-old Wilder’s legs can deal with at this stage of his career.

Boxing analyst Sergio Mora pointed out this week that Wilder no longer has the mobility at his age to avoid being walked down by a big puncher like Bakole. He feels that Wilder will have problems keeping Bakole off of him and will be forced to slug it out right off the bat from round 1 on December 11th.

“If you don’t fight him off the right way, he’s going to mow you down. And you got to have legs to do that,” said Mora on Chris Mannix’s podcast.

Wilder never really had great leg movement. If you look at his earliest fights against Harold Sconiers and Bermane Stiverne, he wasn’t a mover. He was winning by unleashing his right hand on them. Back then, before the two later shoulder surgeries on that side, Wilder’s right hand was lethal. It made up for his lack of mobility and boxing skills.

After his originally scheduled opponent, Jai Opetaia, dropped out due to a hand injury, the former WBC heavyweight champion Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) wanted a rematch with Derek Chisora or a fight with Jarrell Miller. Neither was selected, which is good news for fans. Both are long in the tooth and don’t have the kind of power that could erase Wilder the way Bakole can.

For what Wilder is aiming for, a world title shot in his next fight, he should have to fight and beat the likes of Bakole to get his wish. It would look pathetic if Wilder is given a title shot after beating an old war horse like Chisora a second time or getting past Miller.

Why Bakole Is A Dangerous Gamble

Despite Bakole being held to a draw against Efe Ajagba in his last outing, and knocked out in the second round by Joseph Parker in a short-notice fight in 2025, Bakole still has power in both hands. He’s dangerous up close when he lands cleanly.

In those two fights, Bakole wasn’t in the best shape in terms of his weight. For this one, he’d been training to fight Solomon Adebayo on the December 11th undercard. Being in shape for this fight means Bakole will be a constant threat to Wilder in the early rounds.

If Wilder’s right hand is back to full strength, he could stop Bakole. However, Wilder hasn’t shown his once-devastating power since 2022, when he knocked out Robert Helenius in the 1st round. Mora and Mannix agreed that Jarrell Miller would have been the better choice to sell the matchup without carrying the same threat as Bakole. The organizers made the right choice because the card needed a high-drama matchup. We don’t see that in the main event or any of the undercard fights.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Picks Safe Money Fights Over Young Sharks
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) is already looking past his December 11 clash against Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) at a 1:30 AM UK start in Cardiff to map out his final two retirement fights. The early morning start time for the Joshua fight is to satisfy American viewers on Netflix, and it’s obviously not ideal for the aging 38-year-old Fury.

Staying up late will be hard on his body and could lead to another off performance, as we saw in his two defeats against Oleksandr Usyk. The last thing Fury needs is to look slow and lose to Joshua, setting a bad start to his three-fight retirement plan.

Today, the Cardiff Council’s licensing sub-committee granted a special variation, extending the stadium’s operating hours until 3:00 AM. This move made it possible for the Fury vs. Joshua fight to begin at 1:30 AM local time in Cardiff.

Also today, Fury revealed his schedule on OOOSCH TV, saying he will fight only two more times after Joshua. He wants a rematch with Joshua if the first fight is competitive, followed by a trilogy bout against Oleksandr Usyk.

“I’m interested in fighting Anthony Joshua, maybe rematch him if it’s a good fight, and then maybe [have] a trilogy with Oleksandr Usyk if it makes sense and if I get a fair shake,” Fury told OOOSCH TV. “There’s nobody else, really, that I’m interested in fighting.”

It’s not a coincidence that the two fighters Fury plans on facing to end his career, Joshua and Usyk, are the biggest money heavyweights in the division. Even if Fury loses to both, he’ll be paid far better than if he were to face another top contender, like Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois, or Agit Kabayel.

Ideally, it would be better for the sport if Fury faced one of those heavyweights or Moses Itauma to serve as a springboard to make a star out of one of the younger contenders or champions. Fighters in the past were willing to do that, yet we see it less and less in an era where fighters are more protective, selfish, careful, and money-focused. As such, you see Fury aiming for 37-year-old Joshua and 39-year-old Usyk for his final two fights instead of the young guns, Dubois and Itauma.

Fury Overlooks His Recent Form

What we saw of Joshua and Fury in recent fights was lackluster performances, showing that both fighters are long in the tooth ahead of their December 11 fight. Those outings may be one reason why there is so little interest in their clash next month. They both looked so feeble that fans can’t get excited about a fight between two faded heavyweights.

To make it interesting for fans, it would have been more appealing to see Fury and Joshua walk the plank against one of the big four: Itauma, Dubois, Kabayel, or Hrgovic. Fans would tune in just to see how the older heavyweights hold up. Putting them in together is not appealing in the least, because there’s no real gain for the winner in a battle of shot fighters. It only gets interesting if you throw Joshua and Fury in the ring with one of those ravenous sharks to see how they fare.

Fury looked terrible stopping 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in seven rounds in Thailand on July 24. One day later in Jeddah, the 37-year-old Joshua was surprisingly dropped by what was supposed to be a soft opponent, Kristian Prenga, before coming back to stop him in the second round.

That fight was very strange, as Prenga didn’t throw any punches in the second round after having Joshua on the verge of being halted as the first round ended. Why not go for the kill? I’ve never seen anything like it, and Joshua got lucky. If Prenga had thrown anything, he likely would have finished Joshua at the beginning of the second round.

Interestingly, the December 11 fight contract doesn’t include a rematch clause for their vacant WBA heavyweight title. That leaves it up to Turki Alalshikh and Netflix to decide whether they wish to finance a second fight between Joshua and Fury. It would be perfectly understandable if they pass. If both look poor or if the card bombs in bringing in subscribers to Netflix, I don’t see why they would want to pay for a second fight.

That goes for putting the winner or the loser in with Usyk. A fight between Fury or Joshua and Usyk would be expensive and wouldn’t produce the numbers or entertainment needed to make it worthwhile. Putting them in with Itauma and watching the timer to see how long they last would be far more fun to watch.

Usyk already beat Fury twice in 2024, and he’s talking about moving down to cruiserweight to fight champion David Benavidez instead of waiting for Fury. You can respect that.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Claims Martin Bakole Win Earns Title Shot
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder believes a victory over his replacement opponent, Martin Bakole, on December 11 in Cardiff will pave the way to a world heavyweight title shot. As wacky as this sounds, it wouldn’t be a shock if it actually happens. The division is starved for recognizable names, and if nothing else, the 41-year-old Wilder is well known.

Turki Alalshikh confirmed that Bakole (21-2-1, 16 KOs) would replace the injured Jai Opetaia as Wilder’s opponent for their co-feature fight on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium.

Bakole is a decent opponent for Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs), but hardly the type of contender that would erase six years of repeated losses. Definitely not good enough to vault Wilder into a world title fight.

“We’re going to be fighting Martin Bakole. He is next, and then after that it’s going to be crazy,” said Wilder in a social media video. “Once I beat him, I’m not going to move forward with the information I’ve received, but once I beat him, you’re looking at the new heavyweight champion of the world. And the new two-time heavyweight champion. Martin, here we come. I appreciate you for accepting the opportunity. Let’s give the fans and the people something to talk about for the rest of their lives.”

Instead of Wilder hoping for a shot at one of the other heavyweight champions, he should be campaigning for the winner of the Fury vs. Joshua WBA title fight. That’s the bigger payday by far.

If Joshua and Wilder both come out victorious, promoters can finally make their long-awaited fight, as long as Fury doesn’t push for an immediate rematch.

How The Title Path Works

Deontay has been beltless since Fury knocked him out in February 2020. Beating 42-year-old Derek Chisora by a 12-round split decision in April and stopping little-known Tyrrell Anthony Herndon in June 2025 in his last two fights aren’t enough to overcome being stopped in five rounds by Zhilei Zhang and beaten by Joseph Parker by a 12-round decision.

Still, Wilder’s commercial leverage gives him an edge over more deserving contenders in the division who have been grinding hard and winning fights. His long 18-year pro career has given him plenty of opportunities to be seen by fans, and that should help when it comes to being picked by one of the current champions.

It’s still asking a lot of Wilder to defeat Bakole. If Bakole comes in near 300 lbs, his punching power could still take out Wilder if he lasts long enough to land something. Wilder’s advantage is that Bakole hasn’t looked good since beating Jared Anderson in 2024. If the ‘Bronze Bomber’ doesn’t take Bakole out early, he can forget about his dream of fighting for a world title.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Threatens to Smack Rayo Valenzuela in Leaked DMs After Walking Away From Zuffa
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela posted a screenshot of an Instagram message exchange between him and Shakur Stevenson on Tuesday, showing the bitterness on Rayo’s part after Shakur left Zuffa without accepting an offer to fight him.

Rayo (16-3, 10 KOs) had hoped to fight Shakur (25-0, 11 KOs) while they were briefly teammates, but Shakur rejected Zuffa’s offer.

Posting the exchange on X, Valenzuela captioned the image, “Saying everything but ‘let’s fight!'”

Valenzuela’s post comes after he was interviewed by Ring Magazine and called Shakur “weak” for leaving Zuffa Boxing instead of being a team player and agreeing to fight him in an in-house contest. Stevenson signed with Zuffa on July 9th of this year, but the two mutually parted ways three months later in October, with Stevenson failing to fight once while signed.

The comments from Valenzuela clearly bothered Shakur, causing him to slide into Valenzuela’s DMs.

“Say bh ass n* watch how loose you is with yo words, All that calling me a p*y st watch that.. Ion play them type of games,” said Shakur.

“Shut yo ass up and fight!” said Valenzuela.

“U a b*h, That’s why u clout chasing. I thought u was more solid then that, But look u using them disrespectful ass words stand on that st when u run into me!!” said Stevenson.

“You a b***h and ain’t nobody scared of you. We can fight next and settle it!” said Valenzuela.

“Just know I will smack the holy st out of u if u keep disrespecting me,” said Stevenson.

“I used to look at you and be like I’d beat tf outta dude!” said Valenzuela.

The interaction shows the bad blood between Rayo and Shakur from the brief period when they were both with Zuffa Boxing. It was a logical fight to make, but Shakur was aiming higher, wanting a bigger money fight. Being dismissed as inadequate has likely gotten on Valenzuela’s nerves because this is a fight that could have easily happened. Stevenson turned it down.

Stevenson would have been better off if he had taken it because he’s just been sitting inactive. At least he would have gotten the opportunity to be seen by fans while showing he’s a team player by fighting one of Zuffa’s fighters. Turki Alalshikh owns 60% of Zuffa, and it would have worked well for Stevenson’s career to fight one of his fighters instead of wasting time trying to get a fight with Devin Haney (31-0, 15 KOs) while insisting on a weight handicap.

In Valenzuela’s interview with Ring Magazine, he was critical of Shakur for trying to get a catchweight against Haney and Raymond Muratalla (24-0, 17 KOs), viewing that behavior as showing weakness.

Shakur is now a free agent and has a purse bid scheduled for November 30th for his mandatory defense against Muratalla. No one has signed Stevenson, and it may not be worth it if he’s going to price himself out and waste time trying to get weight advantages for fights.

Valenzuela is still with Zuffa Boxing and is in negotiations for a fight against WBA lightweight champion Floyd Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs). The two have a December 11th deadline before a purse bid is called.

If Stevenson wanted to smack Valenzuela, he had the perfect chance to do that when he was signed with Zuffa. They wanted the fight, but he turned it down and left the company.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa announces medical support, repatriation for Ghanaian domestic workers abroad
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, has announced that Ghana's diplomatic missions abroad have received consular approval to settle the medical bills of Ghanaian domestic workers who have been hospitalised, facilitate their discharge and arrange their return home.

He said the intervention forms part of measures to protect Ghanaian workers abroad as the government prepares to impose defined bans and restrictions.

In a post on Thursday, November 26, expressing gratitude to Ghanaians for their support and solidarity, Mr Ablakwa said the necessary approval had been granted to a considerable number of diplomatic missions to assist affected workers.

"May I, therefore, use this opportunity to announce that consular approval has been granted to a considerable number of our diplomatic missions to assist all Ghanaian domestic workers who have been hospitalised by resolving medical bills, facilitating their discharge and fully catering for their return home as Government prepares to impose defined bans and restrictions," he said.

The announcement comes amid growing concerns over the treatment and safety of Ghanaian domestic workers abroad, following the circulation of a viral video showing Ghanaian national Stephanie Nkrumah being physically assaulted by her employer in Iraq.

The government has formally protested to Iraqi authorities over the incident and is considering a moratorium on the recruitment of domestic workers to the country.

The Minister also addressed what he described as "false, vicious and puerile" allegations against him, expressing confidence that independent institutions investigating the matters would vindicate him.

He said he was deeply moved by the support he had received from Ghanaians both at home and abroad, adding that the country must remain united in protecting its image and the dignity of its citizens.

"I am enormously grateful and deeply moved by the show of support and solidarity from so many Ghanaians at home and abroad. God bless you all," he said.

Mr Ablakwa maintained that the allegations would not deter him from pursuing his responsibilities, insisting that the welfare and dignity of Ghanaians would remain a priority.

"I am absolutely confident that the independent institutions looking into these matters shall vindicate me," he said.

He added that the government would continue to defend Ghanaians wherever they found themselves, despite what he described as dishonest attempts to undermine those efforts.

The Minister also urged Ghanaians to respond to hostility with restraint, compassion, integrity and mutual respect.

"When they get nasty, we must demonstrate we are different by exhibiting more grace, composure, compassion, integrity and respect for each other," he stated.

He further expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama for his leadership and support, which he credited for the government's foreign policy achievements.

"I am eternally thankful to President John Mahama for his incredible leadership and unwavering support which have made all our foreign policy accomplishments possible," he added.

Ghana News.title: Okyenhene to honour Sir Sam Jonah for contributions to business and Okyeman
Ghana News.content:
Distinguished Ghanaian business leader and global statesman, Sir Sam Jonah, will be celebrated for his exceptional legacy of leadership, service to humanity and enduring contribution to Okyeman and Africa.

Osagyefuo Amoatia Ofori Panin, the Okyenhene, and the Okyeman Traditional Council will confer the distinguished honour of Okyeman Kanea Keseɛ, translated as the “Light of Okyeman”, on Sir Sam Jonah, on Saturday, 5 December 2026, at the Ofori Panin Fie in Kyebi.

The honour represents a profound recognition of a lifetime dedicated to enterprise, institutional development, education, mentorship and the advancement of Africa, as well as Sir Sam Jonah’s enduring relationship with Okyeman.

A royal of Assin Kushea and a distinguished son of the land of Okyeman, Sir Sam Jonah stands among Africa’s most accomplished business leaders. His remarkable journey from the mining industry to the highest levels of international corporate leadership has inspired generations of African entrepreneurs, professionals and emerging leaders.

As the former Chief Executive of Ashanti Goldfields Company, Sir Sam Jonah played an instrumental role in transforming a Ghanaian mining enterprise into a globally recognised corporation, demonstrating the capacity of African leadership to compete and excel on the international stage.

Beyond his corporate accomplishments, his commitment to education, mentorship and institution-building has helped shape a generation of leaders across Africa and beyond. His contributions to public discourse, good governance and the continent’s economic transformation continue to reflect his unwavering belief in Africa’s potential.

For Okyeman, however, the honour carries an even deeper significance. It celebrates a man whose relationship with the traditional kingdom has been characterised by loyalty, friendship, wise counsel and a genuine commitment to its progress.

The conferment reflects the Okyenhene’s vision of celebrating distinguished individuals whose lives and achievements embody the values of excellence, integrity, humility and selfless service, while providing enduring examples for future generations.

The symbolism of the Okyeman Kanea Keseɛ is particularly significant. In Akan tradition, light represents guidance, wisdom, hope and enlightenment. To be recognised as the Light of Okyeman is to be celebrated not merely for personal achievement, but for illuminating the path for others.

The ceremony will also underscore the enduring relevance of traditional institutions in recognising excellence, preserving societal values and inspiring leadership that transcends generations.

On 5 December, Okyeman will celebrate more than the extraordinary accomplishments of one of Africa’s most distinguished business figures. It will honour a legacy that demonstrates that the true measure of greatness lies not only in the heights one attains, but in the lives one transforms, the institutions one builds and the paths one illuminates for others.

For Sir Sam Jonah, the Okyeman Kanea Keseɛ will stand as an enduring testament to a life of purpose, distinction and service.

For Okyeman, it will be a celebration of a son whose light continues to shine far beyond its borders.

Ghana News.title: Calm returns to Nyanyano after gunshots; police deploy 50 officers
Ghana News.content:
Calm has returned to Gomoa Nyanyano in the Gomoa East District of the Central Region following sporadic gunshots that rocked the community on Wednesday night.

The Central Regional Police Command has deployed about 50 officers to the area, with an additional five patrol vehicles assigned to maintain security.

Adom FM's Kofi Adjei, who reported from the community on Joy FM's Middaynews on Thursday, November 26, said the patrol vehicles had been stationed at the District Police Command and the chief's palace.

Read also: VIDEO: Gunshots heighten tension at Nyanyano over chieftaincy dispute

He said the deployment followed reports that some agitated residents had attempted to attack the police station after the latest clashes.

The unrest is linked to a protracted chieftaincy dispute following the death of the late Nana Obeng Wiabor V, with rival factions laying claim to the stool.

The tensions have been heightened by disagreements over a planned homecoming celebration by traditional authorities, which some residents fear could deepen divisions and trigger further violence.

The latest disturbance follows the burning of an official vehicle belonging to the traditional authorities at the chief's palace on Tuesday, November 24.

The community has experienced previous violent confrontations over the chieftaincy dispute, including clashes in December 2025 and an attack on the palace in February 2026.

Police have increased their presence in the area to prevent further violence and maintain peace.

Ghana News.title: Cashew farmers appeal to government to suspend export ban over concerns about market capacity
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Cooperative Cashew Farmers and Marketing Association (GCCFMA) has appealed to the government for the temporary suspension of the Raw Cashew Nut (RCN) export window ban, citing severe operational and financial risks to over 200,000 cashew farmers across seven regions.

The appeal was made during a heavily attended press conference held today at the Wenchi Jubilee Park, which saw a massive turnout of cashew farmers, community leaders (Nananom), and association executives, including Vice President Daniel Tachie.

Commendation for Government's Industrialisation Drive

Speaking on behalf of the association, Secretary Sah Kofi Eric commended President Mahama and the Government of Ghana for their commitment to local value addition and domestic industrialisation within the cashew value chain.

The association particularly applauded the recent inauguration of the Nadkansco Cashew Processing Plant in Techiman, describing it as a significant milestone that holds immense promise for stabilising RCN prices and guaranteeing year-round domestic demand for farmers' produce.

Concerns Over Processing Capacity Gap

However, the association expressed deep concern over the immediate implications of enforcing the export window ban at this stage, referencing statistics shared by the President during the inaugural ceremony.

According to the figures, Ghana produces approximately 262,000 metric tonnes of RCN annually, yet only about 17,000 metric tonnes less than 10 percent is currently processed locally. Even with the addition of the Nadkansco facility's 30,000 metric tonne capacity alongside existing smaller factories, total domestic processing capacity remains well below a quarter of the nation's total RCN output.

Risks to Farmers and Value Chain

The GCCFMA outlined three major risks associated with enforcing a three-month export ban during the peak harvest season:

Withdrawal of Traders and Exporters: With export activities prohibited during the window, many traders, aggregators, and exporters will hesitate to purchase RCN due to the high cost of warehousing, capital lock-up, and weight/quality depreciation during prolonged storage, creating an immediate market glut.

Severe Liquidity Crisis for Farmers: Cashew farming is capital-intensive, and farmers rely on immediate harvest sales to fund critical operations including land clearing, nut picking, carting, and drying. Without active off-takers, farmers face acute financial distress.

Post-Harvest Losses and Quality Degradation: Smallholder farmers lack adequate warehousing facilities and standard jute sacks to safely store unsold RCN. If local processors cannot absorb the harvest and exporters step back, nuts will be stored under poor conditions, leading to moisture damage, poor out-turn quality, and heavy financial discounts for Ghanaian cashew on the international market.

Four Key Recommendations

In light of these realities, the association submitted four recommendations for government consideration:

Immediate Suspension of the Export Window Restriction: Lift the export restriction until domestic processing factories are sufficiently expanded and resourced to absorb at least 75 percent of Ghana's total annual RCN production. Broad-Based Stakeholder Engagement: Convene urgent, inclusive consultations involving farmers, aggregators, local processors, and exporters to align policy implementation with the practical realities of the industry. Establishment of an Alternative Market/Off-Take Mechanism: Put in place a structured buffer or guaranteed off-take arrangement to absorb excess RCN that local factories cannot purchase, ensuring farmer relief and sustained production growth. Targeted Farmer Support Interventions: Roll out practical interventions such as access to affordable jute sacks, community storage facilities, and input financing to cushion farmers against post-harvest challenges.

Commitment to Sector Transformation

The GCCFMA reaffirmed its commitment as a steadfast partner in advancing the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA) and Government's agenda to transform Ghana's cashew sector.

The association expressed confidence that Cashew Council Ghana will give the appeal the urgent attention it deserves and forward the plea to the Honourable Minister and the President for favourable consideration.

Ghana News.title: NHIA warns healthcare providers against illegal charges as it commissions new Wa office
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), Dr Victor Asare Bampoe, has formally commissioned a newly constructed National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) municipal office in Wa, using the occasion to issue a stern warning against healthcare providers who extort unauthorised fees from subscribers.

Addressing traditional leaders, health officials and residents at the ceremony in Wa, Dr Bampoe declared that the imposition of illegal charges remains one of the gravest threats to public confidence in the scheme.

He noted that the practice persists among some facilities despite regular claims disbursements and upward tariff adjustments.

"Let me state unequivocally: NHIS members must not be made to pay illegal fees for services to which they are entitled. This practice must stop," Dr Bampoe said.

While commending recent directives by the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service (GHS), the Christian Health Association of Ghana and private facility associations ordering staff to halt extortion, the NHIA Chief Executive stressed that administrative warnings must be backed by strict enforcement.

"However, directives alone are not enough. We expect full compliance," he warned. "The Authority has strengthened monitoring, investigates reported cases and will apply appropriate sanctions against providers found culpable, in accordance with applicable laws and accreditation requirements."

Dr Bampoe urged subscribers confronted with unauthorised charges to demand official receipts and report offenders to the nearest NHIS office or through the Authority's toll-free short code, 6447, on MTN and Telecel.

The modern office complex, built on land allocated by the Overlord of the Waala Traditional Area, Wa Naa Fuseini Pelpuo IV, was completed in July 2025 and furnished in September 2025, allowing staff to commence operations ahead of its formal commissioning.

Dr Bampoe expressed profound gratitude to the Wa Naa for facilitating the land acquisition and praised President John Dramani Mahama for uncapping the NHIA fund to boost resource inflows into the scheme.

He also acknowledged Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson, Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh and the NHIA Board, led by Mr Larry Adjetey, for supporting health infrastructure retooling, free primary healthcare and the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, popularly known as MahamaCares.

During the introduction of the Wa Municipal staff to the gathering, Dr Bampoe charged them to maintain the facility in pristine condition and expand membership. He promised to return within six months to assess their performance.

The Upper West Regional Director of the NHIA, Mr Rashid Mohammed Tindogo, revealed that the region continues to record strong universal health coverage indicators.

At the end of October 2026, active NHIS membership in the Upper West Region stood at 870,518, representing 85.6 per cent of the region's estimated population.

According to Mr Tindogo, 572,084 of those active subscribers, representing approximately 65 per cent, are vulnerable citizens registered free of charge. They include pupils under the Ghana School Feeding Programme, beneficiaries of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) programme and indigents.

He lauded Dr Bampoe for championing a 50 per cent increase in provider tariffs alongside prompt claims payments, as well as confronting illegal co-payments.

"Many leaders have come through the NHIA, but many never had the courage to tackle this canker of illegal payments," Mr Mohammed said. "As staff of the NHIS in the Upper West Region, we will make sure that there is zero tolerance for illegal payments."

Mr Tindogo noted that GHS facilities account for more than 85 per cent of accredited healthcare providers in the region and announced that the Regional Minister had scheduled a stakeholder engagement with all providers for December 3 to sustain compliance.

However, the Regional Director appealed to the NHIA leadership to address pressing operational challenges. He noted that only three of the region's 11 district offices currently operate from purpose-built NHIS structures, while the others occupy rented or unsuitable premises.

He also appealed for operational vehicles and motorbikes to support field registration and enable a rapid response to extortion complaints, particularly in areas without commercial transport services.

In his remarks, the Upper West Regional Minister, Charles Lwanga Puozuing, described the new facility as a tangible dividend of President Mahama's "resetting agenda" and expressed confidence that similar facilities would be replicated across the region's remaining 11 districts.

Mr Puozuing used the platform to make a passionate appeal to Dr Bampoe to prioritise the recruitment of young people from the region to staff the expanding NHIS network.

"If you build this edifice, or the target group is that we should get everybody registered under the scheme, we will need to have more persons employed to man the various districts and at various positions within the various districts," the Regional Minister stated.

"On behalf of the chiefs and people of the Upper West Region, and our teeming youth, young women and men, we are pleading that other opportunities be given to create jobs for our people across the various districts."

The Chairman of the occasion and Paramount Chief of the Busa Traditional Area in the Wa Municipality, Naa Ali Seidu Pelpuo Yelmaana, welcomed the delegation and reflected on how the decentralisation of NHIS offices has transformed healthcare access for ordinary citizens.

"We all know that the National Health Insurance Scheme is a very critical intervention of the government in the health sector. And initially, getting a card was very problematic," Naa Yelmaana observed.

"But with the proliferation of offices in the various regions, districts and municipalities, this has become a thing of the past."

Thanking the NHIA Chief Executive for personally travelling to Wa to inaugurate the building, the Paramount Chief added:

"Here in Wa today, we are adding one of the offices in the municipality. And so we are very grateful for the Chief Executive himself coming over to do us this favour."

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s 2027 budget: A New economic direction and what it means for the energy sector
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s 2027 Budget Statement, presented by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson under the theme “The New Economy: New Ghana, Jobs and Prosperity,” represents an important shift in the country's economic policy direction. Beyond the headline fiscal allocations and macroeconomic indicators, the Budget articulates a broader ambition: to transform Ghana from a predominantly commodity-dependent economy into a production-driven, industrialised and investment-oriented economy.

For the energy sector, this ambition is particularly significant. Energy is no longer simply a utility or an infrastructure requirement; it is increasingly recognised as a strategic economic enabler upon which industrialisation, manufacturing, mineral processing, agricultural transformation and the competitiveness of the private sector depend.

The central question, therefore, is whether Ghana can translate its improved macroeconomic conditions into a more reliable, affordable, diversified and financially sustainable energy system.

1. The US$10 Billion New Economy Programme: Energy at the Centre of Transformation

One of the most consequential announcements in the Budget is the US$10 billion New Economy Programme covering 2027–2030, with GH¢30 billion earmarked for implementation in 2027.

The programme identifies energy infrastructure as one of its eight strategic pillars. This is a significant recognition of the relationship between energy security and economic transformation.

The government's proposed investments include a 1,450MW state-owned thermal power plant, a 600MW solar power plant supported by 2,000MWh of battery storage, and US$500 million for transmission network modernisation.

The ambition is to increase generation capacity, strengthen grid reliability, reduce the cost of electricity and eliminate dependence on expensive emergency power plants by 2030.

This is potentially transformative. However, the success of the programme will depend not merely on installed generation capacity, but on the quality of project preparation, financing arrangements, fuel security, transmission readiness, distribution efficiency and the financial sustainability of the entire electricity value chain.

The private sector must also be positioned as a meaningful investment partner rather than merely a contractor to government.

2. The Power Sector: A New Opportunity for Energy Security and Industrial Competitiveness

The Budget acknowledges the structural challenges confronting Ghana's electricity sector, including high tariffs, distribution losses, weak revenue collection, fuel supply risks and accumulated financial obligations.

The reported annual energy sector shortfall of approximately US$1.4 billion in 2025, alongside arrears of approximately US$1.7 billion owed to Independent Power Producers and fuel suppliers, demonstrates the scale of the challenge.

The proposed generation investments are therefore important, but they must be accompanied by deeper structural reforms.

First, the 1,450MW thermal plant must be supported by a credible gas supply strategy. The Budget anticipates approximately 150 million standard cubic feet of additional gas daily from the Sankofa and Jubilee fields. This creates an important linkage between upstream petroleum production and downstream power generation.

Second, the 600MW solar project and associated battery storage present an opportunity to diversify Ghana's generation mix, improve peak-load management and strengthen grid stability.

Third, the proposed US$500 million investment in transmission infrastructure is critical. Generation without adequate transmission and distribution capacity will not deliver the expected economic benefits.

Perhaps most importantly, the ambition to reduce generation costs from approximately US$0.16/kWh to US$0.08/kWh or below could materially improve the competitiveness of Ghanaian industries.

For businesses operating in manufacturing, mining, agro-processing and other energy-intensive sectors, affordable electricity is a fundamental determinant of investment decisions.

The opportunity is substantial, but the implementation discipline must match the ambition.

3. The Downstream Petroleum Sector: From Import Dependency to Strategic Value Creation

The implications of the 2027 Budget for the downstream petroleum sector deserve particular attention.

Ghana's downstream petroleum market has evolved into a highly competitive environment characterised by multiple Bulk Distribution Companies, international oil trading companies, importers and petroleum service providers.

In this environment, the long-term competitiveness of the sector will depend on supply-chain efficiency, access to trade finance, storage infrastructure, product quality, logistics and the ability to manage international price and foreign exchange risks.

The New Economy Programme presents opportunities for the sector in several areas.

First, the expansion of industrial activity and the proposed 24-Hour Economy will increase demand for petroleum products, particularly in transportation, manufacturing, construction, mining and logistics.

Second, the transition towards cleaner energy creates opportunities for investments in biofuels, ethanol blending, sustainable aviation fuels, LNG, LPG infrastructure and other alternative fuels.

Third, the country's ambition to expand domestic production and value addition creates a compelling case for strengthening petroleum storage, distribution and strategic logistics infrastructure.

For BOST and other downstream sector institutions, the changing energy landscape presents an opportunity to evolve beyond traditional petroleum storage and distribution towards integrated energy logistics, cleaner fuels and strategic infrastructure development.

However, this transition must be commercially viable. Investments in alternative fuels, renewable energy and low-carbon infrastructure must be supported by credible demand assessments, bankable business models, appropriate regulation and sustainable financing structures.

The downstream sector must increasingly become an enabler of Ghana's broader energy transition rather than remain exclusively focused on conventional petroleum supply.

4. The Upstream Petroleum Sector: Unlocking Domestic Resources and Strengthening Energy Security

The Budget's proposed reliance on additional gas from the Sankofa and Jubilee fields to support the new thermal generation capacity reinforces the strategic importance of Ghana's upstream petroleum industry.

This creates an opportunity to strengthen the link between domestic hydrocarbon production and national economic development.

Ghana's upstream sector must increasingly be evaluated not only by crude oil production and export receipts but also by its contribution to domestic gas availability, power generation, industrial feedstock and the development of local capabilities.

The proposed increase in gas requirements for thermal generation will require sustained investment in production, processing, transportation and gas infrastructure.

It also raises important questions around the reliability of domestic gas supply, contractual commitments, pricing, infrastructure constraints and the coordination of upstream production with downstream demand.

Furthermore, the long-term sustainability of Ghana's upstream petroleum industry will depend on attracting new investment, improving operational efficiency, strengthening local participation and maintaining a competitive regulatory environment.

The challenge is to maximise the economic value of existing petroleum resources while ensuring that the country is adequately prepared for the gradual transition towards lower-carbon energy systems.

My Two Pesewas

Ghana's 2027 Budget offers an opportunity to make energy a catalyst for industrialisation, investment and economic competitiveness. Achieving this requires an integrated energy strategy that strengthens the power sector, maximises domestic petroleum resources and accelerates investment in renewable energy and alternative fuels.

The priority now must be execution: bankable projects, secured financing, clear timelines, stronger institutional accountability, improved sector efficiency and meaningful private-sector participation.

Ultimately, Ghana must move from policy ambition to measurable delivery. The success of the Budget will be judged not by the announcements made, but by the energy security, investment, jobs and economic value we create. Getting the energy equation right is fundamental to our national prosperity.

Ghana News.title: KNUST professor urges graduates to look beyond certificates and develop critical thinking
Ghana News.content:
A Professor of Educational Innovations in Science and Technology at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Eric Appau Asante, has urged young people to look beyond academic qualifications and develop critical thinking, adaptability and problem-solving skills to remain relevant in a rapidly changing world.

He says the traditional education system places excessive emphasis on examinations, grades and certificates, often at the expense of practical skills needed to navigate unfamiliar situations.

Prof. Appau Asante is therefore calling on educational institutions to prioritise creativity, independent thinking and problem-solving rather than relying heavily on rote learning and examination performance.

He made the remarks while speaking on the theme, “Pangolin: Architects of an Impenetrable Future,” at a TEDxKNUST event at the university.

The event used the pangolin as a metaphor for resilience and survival. The animal's protective scales help defend it against predators but also make it vulnerable to human poachers.

Prof. Appau Asante said the pangolin's survival mechanism offered an important lesson about the limitations of relying solely on protection instead of developing the capacity to adapt.

“Protection is not the same as preparation. And survival is not the same as progress,” he said.

He argued that education should prepare learners for a world where problems do not come with predetermined questions or guaranteed pathways to success.

The professor also questioned the value of academic qualifications when graduates lack the practical ability to apply their knowledge to unfamiliar situations.

“If your certificate disappeared tomorrow, what would remain of your education?” he asked.

On artificial intelligence (AI), Prof. Appau Asante encouraged young people to embrace emerging technologies but warned against becoming so dependent on them that they lose the ability to think independently.

He acknowledged that AI tools could improve productivity and make information more accessible but said their growing capabilities raised concerns about people's willingness to exercise critical thinking and sound judgment.

“The danger is that human beings may become less willing to think because machines have made thinking appear optional,” he said.

“Experiment with AI and develop competence in its use, while retaining responsibility for their decisions and the consequences of applying technology. Let machines accelerate your work. Do not allow them to replace your thinking,” he advised.

He further challenged graduates to measure the value of their education by their contributions to society rather than the qualifications they acquire.

According to him, Africa needs graduates who can identify weaknesses in existing systems, develop solutions to societal challenges and create innovations that respond to people's actual needs.

Also speaking at the event, Ghanaian entrepreneur and value chain leader Victoria Afua Agbai said limited early exposure to technology in Ghana makes it important for young people to take deliberate steps to develop their skills and remain competitive.

She observed that artificial intelligence and machine learning have significantly changed the world of work, making some of the career pathways young people previously prepared for less relevant.

“The world of work has changed, and the future many of us prepared for no longer exists. AI and machine learning have changed everything,” she said.

Ms Agbai encouraged young people to pursue internships, volunteer opportunities and other forms of practical work experience to improve their exposure to technology and workplace demands.

“Our environment exposes us less to technology at an early age, so I would encourage young people to volunteer their services to companies, seek internships, and explore other opportunities to gain practical experience,” she said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
