World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Is UBI the solution to mass unemployment in an AI economy?
World.content:
AI’s rapid advance has fueled calls for universal payments to prevent poverty and wealth inequality.

Share Is UBI the solution to mass unemployment in an AI economy? on social media

As rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI) raise fears of mass job losses, calls for the rollout of universal basic income (UBI) are gaining traction.

UBI is a regular cash payment made to every citizen regardless of employment status, income or wealth.

Proponents of UBI in the United States argue that governments should look to UBI to offset AI’s expected impact on the labour market and prevent extreme poverty and wealth inequality.

Here is what we know:

When did the concept of UBI begin?

The idea of universal payments is not new.

In 1797, Thomas Paine, one of the key thinkers of the American Revolution, proposed an early version of UBI in a pamphlet titled Agrarian Justice. He argued that land was originally common property, shared by all of humanity. Those with no land, he said, were owed compensation as a basic human right.

Under Paine’s proposal, each person would have received a lump sum of 15 pounds when they turned 21, followed by an annual payment of 10 pounds from age 50, paid for by a tax on inherited property.

The idea resurfaced in the 1960s from opposing ends of the ideological spectrum.

US economist Milton Friedman proposed a “negative income tax”, under which the government would top up the earnings of anyone falling below a set threshold. Friedman, a champion of free-market policies, argued that his proposal would be cheaper than existing welfare programmes.

US civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr, in his 1967 book Where Do We Go from Here, called for a guaranteed income as a way to end poverty.



King Jr’s vision came close to being enshrined in law in 1969, when President Richard Nixon proposed the Family Assistance Plan, a minimum income for families with children. Nixon’s proposal passed the House of Representatives but stalled in the Senate, and the plan was eventually abandoned.

After falling out of fashion in subsequent decades, proposals for universal payments have re-entered the mainstream in recent years amid the rise of automation and AI.

Who is backing UBI?

Some of the loudest proponents of UBI are the people developing AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has been pushing the idea for years.

In a 2024 interview with the All-In Podcast, Altman proposed a twist on UBI that would give everyone a stake in the productive gains of AI.

“I wonder if the future looks something like more like universal basic compute than universal basic income and everybody gets like a slice of GPT 7’s compute and they can use it, they can resell it, they can donate it to somebody to use for cancer research,” Altman said, suggesting that citizens could “own part of the productivity” generated by AI instead of receiving cash.

In April, SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said in an X post that a government-distributed “Universal High Income” would be the best way to deal with large-scale unemployment caused by AI.

Musk said AI and robotics would produce an abundance of goods and services far in excess of the increase in the money supply in future, so there would not be inflation.

Some observers have questioned the motivations of such proposals from billionaire tech executives.

Jonathan Portes, a professor of economics and public policy at King’s College, London, said tech leaders promoting UBI are acting out of “perceived self-interest”. In his view, a basic income could make job losses easier to accept as people are more likely to tolerate AI replacing their work if they are being paid.



“Partly it’s just another cool sounding idea,” Portes told Al Jazeera. “We should not take these people seriously on public policy issues at all.”

Who would pay for UBI, and how is it different from social welfare?

Most UBI proposals envision a system paid for by taxes, much in the same way as existing welfare programmes, though some pilot schemes have been funded by private donations.



Unlike traditional social welfare, which typically requires applicants to demonstrate financial hardship, UBI is paid to every member of a population without conditions.

Portes said UBI high enough to support acceptable living standards is not likely to be economically or politically viable in the near future.

While “a realistic UBI could help provide a better level of protection, increase individual autonomy and increase labour market flexibility, getting there would be complex”, he added.

“Many of the claims for it and fears are grossly exaggerated,” Portes said.

So who would benefit from UBI?

While everyone would get some financial benefit, some economists and technologists argue that the biggest beneficiary could be the economy.

In a scenario where AI leads to mass layoffs, people will have less money to spend. From this perspective, UBI would function less as a form of charity than as a way to keep consumer spending going.

That is the case made by Martin Ford, a futurist and the author of Rise of the Robots.

Ford argues that jobs are how purchasing power reaches common consumers, viewing UBI as a way to repair the link between production and spending rather than redistributing wealth for its own sake.

“Jobs are that mechanism that gets purchasing power to consumers so they can then drive the economy,” Ford said in a 2017 TED Talk.

“If, in fact, that mechanism begins to erode in the future, then we’re going to need to replace it with something else, or we’re going to face the risk that our whole system simply may not be sustainable.”

What are the arguments against UBI?

The most common objection is that unconditional cash discourages work. The evidence suggests the effect is real but modest.

In the biggest US trial of its kind, about 1,000 low-income participants were given $1,000 a month for three years.

OpenResearch’s Unconditional Cash Study, backed by OpenAI’s Altman, found that participants worked only 1.3-1.4 hours less each week compared with the control group.

More than half of recipients’ increased spending went on basic necessities such as food, housing and transport.

The study found no significant effect on physical health, and gains in wellbeing faded after the first year.

Another objection is cost.

In the US, paying each family of four a universal payment of $30,000 – slightly below the official poverty line – would cost approximately $8.5 trillion each year, according to the Tax Project Institute.

That would dwarf current levels of spending on welfare.

The US government spent $1.7 trillion on some 90 welfare programmes in 2025, according to the conservative Heritage Foundation.

World.title: Film shows testimonies of international doctors amid Gaza genocide
World.content:
NewsFeed Film shows testimonies of international doctors amid Gaza genocide

“It is an entire archive of evidence that must be presented in the courts of the world.” Al Jazeera interviewed the team behind a documentary showcasing first-hand collective footage, from international doctors who bore witness to the collapse of the healthcare system in Gaza.

World.title: Eyewitnesses describe scenes of Egypt’s deadly vehicle fire
World.content:
NewsFeed Eyewitnesses describe scenes of Egypt’s deadly vehicle fire

Scenes in the aftermath of a deadly fire in Egypt show crowds gathered around charred vehicles, firefighters, and ambulances. Eyewitnesses describe the chaos that erupted during the fire which killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others.

World.title: FIFA says personal and business information stolen in cyberattack
World.content:
No files from the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed, according to media reports.

Share FIFA says personal and business information stolen in cyberattack on social media

FIFA said it had been the victim of a criminal cyberattack that gave unauthorised access to personal and business information, although no files from the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed, according to media reports.

FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Al Jazeera.

FIFA strongly condemned the “unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data,” adding that such actions were “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”.

It also said that :”FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.”

FIFA did not say how many people or organisations were affected, when the attack took place or what the business information included. Its reference to publication did not say whether any data had appeared online, or where.

Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were FIFA files. Three days later, it appeared to take credit for the hack when responding to a post that said more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.

The person with knowledge of the matter told the Reuters news agency that less than 0.1 percent of the total data held by world football’s governing body was affected.

A FIFA source told The Athletic that the person – or group – responsible for carrying out the cyberattack gained access by impersonating staff rather than a systems or technical failure.



FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in July that his organisation had scrapped plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors following a widespread backlash.

The plan ‌involved raising up to $4.2bn by selling a 20 percent stake in a new unit that would run FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

World.title: With the rise of AI, are we close to having universal basic income
World.content: AI’s rapid advance has led to calls for a solution to prevent poverty and wealth inequality. But is the solution giving people universal basic income just for existing? Al Jazeera’s Yasmeen ElTahan explains.

World.title: ‘Symbolic’: Why did UK sanction Yemen’s Houthis amid attacks on Saudi?
World.content:
UK sanctions Iran-backed group and its leaders, accusing them of undermining stability in the Middle East.

Share ‘Symbolic’: Why did UK sanction Yemen’s Houthis amid attacks on Saudi? on social media

London, United Kingdom – The United Kingdom has slapped sanctions on Yemen’s Houthis and four of their senior leaders after accusing the Iran-backed group of renewed “aggression” inside Yemen and attacks targeting civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis have escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting the financial district in Riyadh this week, as they engage in a civil war with Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

Fighting has escalated since July as a 2022 United Nations-brokered ceasefire collapsed. Since then, the Houthis have captured the Red Sea port of Mocha and the island of Mayyun, extending control over the Red Sea in a setback to the Saudi-backed government.

The war erupted after the Houthis captured the capital, Sanaa, in late 2014, forcing President Abd Rabbu Mansour Hadi to flee. Saudi Arabia intervened in support of the Hadi government as it saw the Iran-backed group’s rise in neighbouring Yemen as a security threat.

The UK government announced its sanctions on Tuesday, accusing the Houthis of undermining peace and security in Yemen and the region. It froze assets and placed travel bans on the group and its leaders, including Interior Minister Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi and Security and Intelligence chief Abdul Hakim Hashem Ali al-Khaiwani.

Chief prosecutor Sarim al-Din Mufadal, who has been accused of perpetrating “sexual violence, including rape and torture”, also faces an asset freeze and travel ban.

UK’s interests in the Middle East

“The Houthis’ renewed aggression targeting our partners and innocent civilians is unacceptable, and they must be held to account,” said UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who linked the sanctions to attacks on shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb strait in the Red Sea, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world.



“Today’s measures send a clear message to the Houthis – we will always act in support of British values and interests,” he said in a statement.

The British move comes nearly a month after it decided to deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia, a close ally going back decades that has increasingly come under missile and drone attacks in recent weeks.

Britain also sent Tornado fighters to Saudi Arabia in the wake of the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait in 1990, according to the Royal Air Force Museum.

The Houthis have also targeted oil installations and a major pipeline that helped Saudi Arabia export its oil while Iran essentially blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a global oil chokepoint. Tehran said it has blocked the vital waterway, through which most of the Gulf oil and natural gas passes, in response to the US-Israel war on Iran.

The UK has naval and logistics bases in the neighbouring Gulf nations of Bahrain and Oman. In May, it agreed a free trade deal with the six Gulf Cooperation Council states.

‘To turn the screw on the Houthis’

Thomas Juneau, an associate fellow with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, said the sanctions were imposed during a diplomatic push by Riyadh.

“Saudi Arabia has been asking other countries to list the Houthis as a terrorist entity, to turn the screw on the Houthis and to help in its campaign against the group,” he told Al Jazeera.

The sanctions, Ahmed Nagi from the International Crisis Group (ICG) said, are “intended to send a political message about where the UK stands on the current escalation and the Houthi actions”.

In January 2024, the UK and the United States jointly sanctioned four Houthi figures, including the group’s defence minister and naval commander, over attacks on Red Sea shipping, and a month later, a second package targeted the Quds Force, the overseas unit of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

The same month, the UK joined the US in carrying out air strikes on Houthi positions over attacks on ships in the Red Sea, which had disrupted maritime trade. The Houthis had imposed a ban on ships linked to Israel from passing through the waterway in response to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

The Houthis are already under a UN arms embargo, and London is now “going further”, Nagi, who is a senior Yemen analyst at the ICG, said.

This month, the UN Security Council renewed its Yemen sanctions regime until November 2027 through a UK-led resolution.

Raiman al-Hamdani, a Yemeni researcher and analyst, said the UK, as the Security Council’s lead on Yemen, had helped shape that regime and “this latest step continues a longstanding policy rather than breaking from it.”

‘Largely symbolic’

But Nagi called the UK move “largely symbolic”.



“The four Houthi leaders targeted by the sanctions are unlikely to travel to the UK or hold assets there, so the practical impact will probably be limited.”

Al-Hamdani said the group’s income comes “largely from the black market, smuggling, taxation of local businesses and control of ports and customs, none of which a UK asset freeze touches”.

“The missile and drone programme hasn’t slowed despite years of UN, US, EU and UK listings,” he added.

Juneau from Chatham House agreed the sanctions would not change Houthi behaviour soon but said that while sanctions by individual countries other than the US have little effect alone, they can matter collectively, which is why Saudi Arabia is pressing as many countries as possible to act.

He also pointed to the Houthis’ growing influence in the Red Sea, which has concerned Saudi Arabia as well as its Western allies.

The British foreign secretary on Tuesday pointed out how Houthi actions in the Red Sea were “driving up the cost of living for the British people” and “undermining the stability of the Middle East”.

Analysts pointed out that the UK government statement is silent on the other parties to the war – the Yemeni government forces and Saudi Arabia – even as it said the Houthis’ “reckless aggression is responsible for this conflict”.

Nagi said the omission reflected how London sees the war.

“From London’s perspective, the Houthis are the ones attacking Saudi Arabia and escalating the conflict, rather than the other way around,” he said.

Juneau was blunter. “Sanctions are always political. You sanction your opponents. You don’t sanction your partners or friends,” he said.

Humanitarian concerns

Niku Jafarnia, a Yemen researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressed concerns that the sanctions would impact aid organisations engaged in humanitarian work in Houthi-held areas.

“As Yemen relies heavily on imports, curbs affecting commercial goods could also push up food prices,” she told Al Jazeera.

“The sanctions really can have quite devastating impacts for the populations living in territories under Houthi control, even if that’s not what the UK intends by the sanctions,” she warned.

This is the case even though the UK’s sanctions already include a humanitarian exception covering aid and other activities that meet basic human needs, she said.

Moreover, the UK has not proscribed the Houthis under “antiterrorism” laws despite its other Western allies – the US, Canada and Australia – designating the Iran-backed group as a “terrorist” organisation.

Juneau called the aid agencies’ fear that proscription could hamper humanitarian deliveries “a valid concern” although some people argued the Houthis’ diversion of aid has already made such work extremely difficult.

The Houthis have repeatedly denied that they have diverted humanitarian aid.

Al-Hamdani said sanctions have not forced the Houthis to change their tactics. They do not “appear to respond to human rights criticism or listings”, he said, adding that the group “tends to treat detainees and abuses as bargaining chips to strengthen its negotiating position and demands”.



Rather, he said, sanctions “risk deepening polarisation and closing off the political settlement the war needs”.

World.title: James ‘Fergie’ Chambers: US trying to cast ‘antiwar ideas as extremist’
World.content:
The recently bailed activist denies US accusations of supporting Hamas, claiming he is being targeted for supporting Palestine.

Share James ‘Fergie’ Chambers: US trying to cast ‘antiwar ideas as extremist’ on social media

Madrid, Spain – James “Fergie” Chambers, a pro-Palestine philanthropist who is the subject of an ongoing extradition request by the United States government, said he believed the US is targeting supporters of the people of Gaza worldwide.

The US government’s case centres on Chambers’s alleged laundering of $7.5m, which he is said to have wired several years ago from a US bank account to Tunisia, where he lived at the time, allegedly using the cash to support Hamas.

He is not charged with any “terrorism” offences and denies any wrongdoing.

Chambers, a self-proclaimed Marxist-Leninist and the heir to the Cox Enterprises media fortune, believes supporters of the Palestinian cause are being targeted around the globe.

“I think that when the neocolonial system starts to break apart economically, militarily, which I believe is happening, it becomes desperate. And when it becomes desperate, it becomes more violent and more violent,” he told Al Jazeera.

“And all these things sort of converge around the occupation of Palestine because we understand the occupation of Palestine as basically nothing more than an expression of US military and business interest. So that is the focal point of repression.”

He added: “In relation to the Palestinian cause and other causes, I think there is a kind of effort certainly in the US to designate [expressing] antiwar ideas as extremist and terrorist.”

‘They haven’t accused me of sending money to Hamas’

Chambers, who was released from prison in Madrid on bail last week after serving four months on remand, said he was being targeted by the US because of his support for the Palestinian cause.



“I’m not even accused of sending money anywhere illegal. I’m accused of wanting to, which is sort of a crazy distinction to me. They haven’t accused me of sending money to Hamas, no. They’ve accused me of wanting to send money to Hamas,” he said.

A keen football fan, he said he transferred the money to Club Africain, a Tunisian football team, which he sponsors.

He said he had met someone from the Iranian embassy in Tunisia at an international book fair in 2023.

“[They] tied in a narrative which says that … I allegedly visited the Iranian diplomats, which is not true. I met someone from the Iranian embassy at an international book fair, who told me that US citizens are allowed to have tourist visas. I never met an official at the embassy. I never went into the offices at the embassy.”

The 41-year-old said a forensic accountant had presented Club Africain’s accounts to the Madrid court.

As part of a deal in which his family cut ties with him at the time, he sold stock back to his family worth about $250m in mid-2023.

“I’m assuming the implication is that I would have met with these people and then transferred money to Tunisia to a football club with the intention of then laundering it to Hamas.”

The US Department of Justice said it did not want to comment when contacted by Al Jazeera.

Chambers said he was “very publicly” affiliated with the club, which won the Tunisian championship this year, and he made a four-year sponsorship deal.

“They had millions of euros worth of debt, which is why they contacted me to get involved. And the money was used to pay off debts, to revamp the team facilities, training facilities, youth programmes, pay overdue salaries. And then in return I had some involvement in management,” he said.

Chambers also said Tunisia was a “closed economy”.

“When you move money into Tunisia, you’re not allowed to move it out,” he said, adding that one of his “most constant emotions in all of this is just downright confusion”.

Chambers, who has given financial aid to 100 projects in 20 countries, including some in Palestine, said he was always careful to obey the law.

“There is no smoking gun. There’s no unloaded gun. There’s nowhere that I said I wanted to support any illegal groups,” he said.

Chambers said he was a target for supporting the Palestinian cause.

“I think the combination of an overall effort by the US authorities to criminalise basically the Palestinian cause in any capacity … this is a part of that,” he said. “You know the fact that I happen to have a lot of resources. And I speak out unapologetically and freely about my positions on US imperialism. These things just combined to make me a target and an example.”



Prison staff ‘saw me as being somebody who shouldn’t be there’

The father-of-four, who has been reunited with his family after being released on bail, is awaiting the court’s decision. His case has also drawn attention to concerns about the implications of the US extradition request.

During his time in jail, he said he received letters of support from many strangers as well as political parties from all sides.

“Even within the prison staff, there was a kind of consensus that people saw me as being somebody who shouldn’t be there,” he said.

However, he said he faces an uncertain future.

“I still don’t know … whether I am going to face decades of my life in a federal penitentiary in the US,” he said.

The High Court said it had decided to release Chambers after US authorities acknowledged what they described as substantial and unintentional errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent’s sworn statement, submitted in support of the extradition request. The proceedings have been the subject of further reporting on the extradition case in Spain.

Chambers was arrested on an Interpol Red Notice in Ibiza in July, but has since applied for asylum in Spain.

He cannot be extradited until the asylum claim is resolved, and if it is successful, he cannot be extradited from Spain to the US at all.

World.title: LeBron James becomes oldest NBA player to post triple-double as 76ers win
World.content:
Share LeBron James becomes oldest NBA player to post triple-double as 76ers win on social media

LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over the Miami Heat in the NBA Cup on Wednesday.

Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player James, who turns 42 on December 30, scored a season-high 25 points, passed off a season-high 12 assists and pulled down 10 rebounds to break his own triple-double age mark.

“Father Time always wins, but right now he’s giving Father Time hell,” Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said.

Miami grabbed a 32-29 lead after the first quarter, but James scored 14 consecutive Sixers points in a second-quarter run for a 62-53 half-time lead, and the hosts never lost the edge in the second half.

“We wanted to get back to our defensive identity,” James said. “We didn’t do that in the first quarter, but for the next 36 minutes I thought we got back to that.”

The 76ers improved the best record in the Eastern Conference to 15-4 while snapping a seven-game win streak for Miami (10-7).

Both clubs are 2-1 atop Cup East Group B, but with a win, Miami would have clinched the group and advanced to the knockout stage of the in-season tournament.

With Joel Embiid out due to illness and Jaylen Brown out after early left hamstring tightness, it fell to James to score and set up his teammates.

“That’s my favourite aspect of my game besides my IQ,” James said.

“To be able to go out there and just play like a quarterback role and watch these guys run the right routes, and it’s my job to put it on time and on target, it was fun.”

Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 30 points while VJ Edgecombe added 18.



“These are my young bulls right here,” James said. “They keep me going. They keep me energised.”

Giannis Antetokounmpo led Miami with 32 points and 14 rebounds.

James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the off-season and selected the 76ers from several clubs in hopes of capturing a fifth NBA crown.

Mavericks win group

The idle Dallas Mavericks became the first team to reach the Cup knockout round, clinching the West Group A title when the Phoenix Suns lost 116-104 at Houston.

Alperen Sengun had a triple-double with 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists for Houston, while Kevin Durant added 20 points and Devin Booker led Phoenix with 25.

At Portland, Deni Avdija scored 33 points, and Damian Lillard added 29 to lead the host Trail Blazers over San Antonio 116-111, leaving West Group C deadlocked with the Spurs, Lakers, Portland and Golden State atop it at 2-1.

“It showed our maturity,” Lillard said. “We won a tough one.”

French star Victor Wembanyama scored 44 points and grabbed 16 rebounds to lead the Spurs, who fell to 15-4 after their first road loss of the season.

Jalen Brunson and Mikal Bridges each scored 19 points as the defending NBA and NBA Cup champion New York Knicks beat visiting Cleveland 121-102 for their sixth consecutive victory.

Karl-Anthony Towns had 12 points and 10 rebounds, and Jose Alvarado scored 21 off the bench for New York. Donovan Mitchell scored 30 points, and James Harden added 28 for the Cavaliers.

Minnesota’s Jaden McDaniels scored 32 points and grabbed 10 rebounds to lead the Timberwolves in a 113-106 victory at Oklahoma City.

Minnesota’s LaMelo Ball had 19 points, eight assists and seven rebounds but left the game late with a left ankle injury.

Two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led Oklahoma City with 32 points.

Julius Randle scored 28 points to lead Brooklyn’s 104-97 victory at Milwaukee, the Nets snapping a five-game losing skid.

Jaylen Wells scored 19 points to lead Memphis’ 115-97 home victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.

Golden State’s De’Anthony Melton scored 24 points to lead the Warriors over visiting Sacramento 129-110.

Matas Buzelis scored 24 points to lead Chicago over host Charlotte 107-105 as the Hornets’ losing skid reached six games.

World.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
World.content:
A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

The managing director, Marvin Reuter, is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

His equipment is suspected of being linked to two fatal accidents, in which four men died.

We confronted the 35-year-old at his business near Dortmund, but he would not answer our questions. He said he was reporting us to the police.

Reuter cannot be formally charged until extradited to France but could face jail time, if tried and convicted. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

The BBC - alongside German broadcasters WDR and NDR, newspaper SÃ¼ddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) - and France's Le Monde newspaper - has obtained and reviewed hundreds of police, court and tax documents about the case. We have blurred images of Reuter because of German privacy rules.

Investigators, we have learned, believe they have uncovered clear, persistent links between Reuter and smuggling networks.

Evidence has been gathered through the confessions of alleged accomplices and covert jail-cell recordings of an alleged gang chief - as well as the two deadly crossing attempts.

World.title: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
World.content:
Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.

The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.

Myanmar denied committing genocide, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. It is the first state to have been found in violation of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Min Aung Hlaing said "the term 'genocide' had seriously affected the country's reputation", state media report.

"Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," the country's coup leader-turned-president said at a meeting on Wednesday, according to state media.

The statement did not specify which parts of the ruling the country objects to.

The genocide case, brought by The Gambia in 2019, centred around so-called "clearance operations" initiated in 2017 in Rakhine State, where many of the Rohingya Muslim minority resided.

The ICJ determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed during the operation, while more than 700,000 are thought to have fled to Bangladesh by foot or by sea. The court found that approximately 815,000 had been targeted in some way.

The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world.

The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

The ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

The ICJ ordered Myanmar to pay proportionate reparations, but said an exact figure should be determined at a later date.

The court also ordered Myanmar to stop ongoing violations and immediately investigate those suspected of breaking the Convention.

But the ICJ does not have the power to enforce these demands. Instead it has to rely on the UN Security Council and political pressure to make its rulings stick.

While the ruling was largely symbolic, it was welcomed by Rohingya communities and human rights groups who have long called attention to the suffering faced by the Rohingya.

More than a dozen countries have acknowledged the ICJ ruling, and the UK has announced sanctions on several senior Myanmar military leaders.

Myanmar has been devastated by civil war since Min Aung Hlaing led a military coup to oust civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. The move turned Myanmar into an international pariah, and its military regime has faced sweeping international sanctions.

Since then, Min Aung Hlaing has been trying to reintegrate Myanmar into the international community, but it remains largely shut out of key diplomatic arenas.

World.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
World.content:
Taraneh Rahimi is on death row in Iran.

In recent weeks, the 21-year-old has been unable to walk properly after her legs were beaten, and an ear-infection caused by an untreated head injury has affected her balance, her cousin says.

She is "keeping her spirits up" but "there are days she breaks down in tears," Masoud Nourmohammadi tells BBC News Persian.

He says Taraneh and her twin sister Romina were arrested after joining the anti-government protests that swept the country in January.

When the twins' mother first saw them in prison, their faces were so swollen and bruised, and their hair pulled out, that she could only recognise them by their voices, Nourmohammadi says, speaking from the US.

He says Taraneh signed a confession after interrogators threatened that her sister would be raped in front of her.

Taraneh is one of six women who have been sentenced to death this year in connection with the January protests, according to the UN's human rights rapporteur for Iran, Mai Sato.

The figure for men is much higher. However, women protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, as part of a "horrific rise" in politically motivated executions, Amnesty International's Iran researcher Raha Bahreini says.

World.title: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes sinks near Ibiza, killing one
World.content:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has sunk off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

The Med Emre sank 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.

The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.

World.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
World.content:
Lenacapavir works by targeting the protective protein shell of HIV, disrupting the virus's ability to multiply and establish an infection in the body.

In a landmark clinical trial involving more than 5,000 adolescent girls and young women in Uganda and South Africa in 2024, none of those who received the injection contracted HIV.

Health experts say the injection offers a major advantage over existing HIV prevention pills, known as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which must be taken every day and can carry social stigma.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommended the drug for HIV prevention in July 2025.

The Global Fund described the arrival of the drug in Africa as a "major breakthrough" in the fight against HIV, saying cheaper supplies would help reach millions more people at risk of infection.

"These deliveries mark an unprecedented acceleration and expansion in access to a highly effective, quality-assured generic HIV prevention medicine in low- and middle-income settings," the group said in a statement on Wednesday.

More than 189,000 people across 10 countries have already received their first injection of lenacapavir, according to the Global Fund.

The organisation expects 24 countries to have received supplies by the end of this year and, working with the US government, plans to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028.

It is eventually expected to be available in 120 low- and middle-income countries.

Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for nearly two-thirds of people living with HIV globally, with adolescent girls and young women disproportionately affected.

South Africa has the world's largest HIV-positive population, with nearly eight million people living with the virus. It is among the countries expected to receive the cheaper injection.

Some 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV last year, while 570,000 died from HIV-related illnesses, according to the WHO.

The rollout comes amid concerns that sweeping cuts to US foreign aid under President Donald Trump's administration could undermine decades of progress in tackling HIV in Africa, where many countries rely heavily on international funding for prevention and treatment.

The UN aims to end Aids as a public health threat by 2030.

World.title: Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65
World.content:
Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.

Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.

Le Bon and his bandmates paid tribute, saying "he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music", while Sir Rod remembered his "dear pal" and Spandau Ballet's Kemp called him "a great player who set the tone for the 80s".

Taylor's wife Tracey called him "the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day." He died after "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", Duran Duran said in a statement on Wednesday.

World.title: Seven injured, four critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
World.content:
A alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed that the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the area.

Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

The city-run Erawan Emergency Medical Centre said it was treating four "red" cases and three "yellow" - less severe - cases.

On a visit to the scene, Thailand's energy minister Akanat Promphan said it appeared the impact of the explosion was limited because the fire started in a distillation tower about 100m (330ft) from where oil was being stored.

He said the incident was concerning as the refinery was in a residential area and the government was suspending production until it could be confident that operations would resume without any issues.

Bangchak Corporation said air quality monitoring in the immediate area around the refinery was within normal ranges.

It confirmed that production at the site, which can process up to 120,000 barrels of oil a day had been shut down. The company has a second refinery in Chonburi province, about 50 miles (80km) from Bangkok, handling a daily capacity of about 180,000 barrels.

An explosion occurred at the Bangkok refinery in July 2012, sparking a fire but no reported injuries.

World.title: Court dismisses ex-Minister Saleh Mamman’s application to quash N31.07bn fraud charge
World.content:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court on Thursday dismissed an application by former Minister of Power Saleh Mamman to quash a nine-count fraud and forgery charge brought against him over the alleged diversion of N31.07 billion meant for the Mambilla and Zungeru hydroelectric power projects.

Mr Mamman had asked the court to discharge and acquit him following his conviction by the Federal High Court in May.

He argued that the ingredients of the offences in the charge on which he was convicted were the same as those in the charge filed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) at the FCT High Court.

He filed the application under Section 36(9) of the Constitution, which protects individuals from being tried or punished twice for the same offence.

However, the trial judge, Maryann Anenih, ruled that the application lacked merit, holding that the offences in the two cases were different.

The judge noted that Mr Mamman was convicted of money laundering at the Federal High Court, while the charges before the FCT High Court relate to obtaining money by false pretence and forgery.

Although both cases arose from the Mambilla and Zungeru hydroelectric power projects, the offences were distinct, she ruled.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She consequently dismissed the application and ordered that the trial of Mr Mamman and seven other defendants continue.

“The first defendant’s applicant has therefore proved the facts of his prior conviction but has failed to prove one thing on which his plea depends, namely, that the offences now charged are the same or are offences having the same imminence as those on which he was convicted at the Federal High Court.

“His constitutional objection under section 36 of section 9 has not been engaged yet. His prosecution before this court of nine counts of obtaining by false pretence and conspiracy to forge is not a second trial for the money laundering offences already tried.

It is a first trial for different offences arising from the connected but distinct basis of the same affair.

“The sole issue for determination is therefore resolved in favour of the complainant’s respondent and against the first defendant’s applicant. Having resolved the sole issue against the first defendant’s applicant, the application fails in its entirety.”

The judge fixed 3 December for continuation of the hearing.

Details of charges at the FCT High Court

The EFCC charged Mr Mamman alongside seven others on nine counts bordering on conspiracy, obtaining money by false pretence and intent to defraud, involving N31 billion.

His co-defendants are Mustapha Abubakar Bida, Joseph Omotayo Adewunmi, Ben Nsikak, Stephen Ojo, Oladipo Adebowale, Michael Achua and Ogunjobi Olusila.

On 16 October 2025, the EFCC arraigned the defendants before the court. They all pleaded not guilty to the charges.

On 7 May, the Federal High Court in Abuja convicted Mr Mamman of a N33.8 billion fraud. On 26 May, he was sentenced to 75 years’ imprisonment.

State of the case before the FCT High Court

The charges relate to the alleged diversion of funds meant for the Mambilla Power Project. The EFCC alleged that more than N26 billion was diverted on Mr Mamman’s instructions through Bureau de Change operators.

The commission also alleged that the defendants diverted about N31 billion in public funds.

In March, the court rejected an application by the second defendant, Mustapha Bida, seeking to halt the corruption trial involving Mr Mamman and the other defendants.

The EFCC has so far presented two witnesses in the trial. Both are bank officials.

The first prosecution witness, Umar Abba, is a compliance officer with Zenith Bank.

Through Mr Abba, the EFCC tendered account opening packages, signatory mandates, statements of accounts showing transactions on various accounts and certificates of identification for Spinhills Biz International Limited, Silverline Ocean Ventures Limited, Beaver Builders Limited, Gurupche Business Enterprise, Breathable Investment Limited, First-class Construction Project Limited, Royal Perimeter Ventures, Dannywest Limited, Dorino Bright Limited and Sipikin Global Ventures Limited.

However, Mr Abba told the court that he did not know the defendants personally.

The second prosecution witness, Leadu Kpandei, is also a compliance officer, with Guaranty Trust Bank.

Mr Kpandei presented the account opening documents, certificate of identification and statement of account of Fullest Utility Concept Ltd.

Mr Mamman served as minister of power between 2019 and 2021 under former President Muhammadu Buhari.

He was removed from office by Mr Buhari after about two years in the cabinet.

World.title: Lassa Fever: High treatment costs of concern as infections rise for two consecutive weeks- NCDC
World.content:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has identified the high cost of treatment and delayed presentation at health facilities as persistent challenges in Nigeria’s Lassa fever response, as new infections increased for two consecutive weeks.

The agency disclosed this in its situation reports for epidemiological weeks 45 and 46, covering 2 to 8 November and 9 to 15 November 2026, respectively.

According to the reports, new confirmed infections increased from 13 in week 44 to 18 in week 45, before rising further to 22 in week 46.

The figures represent a combined total of 40 new confirmed infections over the two weeks.

The latest infections were reported in Bauchi, Ondo, Edo and Benue states, while those recorded in the preceding week were reported in Ondo, Bauchi, Edo and Plateau states.

The NCDC noted that both suspected and confirmed cases recorded so far in 2026 exceeded those reported during the corresponding period in 2025.

Fatality rate remains higher than in 2025

According to the agency, Nigeria has recorded 278 Lassa fever deaths in 2026, with a case fatality rate (CFR) of 22.7 per cent as of week 46.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Although the fatality rate declined from 23.1 per cent in week 45, it remained higher than the 18.5 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025.

The cumulative number of reported deaths remained unchanged across the two reporting weeks.

The figures indicate that more than one in five people with confirmed Lassa fever infections in Nigeria this year have died.

The NCDC identified late presentation of patients as a contributing factor to the high fatality rate, alongside poor health-seeking behaviour linked to the cost of treatment and clinical management of the disease.

Other challenges identified by the agency include poor environmental sanitation and inadequate awareness in communities with a high burden of infections.

Ondo, Bauchi account for majority of infections

The NCDC said 26 states have recorded at least one confirmed case of Lassa fever across 122 local government areas (LGAs) in 2026.

However, five states, including Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, accounted for 87 per cent of all confirmed infections, while the remaining 21 affected states accounted for 13 per cent.

Ondo recorded the highest proportion of confirmed cases at 37 per cent, followed by Bauchi at 24 per cent, Taraba at 11 per cent, Edo at 10 per cent and Benue at five per cent.

Together, Ondo and Bauchi accounted for 61 per cent of all confirmed infections nationwide.

The reports also showed that people aged between 21 and 30 years remained the most affected age group, although confirmed infections were recorded among individuals aged between one and 93 years.

The median age of confirmed patients was 30 years, with a male-to-female ratio of 1:0.9.

No new healthcare worker infections were reported during either of the two reporting weeks.

Preparations for the next outbreak season

As part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s response to Lassa fever, the NCDC said it had finalised a five-year strategic plan covering 2026 to 2030 and the second edition of the national clinical management guidelines for the disease.

The agency also reported holding a meeting with state commissioners for health to discuss preparations for the forthcoming outbreak season.

In collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the World Health Organisation (WHO), the NCDC trained data teams across eight states to review deaths associated with Lassa fever.

The states are Edo, Bauchi, Ondo, Ebonyi, Benue, Plateau, Nasarawa and Taraba.

Other interventions highlighted in the reports include active case searches, contact tracing, training of frontline healthcare workers and the distribution of personal protective equipment to health facilities.

The agency also reported developing a 30-day healthcare worker protection plan to reduce infections among frontline personnel in endemic states.

Meanwhile, the national Lassa fever Incident Management System has been deactivated and transitioned to alert mode, with coordination efforts continuing through the national multisectoral technical working group.

Recommendations

The NCDC urged state governments to sustain year-round community engagement on Lassa fever prevention rather than limiting such activities to outbreak periods.

It also advised healthcare workers to maintain a high index of suspicion for the disease, facilitate timely referral and treatment, and adhere to standard infection prevention and control procedures.

The agency emphasised the need for continued collaboration with partners to strengthen the capacity of states to prevent, detect and respond promptly to Lassa fever outbreaks.

Lassa fever

Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness transmitted to humans primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rats.

Human-to-human transmission can also occur, particularly in healthcare settings where infection prevention and control measures are inadequate.

The NCDC recommends keeping food in rodent-proof containers, maintaining good environmental sanitation and avoiding contact with rodents.

People who develop symptoms consistent with Lassa fever, particularly after possible exposure, should seek prompt medical attention.

World.title: Rivers United sign three-year N490m shirt sponsorship deal
World.content:
Rivers United have signed a three-year front-of-shirt sponsorship deal worth $350,000 (about N490 million) with Goka Sports and Casino, as the club seeks to strengthen its commercial base amid its push for the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) title.

The agreement was unveiled on Tuesday at Platinum Hall, Hotel Presidential, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

The club’s sole administrator, Christopher Green, said Rivers United rejected Goka’s initial proposal for a one-year agreement, opting instead for a three-year commitment with an upward renewal option.

“Goka wanted a one-year contract with an extension, but we said no. We’ll go for three years first, with an upward renewal.

“So the deal is worth three hundred and fifty thousand US dollars, which is four hundred and ninety million naira in Nigerian currency,” Mr Green said.

The deal comes as Rivers United continue to establish themselves among the leading sides in Nigerian football. The club finished second in last season’s NPFL, narrowly missing out on the title by one point after accumulating 67 points from 38 matches, compared with champions Rangers International’s 68.

The Port Harcourt club have maintained their competitive form this season, remaining in the title race and keeping pressure on the teams above them. Their performances have reinforced their ambition to challenge for the league crown again.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Green said the sponsorship could pave the way for additional commercial agreements covering other parts of the team’s kit, including the back of the shirt and sleeves.

“With this, we’ve opened the door for more sponsorship deals. In no time, we will get the one for the back shirt, one for the sleeve and the others,” he said.

He also disclosed that discussions were ongoing to extend Goka’s involvement to Rivers Hoopers, the state’s basketball team.

“We have been talking to Goka and we have also sold Rivers Hoopers to them. Soon they will come for the same front-shirt sponsorship,” he said.

Goka explains partnership

Speaking on behalf of Goka Sports and Casino, Jide Odi described the agreement as a significant commitment to Nigerian sports, saying the company assessed several clubs before settling on Rivers United.

He said the assessment considered the clubs’ history, coefficients and standing in domestic football.

“We’re here to stay, we’re not going anywhere.

“Goka is here to expand the frontiers of private partnership with sports in Nigeria, and we’re starting with Rivers United,” Mr Odi said.

He said the club’s ambitions aligned with the company’s plan to expand private-sector involvement in Nigerian sports, adding that the partnership was expected to create opportunities for both sides.

Mr Odi expressed regret that the unveiling did not take place before Rivers United’s 6-0 victory over Niger Tornadoes, saying he would have liked to see the new branding on the club’s shirts during the match.

He, however, said the agreement was intended to be a long-term relationship.

“This is just the first step in the long-term relationship. We’re looking to expand the conversation in partnerships and to see how we can take Nigerian football forward,” he said.

Fubara welcomes sponsorship

Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara, represented at the event by former Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Communications, Mike Elechi, commended the club’s management for securing the agreement.

Mr Elechi said the partnership represented an investment in the club, noting that the sponsors would also need to recoup their investment through commercial activities, including jersey sales.

He also thanked Goka for choosing Rivers United, describing the partnership as an opportunity to support the club’s development.

World.title: Algeria vs Nigeria: Eguavoen names 24 Super Falcons for double friendly ahead of Olympic qualifiers
World.content:
Super Falcons interim head coach Augustine Eguavoen has named a 24-player squad for Nigeria’s two international friendly matches against Algeria later this month.

Goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie and forward Asisat Oshoala headline the selection for the matches scheduled for 30 November and 4 December.

The first encounter will take place at the 5 July 1962 Stadium in Algiers, while the second is scheduled for the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium in Tizi-Ouzou.

The squad comprises three goalkeepers, seven defenders, seven midfielders and seven forwards.

Captain Rasheedat Ajibade is absent from the list as she continues her recovery from surgery following an injury sustained during Nigeria’s 2028 Los Angeles Olympic qualifying fixture against Comoros in October.

Other notable selections include defenders Michelle Alozie, Oluwatosin Demehin and Shukurat Oladipo; midfielders Christy Ucheibe, Jennifer Echegini and Toni Payne; and forwards Folashade Ijamilusi and Joy Omewa.

The friendlies will form part of Nigeria’s preparations for the third round of the African qualifying series for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, where the Super Falcons are scheduled to face Morocco between 23 February and 6 March 2027.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria advanced to the third round after defeating Comoros 7-0 on aggregate in October. The two-legged tie against Morocco will determine which country progresses to the next stage of the qualifying competition.

Eguavoen was appointed interim head coach in September following the departure of Justine Madugu and his technical crew. He is working with a technical team that includes Nasarawa Amazons coach Christopher Danjuma and former Super Falcons defender Ayisat Yusuf.

The 24 players selected for the Algeria friendlies are:

Goalkeepers: Chiamaka Nnadozie (Brighton & Hove Albion, England); Comfort Erhabor (Portsmouth Ladies, England); Christiana Uzoma (Edo Queens).

Defenders: Michelle Alozie (Chicago Stars, USA); Shukurat Oladipo (AS Roma, Italy); Glory Ogbonna (Besiktas JK, Turkey); Oluwatosin Demehin (SL Benfica, Portugal); Glory Edet (Bayelsa Queens); Valentina Uroko (Edo Queens); Nicole Payne (Orlando Pride, USA).

Midfielders: Christy Ucheibe (Al-Hilal, Saudi Arabia); Joy Igbokwe (Nasarawa Amazons); Regina Otu (Fenerbahçe, Turkey); Fatimoh Solaty (Nasarawa Amazons); Suliat Abideen (Fenerbahçe, Turkey); Toni Payne (Inter Milan, Italy); Jennifer Echegini (Paris Saint-Germain, France).

Forwards: Asisat Oshoala (Al-Hilal, Saudi Arabia); Folashade Ijamilusi (Liaoning Shenyang Shenbei, China); Shakirat Moshood (SCU Torreense, Portugal); Blessing Okpe (Dnepr Mogilev, Belarus); Joy Omewa (BK Häcken, Sweden); Blessing Nkor (Dynamo Brest, Belarus); Olamide Adugbe (Asteras Tripolis, Greece).

Algeria pick 25

Meanwhile, Algeria have also named a 25-player squad for the double-header, with head coach Farid Benstiti selecting three goalkeepers, eight defenders, seven midfielders and seven forwards.

The North Africans will seek to test their options ahead of their own 2028 Olympic qualifying campaign. They advanced to the third round after thrashing the Central African Republic 8–0 and 7–0 in their two-legged second-round tie, scoring 15 goals without conceding. Algeria will face Burkina Faso in the next round.

World.title: 20 years ago with Muammar Ghaddafi, By Femi Fani-Kayode
World.content:
Permit me to take you on an interesting historical journey.

On 26th November 2006, which is 20 years ago to the day, the great leader Muammar Ghaddafi of Libya came to Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit.

As Minister of Aviation at the time I had the honour and privilege of receiving him at the airport on behalf of my boss His Excellency President Olusegun Obasanjo and I was detailed to spend the next four days with him accompanying him wherever he went.

There is no doubt that Ghaddafi’s charissma was infectious and after spending those four days with him my perception of him changed from being that of a wary skeptic to becoming one of his most vocal admirers.

He was a truly extraordinary man who really did love Africa.

Yet his visit had a very bumpy start.

He arrived at the airport with no less than approximately 200 bodyguards, all with sidearms, and at least 100 cars (which had been sent ahead and were parked at the airport) to convey him to Abuja.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK 47’s and all manner of sophisticated weapons.

They took them from one of the three planes he came in and loaded the boots of the cars with them.

We then proceeded to leave the airport in convoy but we were blocked at the gate by our security personnel and our military.

We were told that it was because of the weapons and that whilst Ghaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in (with their sidearms) the high powered weapons that were in the boots of their vehicles would not.

I was in the car with Ghaddafi and I had the onerous task of explaining the situation to him through his interpreter who was in the car with us.

We went back to the airport and tried to leave again 3 times but we we were blocked each time and during the course of each attempt tempers were rising.

The next thing that happened was beyond shocking.

Ghaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja saying that if the cars were not allowed in he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!

I was right next to him, in panic mode, as we walked and my fear was that he would collapse under the sun and as a consequence of walking so far.

What made my fear even more accute and pronounced was that he was already sweating profusely and panting.

I was expecting the worse even as I was appealing to him not to do this.

My appeals fell on deaf ears.

I called President Obasanjo and, luckily for us all, he told me that he was on his way to the airport to cath a flight and attend a quick function in Lagos.

He said I should tell Ghadaffi that he was on his way to the airport to settle the matter himself and get him to go back to the airport which I did.

Luckily Ghaddaffi, after being told that OBJ was on his way agreed to do so especially after I said that he was rushing to the airport to address the matter himself and appeal to him.

When OBJ arrived they greeted and hugged one another warmly and after a very brief converstation OBJ got up to leave and told him that he is off to Lagos and would be back later in the day and in time for the opening session of the conference the following morning.

As he was leaving Ghaddaffi told him that there was an issue at the gate and that he had been blocked three times.

OBJ feigned ignorance of the event, apologised to him profusely and said the gates would he opened for him immediately.

However as he walked past me he bent over and whispered quietly into my ear that under no circumstances would Ghaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK 47’s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane.

After that he disappeared and left me to handle the mess.

I told Ghaddafi that the weapons needed to be removed and his men reluctantly complied after I had a hot encounter and harsh trading of words with his Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol who were very rude to our security officers, our military personnel and our officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that were present and who had threatened to fly Ghaddafi back to Libya there and then and boycott the entire conference if we refused to allow them to take their heavy weapons in.

The weapons were taken out of the boot of the cars and loaded back in the plane after which a contingent of our soldiers surrounded the plane in order to ensure that they were not smuggled out later.

We then proceeded to the gate and the convoy was allowed through.

As we were leaving my wife Regina called me on the phone and said the whole matter was being reported in detail on the BBC and that she hoped all was well.

I assured her that the matter had been amicably resolved and that we were on our way to town.

On his part Ghaddafi, still angry, remained silent in the car throughout our ride into Abuja and the only time he spoke was when we drove past the Central Mosque and he said how beautiful it was.

It was that day that I learnt about the intricacies of diplomacy and the fact that firmness, the display of mutual respect and a strict adherence to the rules of engagement were vital.

On that day our military personnel and security agencies that were determined to implement the directives from the President and their commanders made me proud whilst the wisdom, strength and courage that OBJ displayed was instructive and exemplary.

We stood our ground and had our way and because we did so Ghaddafi and his team showed us massive respect from that moment on.

For the next four days during the course of the conference he and I became very close and he even invited me as his personal guest to Libya.

The only complaint he had was that I had worne a suit for each of those days and that he would have preferred me to wear an agbada or babariga!

The whole experience was sureal.

Ghaddafi was a truly extraordinary and inspring man and, as I studied him closely for those four days, I learnt much from him.

As for my boss OBJ, he saved lives on that day by putting his foot down and insisting that the heavy weapons must not be let in because, as I was later told when the matter was discussed at the next cabinet meeting, what the Libyans had done in the past when they carried in such weapons was to hand them over to their local associates and leave them behind.

Those lethal weapons would later become part of a stockpile of arms that provided a massive arsenal for terrorists, insurgents and other ruthless non-state actors within our country.

On 20th October 2011, five years almost to the day and month after his visit to our country and our extraordinary airport encounter, Muammar Ghaddafi met a violent end in the hands of his own people in his home town, Sirte.

I watched the footage of his brutal murder on CNN and was deeply saddened.

No-one deserves to be killed in such a barbaric manner.

That an all powerful leader who was literally worshipped by his people can come to such a bloody end in the flash of an eye spoke volumes and serves as a lesson to us all.

This was a clear and graphic example and confirmation of the ephemeral and transient nature of power and the futility of the vanity that goes with it.

What hit me even more was the fact that the Head of Protocol who spoke so loudly and aggressively on the day of our encounter and who said that if we did not allow the arms to be taken in they would fly Ghaddafi back home was one of those condemning him on CNN all the way from Paris on the day he was murdered.

Such is life!

Femi Fani-Kayode is Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, a former minister of Culture and Tourism and a former Minister of Aviation.

World.title: Fountain of Life Crisis: Court orders Jimmy Odukoya’s arrest over absence
World.content:
A Lagos State High Court has issued a warrant for the arrest of Jimmy Odukoya, the embattled Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, after he failed to appear in court on Thursday.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the court had directed Mr Odukoya to appear to answer allegations that he disobeyed an order barring him from acting as the church’s senior pastor.

The court ordered him to appear to show cause in the contempt proceedings filed by the church’s Incorporated Trustees.

However, Mr Odukoya, an actor-turned-pastor, failed to appear for the hearing, prompting Justice O. Adewunmi-Oshin to issue an arrest warrant, TVC News reported.

Justice Adewunmi-Oshin also directed that the case be returned to the administrative judge for reassignment.

Before the hearing commenced, court officials barred journalists from covering the proceedings, reportedly acting on the judge’s instructions.

Summon

This newspaper earlier reported that Mr Odukoya told worshippers at a Sunday service that he knew about the injunction but had not yet received it formally.
