Leadership is not merely about occupying public office; it is also about recognising talent, identifying capacity and placing the right people in positions where their experience can serve the public good. In appointing Dr Olukayode Ajulo, SAN, as Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Ondo State, Governor Aiyedatiwa demonstrated this quality of discernment.

It was a strategic choice that brought considerable legal experience and institutional reform-mindedness into the administration. The Governor deserves credit not only for identifying and bringing Ajulo to Ondo State, but also for providing the leadership space and support within which the Attorney-General could pursue an ambitious justice-sector reform agenda.

From Constitutional Litigation To Public Service

Appointed in February 2024 by Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa, Dr. Ajulo brought to the office considerable experience in constitutional litigation, human rights advocacy, commercial law and arbitration. An alumnus of the University of Jos, where he obtained his LL.B. and LL.M. degrees, he also pursued doctoral research focusing on workers’ rights and corporate social responsibility. His professional journey included service at the Federal Ministry of Justice, Chief Afe Babalola’s Emmanuel Chambers, Dr. Tunji Abayomi & Co. and Wole Adebayo’s House of Law before he established Kayode Ajulo & Co., popularly known as Castle of Law. He became a Senior Advocate of Nigeria in 2023 and was conferred with the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger.

Beyond the courtroom, one of the most enduring expressions of Dr Ajulo’s commitment to access to justice is his establishment of Egalitarian Mission for Africa, a non-profit organisation. Among its pioneering interventions is the Save-A-Prisoner-A-Day Initiative, through which, more than 5,000 prisoners benefited from free legal assistance and related interventions over a ten-year period. One notable case was that of Bamiteko Adeolu, a teenager in Ado-Ekiti who had been sentenced to death by the High Court of Ekiti State. Dr Ajulo took up his appeal, and the Court of Appeal overturned the death sentence, thereby saving the young man’s life.

His constitutional litigation background was also demonstrated in President, Federal Republic of Nigeria & Anor. v. National Assembly & Ors., Suit No. SC/CV/504/2022, in which he represented the National Assembly, the Senate President and the Speaker of the House of Representatives against a suit instituted by President Muhammadu Buhari and the then Attorney-General of the Federation over Section 84(12) of the Electoral Act 2022. On 24 June 2022, a seven-member panel of the Supreme Court unanimously struck out the action for want of jurisdiction. The case placed him in the unusual position of defending the legislature against the President and the nation’s Chief Law Officer, raising important questions about the constitutional relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government.

His professional engagements have also extended beyond litigation into complex public-sector advisory work. Through Kayode Ajulo & Co. (Castle of Law), he provided legal and consultancy services in connection with the Paris Club refund exercise on behalf of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and the 36 states of the Federation. The exercise facilitated the recovery and distribution of substantial multi-billion-dollar refunds to the states, representing a significant intervention in Nigeria’s intergovernmental fiscal relations.

His work in federalism is further reflected in the Supreme Court decision in Attorney-General of Lagos State & Ors. v. Attorney-General of the Federation, Suit No. SC/1/2008, concerning the National Lottery Act. The judgment affirmed the limits of federal legislative authority in matters within the residual legislative competence of states. In Ondo State, the Ministry of Justice has sought to give practical effect to the principles of state regulatory authority, including in the lottery and gaming sector.

The Ajulokay Agenda And The Repositioning Of The Ministry

Upon assuming office, Dr. Ajulo introduced the eight-point AJULOKAY Agenda as a framework for repositioning the Ministry of Justice and improving justice administration. Its priorities include access to justice, institutional reform, improved law enforcement procedures, professional development and welfare for law officers, obedience to court orders and the protection of vulnerable groups. One of its early initiatives was the engagement of 273 legal practitioners as honorary and technical advisers, drawing on the experience of senior practitioners, academics, retired judicial officers and younger lawyers to strengthen the Ministry’s professional capacity.

The Ministry’s role has also extended into policy development and legislative engagement. Policy papers and legislative proposals have been prepared and transmitted to the State House of Assembly for consideration, addressing issues of public importance and the welfare of the people. This reflects an understanding that a Ministry of Justice should do more than provide legal advice or defend government in court, it must also help shape the legal and policy framework through which government responds to society’s needs. The wider objective is to make the Ministry a proactive institution capable of anticipating legal challenges, supporting sound policy and translating governance priorities into effective legal reforms.

Strengthening The Judiciary And Protecting Property Rights

A major component of the administration’s justice-sector interventions has been the strengthening of the Judiciary. For many years, the statutory number of High Court judges in Ondo State remained at 24. The Ondo State High Court (Amendment) Law 2024 increased the statutory complement to 35, with six additional judges subsequently sworn in during October 2024. The administration also engaged additional legal officers, with 44 new lawyers reportedly recruited into the state’s legal service by 2026. Progress has also been made towards securing the financial autonomy of the Judiciary, recognising that judicial independence requires not only constitutional guarantees but also adequate resources and institutional support. The ultimate test, however, is whether these improvements translate into faster and more effective justice delivery.

Another significant intervention has been the protection of property rights and the campaign against land grabbing. Following an Executive Order issued by Governor Aiyedatiwa, the government enacted the Ondo State Property Protection and Documentation Law 2024, signed on 30 December 2024. The Anti-Land Grabbing Task Force, inaugurated on 28 May 2025, has responsibility for strengthening enforcement, with Dr. Ajulo serving as its Chairman. The appointment of 130 Justices of the Peace in November 2025 further supports efforts to strengthen community-level justice mechanisms. Together, these measures seek to replace unlawful occupation and self-help with documentation, lawful processes and institutional enforcement.

Access To Justice And A Long-Term Reform Framework

The effectiveness of justice-sector reform must ultimately be measured by its impact on ordinary citizens. Under Dr. Ajulo’s leadership, the Ministry has pursued initiatives intended to improve access to legal protection, particularly for people who cannot readily afford legal representation or navigate the justice system. The Office of the People Defender is part of this effort, alongside digital initiatives involving electronic legal resources, criminal records management and improved legal-service processes. The 2026 amendments to the Ondo State Office of the Public Defender Law and the Ondo State Law Commission Law also represent efforts to strengthen the statutory foundations of public legal services and law reform.

A further expression of this long-term approach is the Ten-Year Justice Sector Development Plan (2027–2037), with Ondo State as its pilot jurisdiction. Covering 20 strategic pillars, the plan addresses judicial infrastructure, digital justice, access to justice, institutional independence, criminal justice reform, professional development and legislative modernisation. Its proposed initiatives include Ondo Digital Justice, envisioned as a Court Without Walls; Justice City and Justice Service Hubs; the People Defender; the Ondo Government Legal Service; and a Justice Academy for professional training. The plan’s significance lies in its attempt to establish a framework that can outlive the tenure of any individual officeholder. Its real value will depend on implementation, continuity and measurable improvements in the delivery of justice.

The constitutional debate over state policing also forms part of the wider reform conversation. Drawing on the experience of Amotekun, Dr. Ajulo has engaged with the need for security arrangements that respond to local realities while remaining subject to constitutional safeguards, professional standards and accountability. As Chief Law Officer, his responsibility includes ensuring that any emerging framework is legally sound and consistent with constitutional democracy.

Professional Leadership, Staff Welfare And Institutional Devt

Dr. Ajulo’s engagement with the legal profession extends beyond government service. His leadership of the Nigerian Bar Association’s pioneer Mentorship Committee reflects his interest in preparing younger lawyers for the demands of professional practice. He has also maintained an interest in legal education and institutional leadership, including participation in the Cambridge Advanced Leadership Programme at Cambridge Judge Business School in November 2026, which engaged contemporary issues such as innovation, artificial intelligence, geopolitics and the future of work.

Within the Ministry, there has also been an improvement in staff morale, welfare and professional confidence. State Counsel are reportedly better equipped and more motivated in the discharge of their responsibilities. One judge, commenting on the change, remarked that in all his years on the Bench he had rarely, if ever, seen a State Counsel arrive in court in a well-maintained, brand-new official vehicle, chauffeur-driven. So impressed was he by the presentation that he expressed a desire to return to the Ministry of Justice. The observation, beyond the vehicle itself, points to the importance of restoring dignity and confidence to public legal service.

The physical environment of the Ministry has also undergone improvement, with a more organised and professional outlook. Governor Aiyedatiwa has additionally approved the construction of a dedicated building for the Ministry, which would provide a permanent institutional home suited to its responsibilities. Staff recognition has complemented these improvements. At a post-NBA Annual General Conference event, Dr. Ajulo personally rewarded five legal officers with #1 million each, disbursing #5 million from his private funds, while also extending welfare gestures to non-legal staff. These measures underline the importance of recognising the contributions of both legal and non-legal personnel to the effective functioning of the institution.

A Philosophy Of Service: Government And The People As Clients

There is a philosophy underpinning Dr. Ajulo’s approach to public service. He has described the Governor as his Client-in-Chief while regarding every citizen of Ondo State as a client whose interests deserve attention and representation. This reflects an understanding that the Attorney-General’s responsibility cannot be reduced to protecting the interests of the government in power. Government must be advised and defended in ways that remain consistent with the Constitution, the law and the public interest. It also helps explain why his role has extended beyond conventional legal representation to communicating government policy, explaining decisions and addressing issues affecting the people.

Conclusion: Measuring The Office By What It Leaves Behind

Ultimately, the true measure of Dr. Ajulo’s stewardship as Attorney-General will lie not merely in the cases won, policies introduced or reforms initiated, but in the strength of the institutions he leaves behind and the enduring principles he upholds.

His legacy will be defined by the durability of his reforms and their capacity to transcend his tenure.

Governments will change, officeholders will depart, and political seasons will pass; but institutions founded on sound principles must endure. For, in the final analysis, the law is greater than the lawyer, the Constitution greater than the government, and justice greater than the office through which it is administered.

It is against these enduring imperatives, rather than the fleeting measures of political acclaim or official accomplishment, that his stewardship must ultimately be judged.

For the true test of leadership lies not in the power once wielded, but in the principles faithfully upheld; not in the authority once exercised, but in the institutions firmly established; and not in the honours enjoyed in office, but in the legacy that withstands the passage of time.

When the tenure ends, the titles fade and the applause falls silent, it is only the enduring strength of institutions and the fidelity to principle that will speak for the man who once held the office.

*Hamza Nuhu Dantani, Esq, a Legal Practitioner, writes from Abuja.

World.title: RIP | Family to bid farewell to Jeffreys Bay’s Daniël Stevens
World.content:
Family and friends will gather at the Uitenhage Baptist Church on Saturday, 28 November, to celebrate the life of Daniël Stevens. Image: X

The family of Daniël Stevens has invited those whose lives he touched to celebrate his life at a memorial service in Kariega (formerly Uitenhage) on Saturday, 28 November.

The 25-year-old died in hospital on Monday, 23 November, following an alleged assault outside Je’Vista Social Café in Jeffreys Bay.

Ahead of the service, his family has made a special request to those attending.



FAMILY TO BID FAREWELL TO DANIËL STEVENS

Daniël’s brother, JC Stevens, announced the memorial arrangements on social media on Wednesday evening.

“If Daniël meant something to you, feel free to join us for the service. It would have meant a lot to him if you came,” he wrote.

The service will take place at 11:00 at the Uitenhage Baptist Church at 10 Dodd Road.

The family has encouraged those attending to bring small printed photographs of themselves with Daniël to add to a memorial board.

Those unable to attend can follow the service live on Facebook and TikTok.

LOVED ONES REMEMBER DANIËL

Daniël and his best friend, Dylan, shared ambitions of building a business together.



Their friendship dates back to their school years, when a mutual passion for fishing brought them together. They went on to live together in Pretoria and explore business opportunities.

Dylan had been working in the United States to secure funding, with plans to invest their earnings in the business upon his return.

“He’s my best, best friend, my brother,” he said in an earlier interview.

JC also reflected on the challenges Daniël had overcome throughout his life, including surviving a dog attack as a six-year-old and spending 27 days in hospital after an electrical accident in 2019.

JEFFREYS BAY MURDER INVESTIGATION

Eastern Cape police arrested four suspects, aged between 16 and 21, in Jeffreys Bay, Kariega and Humansdorp on Wednesday, 25 November.

Daniël allegedly came under attack after stepping in to help a friend on Saturday, 21 November.

The South African is awaiting confirmation from the provincial National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) regarding the latest court proceedings.

Meanwhile, friends have launched a BackaBuddy campaign to help his parents cover legal expenses as they seek justice for their son.

World.title: Carling Knockout Cup final under threat? Moses Mabhida faces December scheduling headache
World.content:
Durban’s Moses Mabhida Stadium could face an unexpected challenge ahead of the 2026 Carling Knockout Cup final, with a major rugby fixture scheduled to take place nearby on the same day.

The stadium is scheduled to host the Carling Knockout Cup final on Saturday, 12 December 2026.

However, the Sharks are also set to host Welsh outfit Scarlets at a venue that’s two kilometres away, raising potential concerns over traffic congestion, crowd management and security.



While no official decision has been announced regarding a possible change of venue, the situation presents a logistical headache for organisers who will be keen to ensure the smooth running of both sporting events.

CARLING KNOCKOUT CUP FINAL MAY NOT GO TO DURBAN

There is a recent South African football precedent that could offer an indication of how authorities might approach this situation.

Earlier this year, the highly anticipated Soweto Derby between Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs, initially scheduled for 25 April at FNB Stadium, was moved to 26 April.



The decision was influenced by The Ultra Music Festival, which was taking place at the Nasrec Expo Centre and was expected to draw significant crowds to the area.

Authorities opted to move the football spectacle to avoid potential traffic and security complications.

A similar approach could be considered in Durban should organisers conclude that hosting two major sporting events within close proximity on the same day poses unnecessary challenges.



However, whether the Carling Knockout Cup final will remain at Moses Mabhida Stadium remains to be seen.

For now, all eyes will be on the organisers and relevant authorities as they assess the situation ahead of what promises to be a significant day on South Africa’s sporting calendar.

DHL STADIUM A POSSIBILITY?

The DHL Stadium has widely tipped to host the Carling Knockout Cup final between Chiefs and Pirates.



Should this final go to Cape Town, it would be the first time that a Soweto Derby final is played there.

World.title: Former All Black donates R9.5 million to support NWU medical students
World.content:
A former All Blacks star has donated approximately R9.5 million to help financially disadvantaged South African students pursue medical degrees. Image: Supplied

A former All Blacks star has donated approximately R9.5 million to help financially disadvantaged South African students pursue medical degrees.

Dr Lawrie Knight, who represented New Zealand between 1974 and 1977, has donated NZ$1 million to North-West University (NWU) to establish a scholarship fund at its Desmond Tutu School of Medicine.

The Knight Scholarship Fund will support at least 12 students studying towards a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) degree.



The donation will be administered by NWU under a six-year agreement, with bursaries available to cover tuition fees, accommodation, food and other approved study-related costs.

The amount awarded to each student will depend on their individual financial circumstances.

Who can apply for the Knight Scholarship Fund?

The fund is intended for South African citizens who meet the admission requirements for the university’s MBChB programme and can demonstrate financial need.



However, academic eligibility and financial circumstances will not be the only selection criteria.

The selection panel will also consider personal qualities such as integrity, compassion and perseverance.

An interest in sport, physical activity or other pursuits that promote a healthy lifestyle will also be taken into account.



The contribution is expected to help students who might otherwise struggle to meet the substantial costs associated with medical training.

NWU welcomes donation

NWU principal and vice-chancellor Professor Bismark Tyobeka and Faculty of Health Sciences executive dean Professor Awie Kotzé welcomed Knight’s contribution, saying it would make a lasting difference to the students who receive assistance.

They also encouraged other potential donors to support the Desmond Tutu School of Medicine and help more students overcome financial barriers to becoming doctors.



Professor Binu Luke, chief director of the Desmond Tutu School of Medicine, said the institution was grateful for Knight’s generosity.

“The Desmond Tutu School of Medicine is eternally grateful to Dr Lawrie Knight for this act of kindness. It will go a long way towards helping students facing financial challenges pursue a demanding degree like the MBChB and realise their dream of becoming doctors,” he said.

Luke said the university would use the donation responsibly to help students with essential expenses.



“R9.5 million is no small amount, and the school will use it responsibly and wisely to support students with needs such as tuition fees, accommodation and food. This donation energises and motivates the team working to establish and run the school,” he said.

From All Blacks rugby to medicine in Johannesburg

Knight’s contribution also reflects his own experience of balancing rugby with medical studies.

The former international played 35 matches for New Zealand, including six Tests, between 1974 and 1977.



He later practised medicine in Johannesburg.

One of the defining moments of his rugby career came in his final Test against the British and Irish Lions at Eden Park in 1977.

Knight scored a late try to help the All Blacks secure a dramatic 10-9 victory, sealing a 3-1 series win.



His R9.5 million donation will now help a new generation of South African students follow a similar path into medicine, regardless of their financial circumstances.

World.title: ‘Food and grocery vouchers’: South African’s call for SASSA to rethink support
World.content:
Diela Woolf has a straightforward idea to help pensioners who are struggling to put food on the table.

In a comment on a recent post on The South African’s Facebook page, Woolf asked why the government does not offer a different kind of support.

“Why can’t government at least give food & grocery vouchers 2 pensioners & struggling families,” Woolf wrote.



The comment has drawn reactions and a reply from other users.

A call for food voucher support

Woolf’s suggestion centres on two groups who often feel the squeeze most: pensioners and families who are already struggling.

The idea behind food and grocery vouchers is simple. The support goes directly towards food and cannot be swallowed by debts, transport or other costs before the household eats.



For pensioners who support grandchildren, or families where one income feeds many people, that kind of guaranteed food support could make a noticeable difference.

Vouchers already exist in some form

Some food-focused help is already available, although many South Africans are not aware of it. SASSA’s Social Relief of Distress programme, which is separate from the monthly SRD grant, can provide temporary assistance as food parcels, vouchers or cash to people facing a crisis.

The Department of Social Development also supports community nutrition and development centres and food programmes in various areas. The catch is that this help is usually temporary, depends on an application, and is not offered on a regular monthly basis like a grant.



The cash versus vouchers debate

Woolf’s comment touches on a long-running debate. Supporters of vouchers argue that they make sure money goes towards food, especially in households under heavy financial pressure.

Supporters of cash grants argue that cash gives people dignity and the freedom to decide what their household needs most, whether that is food, transport or school shoes.

Many South Africans in comment sections say they would welcome any extra support, whatever form it takes.



For struggling households, Woolf’s question remains a fair one: if money is not enough, why not make sure there is at least food?

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Elon Musk to give two SpaceX shares to ‘every child in America’
World.content:
South Africa-born tech billionaire Elon Musk said he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company. Image: AFP

South Africa-born tech billionaire Elon Musk said he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month.

“Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns.

Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally  November 26, 2026

READ | Cyril Ramaphosa says Elon Musk should remember his South Africa roots

Elon Musk, world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year.

He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work.



“I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.”

“These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said.

73 million children in the US

In October, Elon Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.”



There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau.

The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 (R2 244) on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion – or R4 488 per child.

Ambition to colonise Mars

SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion.



The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonise Mars.

According to Forbes, Elon Musk has a net worth of $823.5 billion.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: World Rugby launches double Springbok investigation – report
World.content:
The Springboks are facing fresh disciplinary uncertainty just days before their Nations Championship final against France. Image: AFP

The Springboks are facing fresh disciplinary uncertainty just days before their Nations Championship final against France, with head coach Rassie Erasmus and assistant coach Mzwandile Stick both reportedly under investigation over separate incidents.

The developments have added another layer of controversy to South Africa’s end-of-year campaign, which has been overshadowed by Erasmus’s six-match suspension following his extraordinary criticism of match officials after the narrow defeat to France in Paris.

World Rugby and Nations Championship organisers are now examining whether Erasmus may have breached the conditions of that suspension during the Springboks’ subsequent match against Ireland.



READ | Springboks want to win Nations Championship for Rassie Erasmus

Stick, meanwhile, has attracted scrutiny over comments questioning the decision to clear Ireland flyhalf Sam Prendergast to play against South Africa.

Neither investigation has resulted in a confirmed additional sanction, but the possibility of further disciplinary action comes at a particularly difficult time for the world champions.



Rassie Erasmus’s six-match suspension

Erasmus was handed a six-international-match suspension on 17 November after an independent panel considered comments he made about the officiating in South Africa’s 21-19 defeat to France.

The Springboks coach questioned the integrity of match officials and raised the possibility of match-fixing or manipulation of the game in relation to decisions involving foul play.

World Rugby ruled that his comments amounted to an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of match officials.



The sanction was imposed under the governing body’s Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, which was introduced in July 2026 to address public criticism of officials.

Importantly, the suspension went beyond simply preventing Erasmus from attending matches.

It also prohibited him from coaching or having direct or indirect contact with players and team management on match days, entering the stadium or technical areas, communicating with match officials and undertaking media duties during the suspension.



Erasmus was therefore unable to be with the Springboks on match day when they faced Ireland in Dublin on Saturday, 21 November.

Erasmus’s Ireland watchalong raises fresh questions

Despite being barred from attending the match, Erasmus watched the Springboks’ 20-17 defeat to Ireland from his hotel room in Dublin.

The 54-year-old hosted an online watchalong, inviting supporters to join him as he followed the match remotely.



The livestream was largely muted to avoid broadcasting copyrighted match commentary, but Erasmus was seen speaking on his phone on several occasions while wearing earbuds and covering his mouth.

Those moments have now attracted the attention of rugby authorities, who are reportedly examining whether he may have communicated with members of the Springboks’ coaching staff or management during the match.

The concern centres on the indirect-contact restrictions included in his suspension.



The investigation is not confirmation that Erasmus passed instructions to the coaches. The question is whether his actions breached the conditions imposed by World Rugby.

South Africa’s coaching staff have denied receiving instructions from their suspended head coach during the match.

Assistant coach Felix Jones said he had no knowledge of Erasmus communicating with the team, while Stick suggested the coach could simply have been speaking to people who had joined his online watch party.



The Springboks lost the match 20-17, despite a second-half fightback that brought them within three points of Ireland.

The second controversy involves assistant coach Stick and his public criticism of the decision to clear Prendergast to face South Africa.

The Ireland flyhalf had been cited following a hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato during an earlier Nations Championship match.



However, an independent disciplinary committee dismissed the citing, ruling that the incident did not meet the threshold required for a red card.

The decision meant Prendergast was available for Ireland’s clash with the Springboks.

Speaking ahead of that match, Stick questioned whether the same outcome would have been reached if the player responsible had been Fijian.



“If that was a Fijian player tackling an Irish player with that hip-drop, that player would be in Fiji now,” Stick said.

He also referred to Fiji’s traditional drink, kava, suggesting a Fijian player would have been sent home and required to undertake additional tackling lessons.

“But it’s an Irish player, it’s free to play,” he added.



According to the42.ie, Stick’s comments have prompted the Nations Championship organisers to investigate whether they could fall under World Rugby’s match officials abuse process or potentially constitute misconduct.

The tournament organisers have reportedly contacted World Rugby to establish how the matter should be handled.

The controversy is particularly sensitive because the independent committee that cleared Prendergast reached its decision unanimously.



No disciplinary outcome against Stick has been announced.

Springboks leave coaching position empty at media event

The controversy continued this week when the Springboks opted not to send an assistant coach to a media event ahead of the Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham.

Erasmus was unable to attend because his suspension also covers media duties.



While other participating teams were represented by their head coaches and captains, South Africa sent only captain Siya Kolisi.

The decision attracted attention, although the Springboks were not contractually obliged to provide an assistant coach.

Asked about the absence, Kolisi made it clear that the decision was not his.



“I don’t make those decisions. I’m here to represent the team and that’s about it,” he said.

The captain also acknowledged that Erasmus’s absence on match days was difficult for the players, but insisted the coach remained involved in preparations during the week.

“He’s coaching us, he’s with us, the only difference is that he’s not there on Saturday, which is tough,” Kolisi said.



“But you can’t make excuses. It’s what is happening right now.”

Springboks face France in Nations Championship final

South Africa now have to put the off-field distractions behind them as they prepare for a major showdown with France.

The Springboks will meet the French at Twickenham on Sunday, 29 November, in the inaugural Nations Championship final.



The match offers South Africa an opportunity to finish the tournament with a major victory, but it also brings a rematch against the team that beat them 21-19 in Paris earlier this month.

The Springboks subsequently suffered another narrow defeat, going down 20-17 to Ireland, although they secured their place in the final with a losing bonus point.

Erasmus will remain unavailable on match day as he serves his suspension, leaving the Springboks without their head coach on the touchline for another crucial encounter.



For Kolisi and the players, the challenge is to ensure that the disciplinary controversies do not become an excuse for their performances.

However, with two separate investigations involving members of the coaching staff, the build-up to the France final has become about much more than the rugby.

Do you agree there’s ultimately only one winner here – and it’s NOT the Springboks?

World.title: THROWBACK: 200mm of rain drenched parts of Gauteng in one day
World.content:
A rainfall station in the extreme southern parts of Gauteng recorded 200mm of rain on 26 November 2001, making it one of the province’s standout weather records.

A study by researchers from the South African Weather Service and the University of Pretoria recorded the rainfall as the highest daily November total measured at a Gauteng station.

The measurement was recorded during a month that brought repeated heavy rainfall to the province.



Gauteng recorded 10 days of heavy rain

November 2001 stood out for its unusually frequent downpours.

Researchers found that at least one rainfall station in Gauteng recorded more than 50mm of rain within 24 hours on 10 days that month.

This was the highest number of such days in November between 1977 and 2013.



The study found that Gauteng usually experiences about three and a half days in November when a station records more than 50mm of rain in 24 hours.

The 2001 figures show how quickly rainfall can build up during the province’s summer storm season.

One station recorded more than a month’s rain

The Highveld receives an average of about 80mm to 100mm of rain during November, while the eastern escarpment receives around 150mm.



The 200mm recorded in southern Gauteng on 26 November exceeded those typical monthly totals in a single day.

However, the figure represents rainfall at one station. It does not mean the entire province received 200mm.

Heavy downpours can bring flooding

Intense rainfall over a short period can overwhelm drainage systems and cause water to collect on roads and in low-lying areas.



The November 2001 rainfall record highlights the risk of localised downpours across Gauteng, where one area can receive a large amount of rain while nearby areas record much less.

The researchers published the findings in a 2018 study examining severe weather over the Highveld.

World.title: Christmas travel nightmare for South Africans in UK
World.content:
South Africans living in the United Kingdom and hoping to fly home for Christmas face a travel nightmare. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South Africans living in the United Kingdom and hoping to fly home for Christmas face a travel nightmare after Norse Atlantic Airways confirmed it is suspending all operations amid a deepening financial crisis.

The Norwegian low-cost long-haul airline announced the suspension shortly before 09:00 local time in an official statement to the Oslo Stock Exchange, where it is publicly listed.

Festive season

The grounding comes just weeks before Christmas, when many South Africans living abroad make the journey home to spend the festive season with family and friends.



With Norse Atlantic suspending flights, passengers who booked with the airline could now face uncertainty over their Christmas travel plans, including the prospect of finding alternative flights at short notice.

The South African spoke to one such traveller, who confirmed that he ‘read about the flight suspensions from London to Cape Town, but hadn’t received notification from Norse Atlantic that his particular flight was suspended’.

The announcement followed hours of speculation about an imminent grounding, after the airline cancelled several flights overnight.



These included services operated for Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) under a wet-lease arrangement.

UK flights affected include London Gatwick to Orlando, Bangkok and Cape Town. This includes the 17:40 flight today back from Orlando to London and the 11:30 flight from Cape Town to London.

Norse Atlantic first launched back in 2022, operating from Oslo to New York followed by its first UK route between London and Gatwick, with fares as low as £219.



Last year, the airline carried 1.84 million passengers, working out to more than 150 000 a month.

Norse Atlantic suspends all operations

Norse Atlantic had warned earlier in the week that its liquidity position was critical and that it was urgently seeking new funding to meet its short-term financial commitments.

In its latest statement, the airline said its board was still considering several options to secure additional financing in a last-ditch effort to save the business.



These include a possible takeover by an external party, an option reportedly under consideration for several months.

The airline is also negotiating with bondholders over an outstanding $52 million senior secured bond.

Bankruptcy now a possibility

The airline’s financial situation has deteriorated to the point where it has suspended all operations while its board continues to explore rescue options.



If negotiations with potential investors and bondholders fail, Norse Atlantic is expected to file for bankruptcy.

The suspension is a major blow to passengers who had planned to use the airline for long-haul travel during the busy Christmas period.

South Africans affected by the grounding will need to contact the airline or their booking provider to establish what options are available for their flights and whether refunds or alternative arrangements can be offered.



Passengers should also check the terms of their travel insurance, particularly where policies cover airline insolvency or disruption.

A difficult time for long-haul budget travel

Founded in 2021, Norse Atlantic operated Boeing 787 Dreamliners on long-haul routes, seeking to offer lower fares between Europe and destinations including the United States and other international markets.

However, the airline had been facing significant financial pressure, with rising operating costs and difficulties sustaining the low-cost long-haul model.



Its suspension leaves passengers with Christmas travel plans facing uncertainty at one of the busiest times of the year.

World.title: Nomathamsanqa Mthembu elected uMhlathuze mayor
World.content:
RICHARDS BAY - The uMkhonto weSizwe Party's (MKP) Nomathamsanqa Mthembu has been elected uMhlathuze Local Municipality's new mayor.

The ANC's Phiwa Mhlongo has been elected Speaker of the municipality.

The pairing comes after the MKP and ANC's coalition deal in the municipality.

World.title: Kieswetter calls for intergovernmental coordination  to curb cross-boarder crime
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former South African Revenue Service (SARS) Commissioner Edward Kieswetter is calling for stronger intergovernmental cooperation to tackle cross-border crime.

He was testifying at the Madlanga Commission on Thursday.

He outlined the weaknesses in law enforcement and intelligence coordination.

Kieswetter told the Commission he is confident the revenue collector can uncover the truth and connect the dots in its investigations.

He also complimented the Commission, saying that it is an institution the country can be proud of.

"I know Commissions get a lot of criticism, but it is going a long way to ensuring that the harm currently being caused is being attended to," he said.

World.title: South African pilot reportedly captured by rebels in DRC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) is investigating reports that a South African pilot has been captured by armed rebels in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

DIRCO says it has received reports of the alleged capture but has not yet confirmed the pilot’s nationality or the circumstances surrounding the incident.

According to the Mail & Guardian, the pilot has been identified as Cape Town-based Alexander Villette, who was reportedly captured by rebels linked to Joseph Kabila’s Front pour la Refondation de la Nation.

READ | Dirco demarches Bozell over Trump administration demands

The group claims that a military aircraft was shot down over Minembwe on Sunday, killing two of the four people on board.

It alleges that the two survivors, identified as South African and Ugandan nationals, were foreign mercenaries working alongside the Congolese military.

The reported capture comes amid escalating fighting in eastern DRC, raising further concerns over the worsening security situation in the region.

World.title: Two teenagers drown in separate Mpumalanga incidents
World.content:
MBOMBELA - Two teenagers have drowned in separate incidents in Mpumalanga following heavy rains that have left rivers and waterways flooded.

Police have recovered the body of a 17-year-old boy who went missing while fishing earlier this week.

In a separate incident, a 15-year-old boy was swept away while attempting to cross a flooded river on Wednesday. Authorities are continuing their search for the teenager.

READ | Motorist rescued after vehicle swept away in Joburg flooding

The incidents come as heavy rainfall continues to affect parts of the country, increasing the risk of flooding and dangerous conditions around rivers and waterways.

Authorities have urged residents to exercise extreme caution and avoid crossing swollen rivers or entering flooded areas, warning that fast-flowing water can pose a serious threat to life.

World.title: All SA swimmers in Beijing after funding challenges
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - No South African swimmer has had to withdraw from the World Aquatics Swimming Championships.

The championships will take place between 1 and 6 December in Beijing, China.

Swimming South Africa had previously announced that athletes would have to foot the bill for their travel to Beijing themselves. This is as the federation was unable to pay for athletes to participate.

Each of the 20 swimmers would have to pay up R55,000 out of their own pockets to go to the championships. Fortunately Curro and FNB jumped in and paid for all the expenses.

Swimmers and coaching teams had their official send-off on Thursday at OR Tambo International Airport.

World.title: Nepal moves to declare dead those still missing after August floods
World.content:
KATHMANDU - Nepal has begun a process to legally declare dead thousands of people still missing after its catastrophic summer floods, authorities said Thursday, three months after the disaster.

A high-altitude glacier on the Nepal-China border collapsed on 26 August, unleashing a torrent of water, ice, rock and debris.

In Nepal, the floods killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,500 missing.

"We have started the process to declare the missing dead by verifying their details," Ram Bahadur KC, spokesman for the disaster management authority, told AFP.

Authorities have issued public notices naming about 4,000 missing people, including 623 foreign nationals, and asked for objections or corrections before formal declarations are made.

Additional names can be added following further verification, with the government expected to issue death declarations once legal procedures are completed.

The move follows a change in Nepal's laws last month, reducing the waiting period to declare disaster victims dead from 12 years to around six weeks.

The flood was one of the deadliest disasters in the Himalayan nation's history.

Despite weeks of rescue operations involving hundreds of workers combing through mountains of mud and debris, only a handful of missing people were found alive.

Just 112 bodies have so far been identified and returned to their families.

The absence of death certificates has left many families unable to claim compensation, transfer property or settle other legal matters.

Some relatives have already held symbolic cremation ceremonies for those whose bodies have never been recovered.

World.title: Mlambo-Ngcuka’s remains expected in Eastern Cape ahead of burial
World.content:
EAST LONDON – The remains of former deputy president Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka are expected to arrive in the Eastern Cape on Thursday morning as she makes her final journey home.

Mlambo-Ngcuka died on Friday, 20 November, aged 71, following complications from a recent medical procedure.

She is expected to be laid to rest in eXesi on Saturday, with President Cyril Ramaphosa expected to deliver the eulogy.

At the time of her death, she was serving as Chancellor of the University of Johannesburg.

Preparations for her arrival were still underway on Thursday, with family members making their way to King Phalo Airport to receive her remains. The body will then be transported to a local mortuary ahead of Saturday’s funeral.

Earlier this week, Mlambo-Ngcuka was remembered at a memorial service held at Our Lady of Lourdes Catholic Church in Rivonia, Johannesburg.

Her brother-in-law, Vuyani Ngcuka, said preparations for the funeral were well underway.

“We are expecting a cross-section of people because Phumzile was accessible to everybody and she was loved by the youth and the elderly, especially in this community. We are expecting traditional and church leaders,” said Ngcuka.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Tshwane councillors elect new mayor
World.content:
PRETORIA - Tshwane’s political future hangs in the balance as newly elected councillors meet on Thursday to choose the city’s next mayor, speaker, deputy mayor and chief whip.

But with no agreement yet among political parties on who should lead the capital, negotiations are expected to play a key role in shaping the city’s new administration.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) emerged as the biggest party with 74 seats, followed by ActionSA with 48 and the African National Congress (ANC) with 44.

However, none of the parties secured an outright majority, meaning they will need to find coalition partners to form a government and take control of the City of Tshwane.

The incoming administration faces a series of pressing challenges, including persistent water shortages, electricity problems and ageing infrastructure.

World.title: NTSA steps up surveillance as 300,000 drivers face licence suspension
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

NTSA Director General Nashon Odhiambo in partnership with the National Police service,unveils 'Msimu Bila Ajali' initiative in Mlolongo along Mombasa road. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At least 300,000 motorists risk losing their driving licences within the next seven days as the National Transport and Safety Authority (NTSA) moves to crack down on speeding and other traffic violations ahead of the December festive season.

The authority says the suspensions will target drivers whose vehicles have been flagged for speeding through its surveillance and instant fines systems but who have neither paid the penalties nor lodged complaints against them.

Those affected include private motorists, public service vehicle (PSV) drivers and commercial vehicle operators.

NTSA Director General Nashon Kondiwa announced the impending crackdown on Thursday during the launch of the Msimu Bila Ajali campaign at Mlolongo Weighbridge in Machakos County. The initiative aims to prevent road deaths during the December holidays.

Kondiwa said the authority had recorded more than 1.7 million traffic violations involving drivers and vehicles in the past 30 days, with speeding accounting for approximately 740,000 cases.

He described the figures as alarming, warning that NTSA would no longer tolerate reckless behaviour on the roads. He said the enforcement measures were intended to save lives rather than punish motorists.

"Speeding alone we have had 740,000 violations related to speed. Now we are going to have a raft of actions that we believe will change the way we behave on our roads because I think speeding is a choice," he said.

The NTSA boss said drivers whose licences are suspended would have to undergo fresh driving tests before being allowed back on the roads. The tests would establish whether they have the necessary skills and discipline to operate vehicles safely.

He said the authority had already suspended 15,000 driving licences in the past month over speeding and reckless driving, with commercial vehicle drivers accounting for the majority of those affected.

"If you know you have an instant fine, you have not paid and you have not lodged any complaint about it, we are going to suspend that licence until that issue is resolved and the only way to unsuspend your licence is to come back for a test," Kondiwa said.

He added: "We will really check if you are really a trained driver and if you know what you're doing on the road and the only way we can tell that is through testing." NTSA officers conduct inspection at Mlolongo on Mombasa Road ahead of the festive season. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The authority will not publicly disclose the identities of affected motorists due to data protection requirements. However, each driver will receive an individual notification, with the suspension status reflected in the NTSA enforcement system.

The crackdown will also target 25,000 vehicles whose inspection status is set to be suspended over suspected tampering with speed limiters.

Kondiwa said investigations had established that some commercial vehicles fitted with speed limiters were still recording excessive speeds, raising concerns that the devices had been interfered with.

NTSA will also intensify surveillance of public transport operators, particularly those undertaking night journeys, as well as motorcycle riders, whom Kondiwa identified as a major contributor to road fatalities.

To strengthen enforcement, the authority has rolled out a new application for traffic police officers following a training session in Naivasha on Wednesday. The application will provide officers with more comprehensive information on drivers and vehicles, enabling them to establish compliance beyond checking physical driving licences.

Kondiwa said enforcement would increasingly be intelligence-driven, using data collected through surveillance systems, corridor officers and other government agencies rather than relying solely on roadside inspections.

He warned that enforcement would continue beyond the festive season, saying motorists would no longer be able to evade checks by hiding their vehicles whenever officers conducted operations.

He also acknowledged the possibility of motorists challenging the enforcement measures in court but maintained that public safety would remain paramount.

On broader road safety challenges, Kondiwa said enforcement alone would not resolve the country's accident crisis. He called for increased investment in road infrastructure, public education and the elimination of accident black spots.

He said addressing 290 identified black spots remained a major challenge, with estimates from the Kenya National Highways Authority indicating that approximately Sh2.8 billion would be required to address some of the infrastructure deficiencies.

For the festive season, however, NTSA will prioritise enforcement and public awareness as longer-term interventions to improve road design and infrastructure are pursued.

"Road safety is a shared responsibility but compliance is not negotiable," Kondiwa said.

World.title: Wetang'ula orders CCTV review as Sabina Chege renews missing phone
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula has ordered a fresh review of CCTV footage capturing a member of Parliament allegedly picking up a mobile phone during a confrontation in the House in June 2023, following renewed demands by nominated MP Sabina Chege to have her device returned.

Wetang’ula, who chairs the Powers and Privileges Committee, said he would recuse himself from the proceedings and appoint another MP to review the recordings and present findings to the House, in a move aimed at ensuring the matter is handled appropriately.

“As your Speaker, I will take the following action. Although I am the Chairperson of the Powers and Privileges Committee, I will recuse myself from chairing this matter. I will forward the CCTV footage to the Committee and appoint another Member to act on my behalf, review the footage and present a report to this House,” he said.

The decision follows fresh revelations by Chege, who told Parliament that she had never recovered her phone, which allegedly disappeared during the confrontation involving several female legislators on June 8, 2023.

Chege narrated how she realised the device was missing after her colleague, Rosa Buyu, picked up her handbag while coming to her rescue during the altercation.

She said the phone was a newly purchased iPhone 16, barely a week old, and that she immediately raised the alarm but was assured by officers from the Sergeant-at-Arms that it could not disappear within the parliamentary chamber.

“That phone was an iPhone 16, Mr Speaker. I had just bought it. It was actually one week old. I had colleagues who were around me, whom I even asked to give me back my phone,” she said.

Chege explained that she was advised to seek medical attention following the confrontation and subsequently tracked the phone from Nairobi Hospital, where its location initially showed that it was still within Parliament.

She said the device's location later shifted to an area around Protection House, near Bunge Towers, before it was eventually traced to Donholm.

“When I got to Nairobi Hospital, we tracked my phone and established that it was still within Parliament. An hour later, its location had changed to an area near Protection House and Bunge Towers. The next day it was tracked somewhere in Donholm and from that time I did not get my phone,” she said.

The nominated MP said she reported the incident to parliamentary police, the Clerk of the National Assembly and the House Powers and Privileges Committee but had yet to recover the device.

“I want to say, till today, I have never recovered my phone,” she told the House.

Chege appealed to Wetang’ula to identify the person captured in the CCTV footage or ask them to return the phone before the current parliamentary term ends.

“To save the image of this House, please name the person. At least my phone should be returned,” she said, adding that a colleague had previously claimed to know who took the device but declined to disclose the identity.

However, her remarks triggered sharp exchanges, with some legislators questioning the manner in which the matter was being presented and warning against damaging Parliament's reputation.

Homa Bay Town MP Millie Odhiambo dismissed the incident as an issue that should not be elevated into a question of institutional integrity, arguing that members could contribute towards replacing the device.

“You can make a WhatsApp group and donate a phone for her. Don't tarnish the name of Parliament because you are a crying baby. You make people think Parliament steals people's properties,” Odhiambo said.

Ruaraka MP TJ Kajwang expressed concern that the allegations risked further damaging the reputation of legislators, saying the House needed to address issues that had become associated with its members.

“I have been in this House for 15 years. I do not want to end my term and request a renewal of my term with a tag of a thief,” he said.

Kajwang added that allegations circulating about MPs, including claims of selling recruitment opportunities, were damaging public confidence and needed to be addressed.

Lamu East MP Ruweida Obo also weighed in, declaring that most legislators did not engage in stealing other people's property.

“Sisi wengi si wezi, sisi hatuibi cha mtu na chetu hatutaki kiibiwe,” she said.

Wetang’ula, in his defence of the decision to review the footage, maintained that the recordings would help establish what happened and clear members who may have been wrongly implicated.

He clarified that he had not declared any legislator a thief, but had only indicated that CCTV footage showed a male member picking up a phone from a seat after the altercation.

“The Speaker never said there was a thief. The Speaker said a member took the phone. It is not right and morally comprehensible for anyone to take another person's property without their consent,” he said.

He cautioned MPs against relying on social media speculation and artificial intelligence-generated images to accuse colleagues, saying the CCTV review would provide an opportunity to establish the facts.

“It is easy and juicy to go on social media and use AI and amplify things and call people names. The CCTV will absolve everybody,” he said.

World.title: Ledama Ole Kina court battle over Sh1.2m dispute takes new turn
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina has been granted a stay of execution in a Sh1.2 million compensation dispute with former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken.

The court has given the senator an opportunity to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The Employment and Labour Relations Court, sitting in Nairobi, issued the orders on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and scheduled the matter for mention on February 18, 2027.

The development follows a protracted legal dispute arising from Rotiken's dismissal, in which the court awarded him Sh1,220,737.61 in compensation.

During Tuesday's proceedings, Ole Kina sought between 30 and 45 days to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The court subsequently granted a stay of execution pending further proceedings in the matter.

In a statement, Rotiken's lawyer, Tonge Yoya, said the stay of execution did not invalidate, overturn or extinguish the original judgment, insisting that the senator remained legally obligated to settle the award.

The claimant's legal team also told the court that it intended to challenge pending applications by Ole Kina, arguing that some of the issues had already been determined in previous proceedings.

The lawyers said an application dated November 19, 2026, seeking to amend a preliminary objection filed on September 25, 2026, was directed to be served upon them.

Ole Kina was further directed to file and serve written submissions on the preliminary objection within 14 days.

The objection is anchored on the doctrine of res judicata, which bars parties from reopening matters that have already been conclusively determined by a competent court.

Rotiken's lawyers contend that a previous application by the senator seeking a stay of judgment was dismissed on April 24, 2026, and argue that subsequent applications touching on the same issues should not be entertained.

However, the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) is considering a request to release funds to settle a court-awarded compensation to Zakayo Rotiken, a former employee of Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina, in a labour dispute that has resurfaced following a dramatic confrontation between the senator and auctioneers.

In a letter addressed to the parties in Employment and Labour Relations Court Cause E165 of 2021, Rotiken versus Ledama Ole Kina, the Commission confirmed that it had received a request seeking the release of funds to settle the decretal sum and costs awarded by the court.

The letter signed by the Commission's Director of Litigation and Compliance, Anthony Njoroge, states that the request has been placed before the Commission for consideration, with a decision expected once deliberations are concluded.

"The Commission's decision shall be communicated to you as soon as the Commission has concluded its deliberations on the matter," reads part of the letter.

The development comes against the backdrop of a viral video showing Senator Ole Kina threatening to shoot a female auctioneer who had gone to repossess a milk delivery lorry belonging to his Enkanasa Cow Milk Company over an outstanding financial obligation.

The confrontation sparked public outrage, with questions emerging over the circumstances surrounding the attempted repossession and the senator's conduct towards the auctioneers.

The dispute is linked to a labour case filed by Rotiken, who had been employed by Ole Kina before his dismissal. The former employee moved to court seeking redress over his termination, resulting in a monetary award against the senator.

The dispute stems from a court case filed by former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken against Senator Ledama Ole Kina at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Nairobi. The court awarded Rotiken KSh 1,220,737.61 in compensation following his dismissal.

The latest communication from the Parliamentary Service Commission signals that the institution is considering facilitating settlement of the court award, although it has not yet made a final commitment to release the funds.

World.title: Ruto backs Didmus Barasa for Bungoma governor in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa with President Ruto at a political rally in Mt Elgon during the President’s development tour in the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has thrown his weight behind Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa in the race to succeed Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka in 2027, setting the stage for a contest over the county's political leadership.

During his ongoing tour of Western Kenya, the President rallied support for Barasa, signalling his preference for the legislator in the battle for control of Bungoma County after the next General Election.

Barasa has expressed confidence in securing the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party nomination, citing his development record and grassroots mobilisation in Kimilili as the foundation of his gubernatorial bid.

The MP has urged Bungoma leaders aligned with Kenya Kwanza to unite behind his candidature, arguing that a common political front would strengthen the region's bargaining power within the national government.

He said he intends to replicate his development model in Kimilili across the county's 45 wards, prioritising healthcare, education and youth empowerment.

“I want to take the development model we have implemented in Kimilili and extend it to all the 45 wards in Bungoma. Our people deserve better healthcare, improved education infrastructure, functional vocational training centres and quality early childhood education facilities,” he said.

The legislator pledged to strengthen county hospitals, improve the availability of medicines and expand access to healthcare services at the grassroots.

He also promised to invest in vocational training centres to equip young people with practical skills for employment and entrepreneurship, while improving Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE).

Barasa identified agriculture, trade, infrastructure and youth entrepreneurship as key sectors requiring investment to unlock Bungoma's economic potential. He said his proposed administration would prioritise accountability, efficient use of public resources and improved service delivery.

His bid has received backing from a section of county leaders, including Senator Wafula Wakoli of Ford Kenya and Webuye East MP Martin Pepela.

However, Ruto's apparent preference for Barasa has attracted opposition from Sirisia MP John Waluke, who has questioned the endorsement and instead declared support for Westlands MP Tim Wanyonyi, who is associated with the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM).

Waluke argued that Bungoma residents should determine their next governor without external political influence.

“Bungoma belongs to its people, and the people must decide who will lead them in 2027. We cannot allow the gubernatorial contest to be determined through political endorsements from outside. Residents must be given the freedom to choose a leader who represents their interests,” he said.

The contest is also unfolding amid political differences between Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, adding to the competing interests shaping Bungoma's succession politics.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.
