World.title: PM Radev says EC’s proposal that Bulgaria be fined over excessive deficit is unfair
World.content:
Prime Minister Roumen Radev said on November 26 that European Commission’s proposal that Bulgaria be fined for its excessive budget deficit is unfair, given the country’s efforts to improve public finances and that other EU countries are also in an excessive deficit procedure but are failing to reduce it.

Radev, speaking to reporters on arrival for a special two-day meeting of the European Council said that Bulgaria was the first for which such a fine is proposed under the new European rules, and he described the reasons as procedural, not political.

“I see purely procedural reasons, because for the first time there is a change in the rules for sanctioning, and for the first time this is happening precisely with the arrival of the Bulgarian budget,” Radev said.

“Don’t forget that this is not a standard budget, it came in August. That’s how we found ourselves – the change in the political situation, the elections in April, a new government in May, a budget only at the end of July,” he said.

“So for the first time our budget encountered a change in the rules. And they are that the fines were much larger. Over 10 times larger and many countries before us had excessive deficits and they were sanctioned under this old procedure,” Radev said.

“But because it has a large ceiling on fines, it has never come to actual fining. Now the ceiling is very low, you know, 0.02 per cent. But we are the first country to come with an excessive deficit under these new rules.”

This fine is “symbolic” in financial terms, Radev said.

“But it is of course reputational and is used with great enthusiasm by the opposition in Sofia, which is actually the reason we got here.”

Under no circumstances will we fulfill the opposition’s nihilistic dreams of having European funds and payments under the Recovery and Resilience Plan stopped, he said.

“There is no question of this at all and it will definitely not happen. Because Bulgaria is very clearly implementing a strict financial policy in our face and this is appreciated. There can be no question of any suspension of EU funds. This is a standard procedure that was necessary due to an excessive deficit and exactly at the moment when our budget was released. So things are clear there.”

According to Radev, the European Commission gave a positive assessment of the government’s measures for the 2027 Budget.

“That is, the assessment of our Budget, which we are making for 2027, is positive and encouraging, that Bulgaria, with the measures taken in this budget, is already starting to significantly reduce its deficit,” Radev said.

“Otherwise, it is unfair, it is unfair, because we have the largest gradient of deficit reduction from 2026 to 2027. And I expect that there will still be reason here, because we should be encouraged for reducing the deficit with such a gradient, while there are other countries that simultaneously have an excessive deficit and fail to reduce it at all. The procedure will be activated for them next year as well.”

The European Commission must analyse its abilities to realistically assess the financial situation in the member states, Radev said.

“Why did the European Commission suddenly find that Bulgaria has such an excessive deficit?” he said.

“How did it suddenly find that we have macroeconomic imbalances? But excuse me, these macroeconomic imbalances do not happen in three months, nor in six months. They accumulate over years.

“How did the Commission now find out that budget funds are being spent indiscriminately in Bulgaria, without the necessary control? How did Bulgaria suddenly, in April and May of last year, lower its inflation enough for the convergence report to be published,” he said.

“And in August, inflation again went beyond any criteria. There are things here that the European Commission must analyse in terms of its ability to realistically assess the financial situation in the member states. If it does not do so, it means that there are political motives, not economic ones, behind our admission to the euro zone.”

Radev commented on what Bulgaria’s position will be in discussing the EU budget.

“There are three important pillars of our demands,” he said.

“First of all, we must not back down from cohesion, we know that this is the main instrument for the unity of the union, for the economic development of the union.

“Second, we insist on clear financial support for the Black Sea region, and not just mentioning it. We all know how much countries like Bulgaria and Romania are involved in the actions in the Black Sea, especially with the attacks on merchant ships,” he said.

“These are significant costs for us and they must be taken into account. Next, this is the refusal of own resources based on the European emissions trading system and tobacco excise duties. For us, this approach is unacceptable because it harms Bulgaria disproportionately. These are our lines of action under this budget.”

“What we are negotiating with President Antonio Costa is a plus for Bulgaria. At least as far as our income in the European budget is concerned. And the amount is not small at all, so I really hope we can find a good balance that will benefit our country.”

He was skeptical that an understanding will be reached on November 26.

“There are many contradictions that we need to iron out. But I rely on the will and responsibility of all member states so that we can reach a consensus. Our view is that the budget must be achieved within this year. So that from 2028 we can already work on this new financial framework.”

Bulgaria wants to implement a new approach to the Ukrainian loan, as Bulgaria is ready to be included in the budget for non-military support, Radev said.

“I want there to be a very clear difference between Bulgaria and Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary. Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary have refused from the very beginning and are not part of the countries that guarantee this loan. From the very beginning. Both 2025 and 2026. They said ‘no’ from the very beginning and are not.”

“While the government of Zhelyazkov and then confirmed by the government of Gyurov, we have so far been guarantors of two loans – 45 billion from last year, 45 billion from this year,” he said.

“That is, Bulgaria has already undertaken to be a guarantor for a loan of 90 billion and we pay the interest within the framework of the general European budget on these loans,” Radev said.

“The question is from now on for next year, the request for another 45 billion for a loan. At our explicit insistence, and I am glad that this is already being accepted by the European institutions and by Antonio Costa, we will also talk today with Mrs. Von der Leyen, but she has already expressed support for our position that this loan is divided into two components.

Twenty-five billion euro goes to military support and 20 billion for budgetary non-military support, he said.

“We are ready to join in non-military support and with a clear request that our support as guarantors go specifically targeted to the areas with a compact Bulgarian population from our historical community,” he said.

“We have over 300 000 Bulgarians in Ukraine. They need healthcare, they need heating, electricity, transport, so I hope the European Commission will accept our approach, which we will insist on, because we, on the other hand, cannot abdicate from our obligations as a state and as a society to our historical diaspora, to our compatriots in Ukraine.”

Radev also commented on the EC’s request to ban Russian athletes from participating in competitions in Europe, as part of the proposed 22nd package of sanctions against Moscow.

“Not just about athletes. We’re also talking about tourism related to sports events and activities, even cultural events. And I think we’re going too far to politicise sports and cultural events in this way. So we have our reservations there,” Radev said.

World.title: Bulgarian Parliament approves draft 2027 Budget package at first reading
World.content:
Bulgaria’s National Assembly passed the 2027 Budget Act at first reading late on November 25, with 126 MPs from Prime Minister Roumen Radev’s ruling Progressive Bulgaria group in favour and 81 opposed.

Earlier in the day, MPs also approved at first reading the health care and pensions budgets, which are separate from state budget and part of the Budget package.

Given Progressive Bulgaria’s majority of 131 MPs in the 240-seat National Assembly, the Budget is expected to pass without much difficulty well before the end of the calendar year 2026.

If that is indeed the case, it would be a rather rare occurrence in Bulgaria’s most recent parliamentary history, where political instability resulted in eight elections in five years, producing short-lived parliaments that often adopted budgets very late. Of the last five Budget packages, only the 2024 Budget Act was passed before the end of the previous calendar year.

The 2027 Budget package tabled by the Cabinet envisions a consolidated fiscal programme with revenues of 51.07 billion euro and 55.97 billion euro in spending, with a target deficit estimated of 4.91 billion euro in real terms, or 3.5 per cent of gross domestic product (on a cash basis, rising to 4.2 per cent with additional defence spending).

The economic growth target set in the Budget is 2.5 per cent and sets the debt ceiling at 44.4 billion euro, with the government allowed to issue 8.6 billion euro in new debt in 2027.

World.title: PM Radev, Finance Ministry, try to shift blame as Bulgaria faces possible fine over excessive deficit
World.content:
Prime Minister Roumen Radev and his Finance Ministry have tried to shift blame on to previous governments as Bulgaria faces a possible fine because of its inaction to address the excessive deficit.

Radev’s comments at a November 25 regular meeting of the Cabinet came nine days after he told his ministers to stop blaming previous governments.

The Bulgarian government information service quoted Radev as telling the November 25 meeting: “Yesterday, the European Commission slapped a resounding slap on everyone who over the years spent recklessly without attracting investments, who borrowed without developing the economy, lied about the real deficit to get us into the euro zone, and led the finances to an excessive deficit and catastrophe”.

According to Radev, the European Commission’s good forecast for next year “is a clear confirmation that the course taken by the government to restore state finances is correct”.

“So we will not fulfill the nihilistic dreams of the opposition to stop our European funding and payments under the RRP (Recovery and Resilience Plan),” Radev said.

Radev said that the government “will continue with the reforms and the elimination of inherited inefficient and corrupt practices in public enterprises”.

“Since the beginning of the year, foreign direct investment has increased by more than 100 per cent, and this percentage is increasing even more,” he said (In fact, going by Bulgarian National Bank data, as reported by The Sofia Globe, the increase in FDI in January – September 2026 is about 66 per cent on an annual basis).

A statement by the Finance Ministry on November 24, when the European Commission announced its recommendation that Bulgaria should be fined, offered similar arguments.

“Today’s assessment by the European Commission (EC)—part of the European Semester’s Autumn Package—points to a significant deviation from the recommended trajectory for net expenditure for 2026, as well as the risk of sanctions for failing to comply with the Council’s recommendation of July 10 2026,” the Finance Ministry said.

“This situation is a direct consequence of accumulated systemic problems and the political crisis of recent years—issues for which all political forces bear shared responsibility,” the ministry said.



According to the Finance Ministry “it is important to clarify that such a sanction has no bearing on the fifth payment under the Recovery and Resilience Plan, nor is it expected to block funds from European sources”.

“The government will continue to restore the state’s financial stability, while strictly safeguarding key social commitments, support for vulnerable groups, and predictability for citizens and public services,” the ministry said.

“The responsibility now lies with the National Assembly—we expect all political parties to demonstrate statesmanship during the adoption and implementation of the 2027 Budget, so that the flawed practices leading to EU sanctions may be consigned to the past once and for all,” it said.

Of the eight governments that Bulgaria had between January 2017 and January 2026, while Radev was president, he appointed four as interim administrations. Of those four, one was in office for 308 days, from 2022 to 2023. It was headed by Gulub Donev, who currently is Radev’s Finance Minister.

Assen Vassilev, leader of opposition party We Continue the Change and a former finance minister, alleged that Radev was lying, saying that the evidence was in the reports of the European Commission on the economy and finances of Bulgaria in the years before 2026.

Vassilev said that the European Commission report clearly states that the 2026 Budget is the one with a problematic deficit.

This budget was written by the Radev Cabinet and adopted by the Progressive Bulgaria MPs – even though the opposition in the form of We Continue the Change and Democratic Bulgaria had warned that it could lead to European sanctions for refusing to optimise spending.

“If there weren’t 1.5 billion euro more for expenses to support the administration, we could easily have a 4.1 per cent deficit, which with the derogation for military spending would have allowed us not to enter an excessive deficit procedure,” Vassilev said.

The derogation to which he was referring is an EU decision that allows a deficit above the three per cent ceiling in the euro zone if the expenditure that leads to it is in the field of defence. The exception is due to the threat to European security from Russia and the war it is waging in Ukraine.

The European Commission said that it also has concerns about the draft Budget for 2027 and will monitor Bulgarian finances closely in the first six months after January 1 due to the risks facing the economy.

Vassilev said that the European Commission’s reports on Bulgaria for each year are public and none of them have mentioned an excessive deficit or a problem with the financial framework.

So far, Bulgaria has not been sanctioned for unbalanced finances, as the Commission is now threatening.

Vassilev said that next year’s Budget, currently at first-reading stage in Parliament, is “even worse” than the criticised Budget 2026, because “it hits the foundation of the economy, investments and consumption and will bring us a recession”.

He again called for the draft Budget to be withdrawn by the Finance Ministry and revised. And for a new version to be submitted “by different Finance Minister”.

(Photo: government.bg)

World.title: European Parliament approves 2027 EU budget
World.content:
In a vote on November 25, the European Parliament gave its final greenlight to the last annual budget of the 2021-2027 EU long-term budget framework.

In the 720-member European Parliament, the 2027 budget was adopted by 406 votes to 184, with 69 abstentions.

In a deal reached on November 11, the European Parliament and member state governments agreed to set the overall level of commitment appropriations (legal promises to pay in the same year or later) at 199.7 billion euro, and payment appropriations (actual payments made to beneficiaries) at 211.5 billion euro.

In commitment appropriations, this sets the 2027 budget at 0.99 per cent of the EU’s gross national income (GNI).

The European Parliament secured an additional 300 million euro for its priorities compared to the European Commission’s proposal, boosting investment in research, transport and energy networks, Erasmus+, civil protection, border management, military mobility, the EU’s neighbourhood, and humanitarian aid. The deal also includes stronger cybersecurity and security capabilities for the EU institutions and delegations.

Key increases compared with the European Commission’s proposal include 39 million euro for the EU’s Southern and Eastern Neighbourhood, 30 million euro for humanitarian aid and 30 million euro for border management and migration.

MEPs secured more research funding through Horizon Europe with 21.5 million euro extra, and for transport and energy networks an additional 22.5 million euro.

For education, the Erasmus+ programme receives an additional 14 million euro and the civil protection mechanism is reinforced by 13.5 million euro.

Further increases support military mobility (10 million euro), and climate and environmental action (10 million euro).

The 4.9 billion euro NextGenerationEU over-run costs are to be dealt with as agreed previously through a “cascade mechanism”, designed to manage the borrowing costs and protect flagship programmes.

The amount allocated to servicing the Ukraine Support Loan debt is set at 650 million euro, in line with the European Commission’s proposal.

The European Parliament, Council and Commission have also acknowledged in a joint statement the possibility of covering the loan’s debt service costs by mobilising the Ukraine Support Loan special instrument in 2027.

As The Sofia Globe reported previously, the Council of the European Union formally adopted on November 23 the EU’s budget for 2027.

World.title: Bulgaria’s capital creates special Christmas in Sofia events website, with version in English
World.content:
Sofia municipality said on November 24 that it has created a special Christmas in Sofia website, where everyone can easily and conveniently find information about holiday events and experiences in Sofia in one place.

After doubling its Christmas decorations last year, Sofia municipality continues to upgrade the city’s festive look, the statement said. This Christmas, Sofia will shine with even more lights, with new and updated decorations along some of the capital’s most iconic streets and boulevards, it said.

For the first time, there will be Christmas decorations on Tsar Osvoboditel Blvd, and Knyaz Alexander Dondukov and Cherni Vruh boulevards will welcome the holidays with renewed decorations.

Sofia municipality will also complete the decoration of Georgi S. Rakovski St., which began last year, by doubling the scope of the holiday decorations.

Additional Christmas lights will also be in front of St. Nedelya Church, and the German Christmas Market will also contribute to the festive look of the city with additional decorations.

On December 1, Sofia mayor Vassil Terziev will light the lights of Sofia’s large Christmas tree in front of the St. Alexander Nevsky cathedral. Festively decorated trees will delight Sofia residents on St. Nedelya Square, Macedonia Square and in front of the National Palace of Culture, the municipality said.

The Christmas train will be among the special experiences for the little ones and will await its passengers at St. Alexander Nevsky Square from December 2 to January 3.

The English-language version of the Christmas in Sofia website is to be found at this link.

(Photo: robspratt/ freeimages.com)

World.title: Opposition lashes Radev’s government over EC recommendation to fine Bulgaria over excessive deficit
World.content:
Opposition parties lashed Prime Minister Roumen Radev and his government on November 24 after the European Commission said that it was recommending that Bulgaria be fined for non-compliance with EU fiscal rules through its excessive deficit.

The Commission is proposing to EU finance ministers, who will meet on December 11, that Bulgaria be fined, as well as steps taken to freeze EU payments to Bulgaria.

This is an extremely serious and bad sign that the Bulgarian government received today, opposition GERB-UDF MP and former finance minister Temenuzhka Petkova said.

“When the European Commission says that Bulgaria’s case is particularly serious in terms of non-implementation of measures related to the excessive deficit procedure, this means nothing other than a lack of trust, a loss of confidence by the European Commission in the Bulgarian government,” Petkova said.

Radev’s Progressive Bulgaria has managed to make the worst-case scenario for the country’s public finances come true, she said.

“Such a thing has never happened before. Bulgaria is facing a sanction that could reach 0.02 percentage points of the country’s GDP and this will happen very soon – on December 11. Then the European Commission will submit a proposal to Ecofin, which the Council will vote on for a sanction against Bulgaria. This is a very bad scenario,” Petkova said.

Democratic Bulgaria MP Ivailo Mirchev said: “This fine signals a lack of confidence in the government”.

“We had been warning for weeks that this would happen. Yet, when we issued these warnings, government ministers claimed it was impossible. To prevent the fine from being imposed, two-thirds of the EU finance ministers would have to vote against it. In practical terms, that is impossible,” Mirchev said.



“While the amount of the fine itself is not particularly large, it carries a symbolic message: Bulgaria is an unreliable partner within the euro zone—it fails to honor its commitments, neglects fiscal discipline, and is taking no steps to get its budget in order,” he said.

Mirchev said that Democratic Bulgaria had put forward concrete proposals to bring the deficit below three per cent as early as the 2027 Budget, but these were rejected by Progressive Bulgaria.

Assen Vassilev, leader of We Continue the Change and a former finance minister, said that the government had received a “sound slap” from the European Commission regarding the 2027 Budget.

“Due to its incompetence, Bulgaria will have to pay a 25 million euro fine. The same 25 million that was not found for the doctors’ salaries,” Vassilev said.

“Unfortunately, the fine is the smallest problem. This Budget is leading the economy into recession, and the price will be paid by Bulgarian citizens,” he said.

“Withdraw the three budget laws. Reconsider them from scratch and introduce a competent budget that does not lead the economy to collapse,” Vassilev said.

On the Bulgarian Parliament’s website, the draft Order Paper – yet to be voted on – showed the first reading of the Budget in the National Assembly pencilled in for November 25.

World.title: EC is recommending Bulgaria be fined for non-compliance with recommendations against excessive deficit
World.content:
The European Commission is recommending to the Council of the EU that Bulgaria has taken no effective action to implement recommendations against its excessive deficit and should face a fine, European Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis told the European Parliament on November 24.

Speaking at the start of a debate on the European Semester autumn package, Dombrovskis said that two member states, Bulgaria and Hungary, are at risk of material non-compliance with EU fiscal rules already this year.

“For these two member states, we find that the responses to the EDP (excessive deficit procedure) recommendation have been insufficient and constitute particularly serious cases of non-compliance,” Dombrovskis said.

This warrants a stepping up of the procedure, he said.

“The Commission is therefore recommending the Council to adopt the decision under Article 126.8 of the Treaty that establishes that no effective action has been taken,” Dombrovskis said.

“This would also lead to the first steps in the process of macroeconomic conditionality. And for Bulgaria, as a euro area member state, will trigger a fine of up to 0.02 per cent of GDP,” he said.

Dombrovskis briefed the sitting on the alert mechanism report, “our screening device to identify countries where an in-depth review is needed to assess potential macroeconomic imbalances”.

The Alert Mechanism Report (AMR) is a screening exercise to detect potential macroeconomic imbalances that could affect individual member states, the euro area or the EU as a whole. It marks the start of the annual Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure cycle, identifying member states requiring in-depth reviews

to assess whether they are affected by macroeconomic imbalances that call for policy action.

This year’s alert mechanism report calls for in-depth reviews for five member states, for Hungary, Italy, Slovakia, and Romania, which are already identified in the previous cycles as experiencing imbalances or excessive imbalances, and as well for the first time, Bulgaria, he said.

In a statement on November 24 on the European Semester autumn package, the European Commission concludes that an in-depth review should be undertaken for Bulgaria “based on concerns regarding a widening current account deficit, fast-deteriorating cost competitiveness, and high house price growth combined with significant household borrowing”.

World.title: Ivan Anušić’s New 24-Year-Old Adviser Earns More Than a Retired General
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – Ivan Anušić’s new 24-year-old adviser Nina Mikulandra will allegedly earn more than a retired general. She is otherwise the vice-president of the Šibenik-Knin County HDZ Youth.

Defence Minister Ivan Anušić has seven special advisers. Ilko Cimic reports for Index that the highest individual net earnings among them will go to the newest member of his team, 24-year-old Nina Mikulandra, a recently graduated political scientist and vice-president of the HDZ Youth of Šibenik-Knin County. Her net salary will amount to around €1,850, which is more than the fees received by retired generals, war commanders and Anušić’s other advisers. No previous work experience was required for the position she holds. According to official data from the Ministry of Defence (MORH) analysed by Index, the highest fee among the previous advisers, €1,700 net, is received by Ivan Hampovčan. Željko Živanović, Božo Kožul, Ivica Ušljebrka and Luka Bandalo each receive €1,100, while Zvonimir Gvozdanović advises the minister without compensation.

The form of engagement also differs. Mikulandra is employed in the minister’s cabinet for a fixed term, at the latest until the end of his mandate, while the other advisers, according to the MORH form, are engaged with an advisory fee and without an employment relationship. We looked at who Anušić’s advisers are, what experience they have, how much they’re paid and what they are actually responsible for.

from the university classroom to the minister’s cabinet

Mikulandra graduated in political science this year from the Faculty of Political Science in Zagreb. She is the vice-president of the county HDZ Youth and a member of the Youth Council of Šibenik-Knin County. She was appointed Anušić’s special adviser on the 20th of November, following a procedure in which nine candidates met the competition conditions. No previous work experience was required for that position. Experience in the defence system, state administration or security policy was not required either. The only condition was a completed appropriate master’s degree in the field of social sciences.

MORH explains her selection with her academic results and performance at the job interview. They state that she completed her studies with the highest praise, summa cum laude, and that she received the Dean’s Award twice, both times with a grade point average of 5.00. She is also attending a postgraduate specialist study in “Security Policy of the Republic of Croatia.” According to the Ministry’s response, she showed the best competences and motivation at the interview. The final decision on the appointment was made by Minister Anušić.

what will she actually do for the salary?

The basic gross salary of the new adviser is €2,794.50. With residence in Zagreb and without additional tax reliefs, that would mean around €1,850 net. The competition lists support tasks for the minister, advising, preparation for strategic planning and cooperation with the media. At the same time it is stated that the person in that position is not a civil servant and “does not perform tasks within the competence of the Ministry of Defence.” MORH replied to Index that her tasks will include “support to the minister and assistance in the implementation of the established policy of the Government of the Republic of Croatia.” They did not, however, specify concrete projects she will take on or the results expected of her.

The best-paid adviser from the previous list, Ivan Hampovčan, is a law graduate and former secretary of Osijek-Baranja County. He was appointed to that position back in 2017, when Anušić became county prefect. Earlier he worked at the RODA development agency in Antunovac, the municipality Anušić ran before moving to the county. Since May this year, Hampovčan has also been listed in the register of the Commission for Deciding on Conflict of Interest as the director of the county Pharmacies Srce. For advising the defence minister he receives €1,700. The MORH form states that he is engaged for “drawing up analyses and opinions and giving advice on individual issues within the competence of the defence sector.” Which issues those are is not explained in the document.

retired generals and commanders receive less than 24-year-old loyal hdz member mikulandra

Željko Živanović is a retired major general and Vukovar defender. He took part in the defence of Vukovar and after the war held positions in the military education system. MORH lists him in official announcements as a special adviser to the defence minister. For that work he receives €1,100. The same amount is received by Božo Kožul, the former commander of the 1st Guard Brigade “Tigers.” During the war he held command duties in that unit and was retired back in 2001. Ivica Ušljebrka, a retired colonel and wartime member of the 4th Guard Brigade “Spiders,” also receives €1,100. He was an adviser during the term of Minister Damir Krstičević and remained in that position under Anušić. For none of them does the official MORH form state a concrete area of work; descriptions of their duties are limited to drawing up analyses and giving opinions and advice on issues within the defence sector.

the director of a state-owned company is also among the advisers

Anušić is also advised by Luka Bandalo, whom the state agency ALAN, responsible for trade in arms and military equipment, presents as its operational director. For advice and opinions on issues within the defence sector he receives €1,100. The only one who, according to the official list, advises the minister without compensation is Zvonimir Gvozdanović, a doctor of dental medicine and director of the Vukovar Health Centre. He too is engaged for drawing up analyses and giving advice on individual issues within the competence of the defence sector. What those issues are cannot be determined from the MORH form.

there was also a former journalist among the ranks

It should certainly be noted that Mikulandra is not the first person Anušić employed as a special adviser in his cabinet. That position was also held after his arrival at MORH by former journalist Iva Puljić Šego. In January 2024 the Ministry confirmed to Index that she was appointed after a competition published on 22 November 2023, also for support tasks for the minister and at the latest until the end of his mandate.

Puljić Šego is no longer a special adviser but is listed by MORH as a civil servant employed within the Ministry of Defence system. As a reminder, Minister Anušić said in Parliament that it was he who had leaked information, not his associate and MORH spokesperson Iva Puljić Šego, who after an investigation by the Military Security and Intelligence Agency (VSOA) lost her NATO security clearance.

World.title: Fake Doctor Defrauds Zagreb Woman of 9,000 Euros
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – A fake doctor has defrauded a Zagreb woman of 9,000 euros, and it turns out the police are already well aware of the individual in question.

Zagreb police have been met with another case of fraud in which the perpetrators posed as no less than doctors. Index reports that they convinced a Zagreb woman that a member of her family needed urgent surgery, after which she handed them 9,000 euros. Police suspected a 42-year-old man for the fraud, who is already in investigative detention for allegedly committing fraud previously.

His currently unknown accomplice has not yet been located. According to police suspicions, the two men contacted the 70-year-old woman by phone and misled her into believing that a family member of hers needed urgent surgery that had to be paid for. The woman believed their story and handed the money over to the 42-year-old.

he was previously arrested at the croatian-serbian border

This is a man against whom the police have already filed criminal charges multiple times for various criminal offences. Back in October, together with a 70-year-old man, he was arrested at the Bajakovo border crossing while attempting to exit Croatia into Serbia. Police suspect them of defrauding a 69-year-old woman from Zagreb’s Susedgrad district, whom they convinced that her daughter had been injured in a traffic accident. Material damage in that case amounted to around 50,000 euros. During a search of his vehicle, police officers found a hidden pouch with money in a portable cooler, which they suspect came from the fraud.

police have issued a public warning

The police have repeatedly warned the general public about scams in which perpetrators pose as doctors and exploit their fear for family members. They therefore advise people to never hand over any money in the event of such a call, to verify the information with family members, and to notify the police immediately. A special report has been filed against the 42-year-old with the competent state attorney’s office, and the criminal investigation continues.

World.title: Mate Rimac Recalls His Argument With Volkswagen Over Bugatti
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – Croatian entrepreneur Mate Rimac recalled his intense argument with Volkswagen over Bugatti in a recent interview with the Classic Driver portal.

In an interview for the automotive portal Classic Driver, Mate Rimac revealed previously lesser-known details about the acquisition of Bugatti and fierce disagreements with the leaders of the Volkswagen Group regarding the future of the French car brand. Index reports that according to his recollection of events, the Germans initially wanted the successor to the Chiron to be an electric SUV with four seats, and later insisted on an all-electric hypercar. Rimac, who built his career precisely on the development of electric hypercars, opposed their plans. He also recounted how he went from being a potential manufacturer of the new Bugatti to acquiring the entire company, reports Motor1.

volkswagen allegedly wanted an electric suv

The story began back in 2020, at a time of great enthusiasm in the automotive industry for electric vehicles. The Volkswagen Group was then considering the possibility of Bugatti’s Chiron being succeeded by an all-electric SUV with four seats. Rimac’s company participated in the development of the electric powertrain for that car, which was supposed to use technology developed for the Nevera. However, it soon became apparent that the realization of the project would be extremely demanding and expensive. For such a car, it was not possible to use any of the existing platforms, so Volkswagen would have to invest billions in developing a completely new one. The project ultimately didn’t prove to be economically viable and as such did not get the green light from the German management.

“why don’t you just take over the entire company?

Since Bugatti did not have a viable plan for a successor to the Chiron, Rimac saw a business opportunity in this. He proposed to the leaders of the Volkswagen Group that his company take over the development and production of the entire car, while Volkswagen would be in charge of its sales. At one of the meetings, he received an answer he did not expect.

“Why don’t you just take over the whole company?” one of the Volkswagen Group leaders asked him.

Rimac initially thought it was a joke. Upon returning home, he didn’t even mention the offer to his associates. However, a few months later, the same man called him and asked why he hadn’t gotten back to him. Only then did Rimac realise that the offer was serious. Negotiations followed that lasted two and a half years.

“i had an extremely serious argument with them”

When the question of Bugatti’s future came up during the negotiations, the leaders of Volkswagen and Porsche told Rimac that the next Bugatti hypercar had to be all-electric. Considering that Rimac had by then developed the electric hypercars Concept One and Nevera and collaborated with major car manufacturers on the development of battery technology, such a choice seemed logical at first glance.

However, Rimac believed that this would be the wrong move for Bugatti. “I had an extremely serious argument with them because I thought it was the wrong move for Bugatti. I said: ‘No, I don’t want to make an electric Bugatti,'” he recounted.

The Volkswagen Group eventually agreed to the development of a car with a hybrid power-train, but in order to reduce costs, it wanted to keep the existing Chiron platform. Rimac opposed this proposal as well. He believed that adapting the existing structure of the car to batteries would require too many compromises. Even before the completion of the negotiations on the acquisition of Bugatti, his company financed the start of the development of a completely new gasoline engine with its own money in collaboration with the British engineering company Cosworth. To test the feasibility of the project, engineers first built a prototype engine with only four cylinders, or a quarter of the planned V16 engine. This allowed them to test performance and emissions and estimate the costs and time required for development. The results, it seems, were good enough for Rimac to convince the other participants in the project of his vision.

now, all the new bugatti units have been sold

The result of multi-year development was the Bugatti Tourbillon, unveiled back in 2024. Instead of an all-electric power-train, it got a new naturally aspirated 8.3-litre V16 engine combined with electric motors. Six years after the start of development, Rimac says his decision paid off. Bugatti has, according to his words, already sold all units of the Tourbillon it plans to produce. Motor1 also points out the irony of the whole story. The man who developed one of the fastest electric cars in the world ended up being the one who convinced the leaders of one of the world’s largest automotive conglomerates that their most prestigious brand should not switch to an all-electric power-train.

World.title: Resolution on Vukovar Undergoes Five Changes
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – The resolution on Vukovar will undergo five changes, and now the liberals will support it as well. Here’s all you need to know.

Political groups in the European Parliament have reached an agreement on the text of a resolution marking the 35th anniversary of the fall and destruction of Vukovar. Index reports that five amendments have been incorporated into the proposal initiated by Croatian MEPs, including a reference to the apology by former Serbian President Boris Tadić at Ovčara and a change in the wording regarding the responsibility of political and social actors in Serbia.

Following the compromise reached, the resolution has also been supported by the liberals from the Renew Europe political group, who had previously submitted their own proposal. The European Parliament will therefore vote on a single agreed text in Strasbourg on Thursday, according to Večernji list. The original proposal, initiated by HDZ MEP Karlo Ressler and supported by all Croatian MEPs, was backed by four political groups: the EPP (People’s Party), the Social Democrats, the Conservatives and the Greens.

the five changes

In the final proposal, the formulation about Milošević’s Greater Serbian aggression against Croatia is retained, but the tribute to the victims is expanded to include the victims of other wars during the violent breakup of Yugoslavia. The text also includes the 2010 visit by the then Serbian President Boris Tadić to Ovčara, when, accompanied by the then Croatian President Ivo Josipović, he paid tribute to the victims and apologised for the crimes committed. The importance of reconciliation and clarifying the fate of the missing is also emphasised. The third change stresses that the families of missing persons of all nationalities are still waiting for information about the fate of their loved ones. The fourth change concerns the part of the resolution dealing with responsibility for fomenting ethnic tensions and hostilities through ultra-nationalist rhetoric and the idea of Greater Serbia. Instead of the previous formulation about Milošević and members of the Serbian political and social establishment, influential individuals from Serbian analytical, political and intellectual circles are now mentioned alongside Milošević.

The final change is terminological. Instead of “Territorial Defence of Serbia,” the resolution will refer to the Serbian Territorial Defence.

the alternative proposal is now also supported by non-governmental organisations

The agreement was preceded by disagreements over the content of the resolution. Representatives of Serbian students publicly opposed the proposal of the Croatian MEPs, while seven human rights organisations from the former Yugoslavia supported the alternative text submitted on behalf of the liberals by Austrian MEP Helmut Brandstätter. Among these organisations are the Croatian Documenta and the Serbian Humanitarian Law Centre. Their joint statement was also published by Serbian human rights activist Nataša Kandić. The organisations called for the resolution to also mention Serbian civilians killed or missing in Vukovar before the start of the siege of the city. They advocated equal criteria towards all countries in the region in confronting the wartime past and individual responsibility for war crimes. Unlike the proposal of the Croatian MEPs, the alternative proposal did not mention concentration camps in Serbia.

what are the demands of serbia?

The proposal of the Croatian MEPs calls on Serbia to open wartime archives, provide information on the locations of mass graves, cooperate in the prosecution of war crimes and adopt a law on missing persons. The aim of the initiative is to make the suffering of Vukovar part of the common European historical memory and to emphasise the importance of establishing responsibility for war crimes and clarifying the fate of the missing. If adopted, it will be the first resolution of the European Parliament specifically dedicated to the suffering of Vukovar. The resolution is not legally binding, which means that its adoption will not in itself introduce new conditions for Serbia’s potential membership of the European Union.

World.title: Garcia and Dendoncker Look Ahead to Sint-Truiden at Poljud
World.content:
Hajduk hosts Belgian side Sint-Truiden at Poljud on Thursday, November 26, at 21:00 in the fourth round of the Conference League league phase.

The match was set to be behind closed doors after UEFA punished the club for crowd trouble at the Ajax game, but the governing body later allowed children aged 8 to 14 to attend. Around 8,000 children have registered, and they will sit in the east stand.

Hajduk trained in the rain on Wednesday without Marko Livaja. Speaking at the pre-match press conference, coach Gonzalo Garcia confirmed the striker is out of the squad with back pain.

Hajduk go into the game on the back of a league win over Lokomotiva, a result that took them to a record 32 points.

“We’re working hard, we worked hard before as well, and now we’ve brought in new players, and we’re ready to keep going like this,” Garcia said. “Our main goal was to get into Europe, but we want to compete on several fronts.”

Garcia also addressed the change of coach at the Belgian club.

“They changed their coach recently, so we don’t know exactly what to expect from them, but we know what we expect from ourselves. They have good, quality players who run a lot, but we’re ready for the game. Pressure isn’t a problem for us. We know how to handle it.”

Hajduk have shown this season that they can respond under pressure.

“A good team has to know how to read a game, and we are a good team. The players know what they need to do. Everyone is ready to play, and they know they have to do their job on the pitch depending on what the opponent does.”

The support from the stands will be missed.

“It’s a shame we’ll be playing without our fans, but we’ll play our game regardless,” he added.

Belgian midfielder Leander Dendoncker joined Garcia at the press conference and was asked about the competition for places in midfield.

“I like playing as a central midfielder most of all, but it’s up to me to be ready whenever the coach needs me, in whatever position he needs me,” Dendoncker said. “I arrived at Hajduk injured, and the recovery has taken longer than I expected. At a club playing as well as Hajduk are, it’s hard when you have to compete for a place.”

Dendoncker arrived in Split at the very end of the transfer window.

“I had a good feeling about it, and it seemed like a good project. I’m happy, it’s lovely here, and life here is very good. The sun, the sea, the beaches, good restaurants. I think Split has the best atmosphere of all the clubs I’ve played for.”

Hajduk in Europe so far

After three rounds, Hajduk are 13th with two wins and a defeat. They made a superb start to the league phase with a 2-1 win over Ajax at Poljud, followed it with a 1-0 win away to Thun, then suffered an unexpected 1-0 defeat to Lincoln Red Imps in Gibraltar.

Jonas De Roeck has been in charge of Sint-Truiden since November 6. They beat Iberia 1999 and Midtjylland and drew with Brann in their last match, and their seven points put them 10th in the table. hajduk.hr

The match officials are from Italy. Matteo Marchetti will referee, assisted by Giovanni Baccini and Khaled Bahri, with Giovanni Ayroldi as fourth official. Rosario Abisso is on VAR, with Matteo Gariglio as assistant VAR.

World.title: What Can We Expect of the Croatian Economy in 2027?
World.content:
November the 25th, 2026 – What can be expected of the Croatian economy in 2027? Three key points in particular stand out according to the prime minister.

Ahead of the parliamentary debate, the Prime Minister said that the Croatian Government is continuing with investments and the protection of living standards, while keeping the general government deficit below three percent of GDP. Poslovni reports that Prime Minister Andrej Plenković stated ahead of the debate on the state budget for 2027 that the government expects economic growth of 2.1 percent, a general government deficit of 2.9 percent of GDP, and a reduction of the public debt ratio to 55.3 percent of GDP.

“This is the 11th budget we are proposing. I think it is ambitious and that it addresses the issue of solidarity of Croatian society in times of crisis,” Plenković said, emphasising that the government continues to manage public finances responsibly. He stressed that the budget for next year has three main priorities: preserving social cohesion, investments and development, and the security and resilience of the state. When asked whether the coalition partners support the proposed budget, he answered affirmatively.

higher expenditure than revenue

According to the official budget proposal, total revenues in 2027 are planned at €37.3 billion, which is two percent more compared with the revised budget for this year. Expenditure is expected to rise by 2.2 percent, to €41.5 billion, so the planned state budget deficit amounts to approximately €4.2 billion. At the same time, the government estimates that the consolidated general government deficit, calculated according to the European methodology, will remain at 2.9 percent of GDP. For next year, a slowdown in inflation to 2.7 percent is also expected, while the public debt ratio should continue to fall.

investments and social spending

According to the government’s proposal, the largest part of budget expenditure will continue to be directed towards pensions, salaries of employees in state and public services, and social benefits. A total of €22.2 billion is planned for these purposes, of which €11.2 billion relates to pensions and pension benefits, €9.2 billion to salaries, and €1.8 billion to social benefits. At the same time, the government is announcing the continuation of investments in transport and energy infrastructure, education, healthcare and projects that should contribute to the competitiveness of the economy.

Special emphasis has been firmly placed on energy security, food self-sufficiency and defence capacities. Plenković believes that such a budget framework enables the continuation of development while preserving fiscal stability, despite global conflicts, energy disruptions and inflationary pressures. The debate on amendments is scheduled for the 30th of November and the vote itself for the 1st of December.

World.title: Ryanair Introduces Additional Seats to and from Croatia for Festive Period
World.content:
November the 25th, 2026 – Ryanair is introducing additional seats to and from Croatia for the upcoming festive period, with strong expectations when it comes to passenger numbers.

The incredibly popular lrish low-cost airline Ryanair has announced that it is introducing additional seats on routes to and from Croatia for this year’s Christmas holidays. Poslovni reports that in addition, it states that it expects to carry more than 103,000 passengers on those routes during the Christmas and festive period. Specifically, for the Christmas holidays Ryanair is announcing more than 26,000 new additional seats on routes to and from Croatia. In this way, the company emphasises, it is responding to “high demand for travel during the festive period.”

Increased demand for travel is expected due to Advent events. Earlier this month, the organisation European Best Destinations (EBD) declared Zagreb the best destination for a short or weekend break in Europe precisely for the Christmas holidays in 2026. Zagreb has been ranked on that list ahead of cities such as Geneva and Edinburgh. The explanation highlights the rich festive offer, atmosphere and tradition of Zagreb’s Advent, which has previously already won European awards. This year, precisely because of these positive reviews, a large influx of tourists is expected, which Ryanair has decided to meet in time.

It should also be added that the portal Ex-Yu Aviation News recently reported that Ryanair plans to increase the number of flights on a series of routes from Zagreb during the summer season of 2027. Passengers will thus have more flights available from Zagreb to some of the more popular European destinations.

World.title: Defence Minister Ivan Anušić Appoints 24-Year-Old HDZ Member as Special Adviser
World.content:
November the 25th, 2026 – Defence Minister Ivan Anušić appointed a 24-year-old HDZ member as a special adviser in his cabinet. The explanation from the ministry has left many raising their eyebrows.

Defence Minister Ivan Anušić recently appointed 24-year-old Nina Mikulandra from Šibenik as a special adviser in his cabinet with a gross salary of almost €2,800. Mikulandra is the vice-president of the county HDZ Youth and a member of the Youth Council of Šibenik-Knin County, where a coalition led by the HDZ is in power.

In the competition for the advisory position, published on the 16th of October, only an appropriate diploma in the field of social sciences was required. No minimum work experience, experience in the defence system, knowledge of security policy, work in state administration, or even knowledge of foreign languages was prescribed. Judging by the results of the tender, Minister Anušić found in Nina Mikulandra a person who will perform “support tasks related to advising, preparatory actions in connection with strategic planning, cooperation with the media and providing assistance in performing the aforementioned tasks.”

“not a civil servant”

The tender for this position also states that “the person who ends up filling the role is not a civil servant, does not perform tasks within the competence of the Ministry of Defence and is not subject to the provisions of the law, other regulations and collective agreements that regulate the rights and obligations of civil servants.” Nine candidates who met the conditions applied for the advertised position. The Ministry of Defence published only their initials and invited them to an interview on the 11th of November. Nine days later Minister Anušić signed the decision appointing Nina Mikulandra as special adviser in the minister’s cabinet for a fixed term, at the latest until the end of the minister’s term of office.

In accordance with the conditions of the competition, Mikulandra is entitled to “a basic salary determined as the product of the coefficient for calculating the salary of the job position, which amounts to 2.70, and the salary calculation base, with the right to an allowance for length of service in the amount of 0.5% of the basic salary for each completed year of service,” as well as the right to return to work with the employer with whom she was previously employed for an indefinite period. This is therefore a gross salary of €2,794.50, without the length-of-service allowance of 0.5 percent for each completed year. Assuming that the young adviser has residence in Zagreb, has no children or additional tax reliefs and has no length-of-service allowance, she will receive around €1,850 net per month. If she remains registered in Šibenik, she will receive around €1,910 net. Starting salaries.

active within her local hdz party

The appointment is based on Article 47, paragraph 3 of the Law on the State Administration System. The commission appointed by the minister invites candidates to an interview in order to determine competences, reasons and motivation, while the final decision is made by the minister himself. Mikulandra graduated this year from the Faculty of Political Science in Zagreb with a master’s thesis on “Transformation of party leadership in contemporary democracies: between the crisis of representation and the rise of populism,” and a few months later she obtained a position in Anušić’s cabinet.

The new ministerial adviser comes from Šibenik and turned 24 on the 28th of October this year. In the previous leadership of the county HDZ Youth she was the secretary, and at the elective assembly on the 27th of November 2025 she was elected as one of the four vice-presidents of the HDZ Youth of Šibenik-Knin County. In addition, on the 2nd of October 2025, the County Assembly elected Mikulandra as a member of the Youth Council of Šibenik-Knin County. She received all 18 votes of the councillors who participated in that vote. As befits, Mikulandra has several photographs with HDZ president and Prime Minister Andrej Plenković.

connected by kickboxing… yes, seriously.

Interestingly, her candidacy is not backed by the HDZ, but by the Kickboxing Club Dalmatino from Šibenik. It may not be unimportant to note that Minister Anušić was also actively involved in kickboxing and later acted as a coach and official. According to the official biography published on the Ministry of Defence website, from 2002 to 2005 he was the president and coach of the Kickboxing Club Antunovac, in a place near Osijek. In an interview for Večernji list back in 2017, Anušić said that he dedicated himself to running a kickboxing club after leaving the army and before entering politics. According to him, 40 children and 18 senior fighters trained in the club.

Anušić was also one of the founders of the Kickboxing Club Antunovac, which was officially registered on the 28th of September 2004. According to data from the Register of Associations, he held the position of president. The club ceased to exist in March 2020, but Anušić’s connection with this sport did not end there. After becoming minister, Anušić continued to participate in events related to kickboxing. In November 2024 he awarded recognitions to members of the Croatian Armed Forces Toni Ćatipović and Antonija Zec for their successes at the European Kickboxing Championship, and in April 2025 he opened the Croatian Championship in the kick light discipline in Osijek.

she won two deans awards

In the Ministry of Defence’s response that later arrived to Index’s enquiry, it is stated that Nina Mikulandra met the only prescribed condition of the  – a completed master’s degree in the field of social sciences – and that she was the best at the interview at which the candidates’ competences and motivation were assessed.

The appointment is also explained in the Ministry by her success at the faculty. “Nina Mikulandra is a Master of Political Science with the highest praise (summa cum laude). She is the winner of two Dean’s Awards, namely for the best student of the master’s degree in Political Science in the academic year 2025/2026 with a grade point average of 5.00, as well as for the best student of the fourth year of the undergraduate degree in Political Science in the academic year 2024/2025, also with a grade point average of 5.00,” the response states. They add that Mikulandra is currently attending a postgraduate specialist study in Security Policy of the Republic of Croatia, which, as they emphasise, is also her area of interest.

The Ministry of Defence says that, “given her academic title, excellent results during her studies, for which she is also the winner of two Dean’s Awards, as well as the area of interest she expressed during her studies,” her tasks will include “support to the minister and assistance in the implementation of the established policy of the Government of the Republic of Croatia.” They emphasise that this is a fixed-term job, at the latest until the end of Anušić’s ministerial term, and that Mikulandra does not have the status of a civil servant. Special advisers are appointed by the minister on the basis of a conducted  by his decision, while the job position, the coefficient for calculating the salary, the salary grade and the conditions for the job position are prescribed by a regulation, the Ministry of Defence concludes.

World.title: Study: No good solutions for insulating fieldstone walls from the inside
World.content:
Insulating old fieldstone walls from the inside can preserve a building's historic facade but risks causing long-term moisture damage, according to new research from the Estonian University of Life Sciences.

"Fieldstone walls are quite common in Estonia. Perhaps less so in northern Estonia, but on the island of Ruhnu, for example, a remarkably large number of fieldstone buildings have survived," said Kadri Leiten, a lecturer at the Estonian University of Life Sciences who recently earned her doctorate. On Ruhnu, for example, people primarily use fieldstone buildings as summer homes because the walls get too cold in winter.

Anyone wishing to use a fieldstone building year-round, however, might want to insulate it somehow. "If you don't want to hide a beautiful facade, you need to find an alternative way to keep the building comfortable inside during the winter months," Leiten explained. In some cases, this means installing insulation on the interior side of the walls.

In her recently defended doctoral dissertation, Leiten assessed how advisable this approach is. Using a wall of the stable at Mooste Manor as a case study, she investigated whether and how an old fieldstone wall could be insulated from the inside using reed or wood fiber boards combined with clay plaster. "Insulating from the inside makes it possible to preserve the exterior facade, but a safe insulation solution has yet to be found," the lecturer noted.

Moisture damage accumulates over time

The fieldstone masonry Leiten studied was at least half a meter thick. Insulating such a wall from the inside makes the masonry colder. "Adding an internal insulation system restricts the flow of heat from the room into the wall," the lecturer explained.

If heat cannot penetrate the insulation attached to the wall, the fieldstone masonry remains cooler. Moisture can gradually accumulate inside the cold wall because the material covering its interior surface prevents the masonry from drying inward. "This can lead to more freeze-thaw cycles, as materials that are already damp are more susceptible to cracking when they freeze," Leiten explained.

In her research, she tested two domestically produced materials for insulating the stable's fieldstone wall: reed boards and wood fiber boards. She used clay plaster as a leveling layer. Short-term experiments indicated that mold might not develop immediately between the masonry and the insulation boards.

Over a five- to seven-year period, however, the model indicated that moisture could still accumulate in the insulated wall. "Unfortunately, based on the results of my research, I cannot currently say that this is a particularly safe method of insulating walls from the inside," Leiten acknowledged.

Old linen warehouse in Puka. Source: Tibukonn/CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

The wall she studied, however, has now been insulated for four or five years. According to Leiten, the coming years will reveal whether moisture actually begins to accumulate as predicted by the model.

"The next step is to investigate what methods could be used to reduce moisture accumulation in the wall. One approach used elsewhere in the world is water-repellent treatment," she said. In Belgium, for example, masonry walls are treated externally with water-repellent coatings, allowing buildings to be insulated from the inside. However, Leiten noted that the climates of Belgium and Estonia are not comparable.

Wetter climate on the way

To assess the climate resilience of wood fiber and reed boards, Kadri Leiten used models developed for the climate of the Vantaa region in Finland. These are also suitable for northern Estonia, as Vantaa's climate is expected to resemble northern Estonia's future climate. "Under an extreme scenario, we would rarely see subzero temperatures in winter anymore. Estonia's long-term climate projections also indicate that temperatures will fall below freezing much less frequently by 2100," the lecturer said. In other words, it makes sense to start designing both stone walls and all other types of walls in Estonia with the expectation of more moisture and rainfall.

Salts can also accumulate in old stone walls, particularly in buildings that have previously served some agricultural purpose. As part of her research, Leiten therefore also investigated how these salts could be removed using clay- and lime-based sacrificial plasters. "The wall is plastered and the plaster is essentially sacrificed. Liquid water containing dissolved salts moves from the masonry into the plaster, which is then removed from the wall," Leiten explained.

Nearly all the sacrificial plasters tested in her study removed salts from the stone masonry. However, another important consideration, according to Leiten, is how easily each type of sacrificial plaster can be removed after use. "Compared with lime-based plaster, clay plaster was generally easier to remove from the wall," she noted.

Leiten advises readers who want to use their fieldstone buildings year-round to exercise caution when insulating them. According to the lecturer, natural materials are not particularly well suited to the task. "Nothing may happen in the first five years after you insulate with clay or reeds. You may simply not be able to see what's happening between the layers inside your wall over the course of 20 years," she warned.

Another option is simply to leave an aesthetically pleasing old stone wall uninsulated. "You might put on some wool socks and a sweater and you'll be fine. For now, leaving the wall uninsulated is a safe option, provided it can dry both inward and outward and the room has ventilation," Leiten said.

Polli Manor stables. Source: Kadri Kroon/CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Kadri Leiten, a doctoral student at the Estonian University of Life Sciences' Institute of Forestry and Engineering, defended her doctoral dissertation, "Long-Term Evolution of Moisture Regime and Damage Risks in Internally Insulated Massive Masonry Walls under Changing Climate Conditions," on November 12. Her dissertation was supervised by Marko Teder, Ph.D. The opponents were Associate Professor Evy Vereecken (KU Leuven, Belgium) and Simo Ilomets, Ph.D. (Tallinn University of Technology, Estonia).

World.title: Watchdog warns bosses not to monitor staff with cameras non-stop
World.content:
Employers cannot use cameras to monitor workers continuously or check their duties, the Data Protection Inspectorate (AKI) warned amid rising workplace complaints.

AKI officials said bosses must disclose camera rules, ban audio or break-room recording and set short deletion limits to meet personal data and defense-of-privacy rules.

Maire Iro-Miller, public relations adviser with the AKI, said workplace cameras have long drawn top inquiries from staff and employers.

"Because the inspectorate receives more complaints every year, we are also seeing quite a few cases involving the use of cameras," Iro-Miller said.

One recent complaint saw a firm using surveillance to track staff continuously, check tasks and verify attendance, without explaining why.

Lawyer Jekaterina Aader said identifiable camera footage counts as personal data processing and so requires a clear lawful purpose and signage.

"Cameras cannot be used for continuous real-time monitoring of employees, to check whether they are at work or to monitor how they carry out their duties," Aader said.

Changing rooms, break rooms, toilets and showers are off-limits, while audio recording is rarely lawful, she noted

"The Data Protection Inspectorate also points out that recording audio in the workplace is even more intrusive and generally does not comply with data protection requirements," Aader continued.

Recordings must be deleted promptly, with justifications growing stricter once 72 hours have elapsed since the recording was made. Access logs and computer-tracking rules also apply.

Europe-wide, video should normally be deleted within days of being captured.

"The European Data Protection Board takes the view that video recordings should in most cases be deleted after a few days, ideally automatically," Aader added.

Workers who suspect unlawful monitoring can file a complaint with the AKI.

World.title: French sports media: Estonian rally driver Robert Virves signed for M-Sport Ford
World.content:
Estonian rally driver Robert Virves has reportedly struck a deal with M-Sport Ford for next season, according to renowned French motorsport magazine Auto Hebdo.

Virves and co-driver Jakko Viilo were crowned world champions in WRC2, the second-tier of the World Rally Championship, this year. Competing in a Škoda Fabia for the Toksport team, the pair contested seven rounds, winning four and finishing second twice.

"In 2026, Robert Virves secured the WRC2 title for Škoda, but according to our information, the Estonian has decided to go his own way and join the M-Sport Ford project," Auto Hebdo wrote Wednesday. "This would be one of the biggest stories of the winter transfer season."

M-Sport would be familiar territory for Virves, who also competed for the team in 2023. It was his debut season in WRC2, during which the Estonian contested six World Rally Championship rounds. His best result was a sixth-place finish in his class at his home event, Rally Estonia.

Robert Virves talking to ERR. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

M-Sport, which at the top-tier WRC level has been much smaller than the dominant Toyota and Hyundai, has yet to confirm its driver lineup for next season, but has previously indicated that three seats should be available. This year, the team's drivers were Irishmen Josh McErlean and Jon Armstrong. The team will compete in the Ford Fiesta Rally1 Kit, a modified Rally2 car eligible for Rally1 competition.

Virves won the 2022 Junior World Rally Championship and became the first Estonian driver to capture the WRC2 title in 2026 while driving for Toksport WRT. He previously spent a 2023 WRC2 stint with M-Sport Ford and claimed his first WRC2 victory at Rally Estonia in 2025. A move to M-Sport Ford would mark his return to the manufacturer's lineup ahead of the new era.

Norwegian-Swedish driver Oliver Solberg won the overall Rally Estonia in July 2025 while he was still a WRC2 competitor. In Estonia he raced in a one-off Rally1 appearance, before stepping up full-time to Toyota's top-tier lineup for 2026.

Virves' fellow Estonian Ott Tänak is also returning to the senior WRC with Toyota in 2027 after sitting out the 2026 season. The 2019 world champion drove one season for M-Sport Ford too, in 2023, winning two races, in Sweden and Chile.

World.title: Video: Fox found at Tallinn Airport, safely returned to the wild
World.content:
A fox that wandered into Tallinn Airport last week was caught by rescuers and released back into the wild.

"It is true that in the early morning of November 16, a young and apparently quite travel-hungry fox was exploring the baggage area of Tallinn Airport. This time, however, it did not get to take a flight. With help from the Rescue Board, the four-legged travel enthusiast was caught and safely returned to the wild. The fox's little airport adventure ended happily for everyone involved," said Tallinn Airport marketing and communications manager Margot Holts.

A wild fox at Tallinn Airport. Source: Tallinn Airport

Holts said that this time the fox was wandering around the airport's baggage handling area, and at that hour there were no arriving passengers it could have encountered.

She added that the fox entered from the airfield side, not through the main entrance.

Holts said the movement of birds and animals is closely monitored in aviation because their presence in operational areas can pose risks both to flight safety and to the animals themselves.

"From time to time, an uninvited guest finds its way onto our grounds, and young animals in particular may not always be able to find their way back out. In such situations, our goal is to ensure flight safety while also making sure the animal can continue its journey safely," Holts said.

A fox climbed onto a baggage conveyor belt at Tallinn Airport. Source: Majaka - Tallinn FB group

The video source is footage from Tallinn Airport's security cameras, provided to ERR by the airport.

World.title: Interior minister: Border closure will free up 160 officials
World.content:
The closure of Estonia's eastern border will free up 160 officials, some of whom are expected to be reassigned to strengthen the country's southern border, says Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200).

In a written question, Riigikogu Isamaa faction leader Helir-Valdor Seeder asked Taro how many officials and employees are currently engaged in keeping the Estonia-Russia temporary control line border crossings open and how many would become available for reassignment if the eastern border were closed.

"A total of 160 officials work at the Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa border crossings. They will be deployed to other border guard duties. It will still be necessary to provide security at the border crossings and respond to possible incidents. Part of the freed-up resources will be directed toward strengthening surveillance of the land border and implementing compensatory measures at internal borders," Taro replied.

Seeder also asked whether the minister considered it appropriate to redirect resources freed up by a complete closure of the Estonia-Russia control line toward strengthening the Estonia-Latvia border and preventing illegal migration more effectively.

Igor Taro Autor/allikas: Ken Mürk/ERR

"The Police and Border Guard Board is analyzing the resources needed to implement compensatory measures and will use border crossing personnel at internal borders as needed. Controls aimed at preventing illegal migration will certainly be strengthened as a result of these changes," Taro replied.

According to Taro, as of November 20 there were 570 people registered as staying illegally in Estonia. He said 92 people had left the country under enforceable departure orders.

"A further 325 people have left Estonia this year under voluntary departure orders. It is important to note that this figure does not include persons returned to Latvia under EU law, of whom there were 199 as of November 20," Taro added.

239 people were being held at the Police and Border Guard Board's detention center as of November 20.

World.title: Ida-Viru County seeks local training for mental health nurses to ease psychiatrist shortage
World.content:
Ida-Viru County is now facing a critical shortage of psychiatrists, and local governments and health care providers are jointly calling for mental health nurses to be trained locally.

Representatives of local governments and health care providers told the education minister in a letter that Ida-Viru County has long had a shortage of mental health specialists.

They said the situation has now become critical because of changes to psychiatric services, including the end of inpatient psychiatric care at Ahtme Hospital at the end of March next year.

Narva Hospital recorded more than 6,000 outpatient psychiatric appointments in 2022, but fewer than 4,800 a year later. The decline was due to a shortage of specialists, while patients' need for care remained undiminished and the wait to see a psychiatrist exceeded six months.

Health care providers in Ida-Viru County raised the need for local training in mental health nursing two years ago, and the signatories stressed that concrete solutions are now needed.

"With no realistic prospect of rapidly increasing the number of psychiatrists, the region cannot simply wait for more specialist doctors to qualify. At the same time, we need solutions we can put into practice by developing the professional skills of our existing nursing staff," the signatories explained.

They added that when people do not get help in time, their condition can deteriorate further. Alongside their mental health problems, they may struggle to manage daily life, work, study, maintain family relationships and participate in society.

According to the letter, Ida-Viru County has nurses who are willing to pursue further training, but studying in Tartu or Tallinn alongside full-time work and family commitments is difficult and costly, and health care providers cannot spare large numbers of nurses at once for an extended period in another region.

"It is important to bear in mind that healthcare providers in Ida-Viru County cannot spare large numbers of nurses at once to allow them to study in another region for an extended period," the letter says.

Training most mental health nurses locally in Ida-Viru County would allow them to combine study with work, complete clinical placements at local health care facilities and fill needs across psychiatric departments, family medicine centers, specialist care and elsewhere.

Ahtme Hospital. Source: ERR

"Mental health nurses cannot replace psychiatrists or solve the shortage of specialist doctors on their own. But making targeted use of their skills can strengthen team-based care and help patients see the right specialist in time," the Ida-Viru County representatives said.

The local governments and health care providers want the Ministry of Education and Research to work with the Ministry of Social Affairs, Tallinn and Tartu health care colleges and partners in Ida-Viru County to explore training mental health nurses locally through a suitable master's program or another form of study, with a substantial share of in-person teaching in Ida-Viru County and the rest organized flexibly.

The Ida-Viru County Association of Local Authorities and regional health care providers says it also wants to help estimate how many students might enroll, assess employers' needs, identify clinical placement opportunities and evaluate funding options together, including whether funding from the Just Transition Fund could be used alongside other sources.

The letter was signed by the mayors of Alutaguse, Jõhvi and Lüganuse rural municipalities and of Kohtla-Järve, Narva-Jõesuu and Sillamäe, the chair of Narva City Council, and representatives of Ida-Viru Central Hospital, Narva Hospital, Järve Health Center, Corrigo, the Neeme Family Medicine Center, Karell Ambulance Service and the Iidla Family Medicine Center.

Tallinn Health Care College, which was also among the recipients of the letter, said it already plans to launch a mental health nursing specialization in its health sciences master's program in Kohtla-Järve next year and intends to apply for funding from PRÕM+, a program for developing vocational and higher education.

"We do not yet know whether we will receive funding, and that will determine whether the planned training goes ahead," said Tallinn Health Care College rector Ulvi Kõrgemaa.

She added the master's program aims to train specialist nurses with advanced expertise, while general nurses can also provide mental health nursing care within their scope of practice where a specialist nursing qualification is unnecessary.

"That is why we see an important role for continuing education and microcredential courses alongside the master's program in developing mental health nursing care in the region. These can help nurses already in practice develop their skills and improve access to mental health nursing care," Kõrgemaa said.

The Ministry of Education and Research plans to decide its position on the issue by next week.
