The confrontation took place outside Essen NY Deli in Midwood, where Israeli brokerage firm CapitIL was hosting a real estate event.Videos on social media showed physical clashes between protesters, Israeli supporters and police, with demonstrators attempting to breach barricades.The Centre told the Delhi High Court that CJP functionary Saurav Das was stopped at Delhi airport from travelling to London due to a lookout circular issued by Mumbai Police. Das has challenged the action, with his lawyer telling the court that he was not informed about the LOC or its purpose. The court also sought responses from the Regional Passport Officer and the Ministry of External Affairs.

World.title: Accredited vs self-proclaimed: SC to examine protection for journalists
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Thursday referred allegations of police assault, manhandling and wrongful detention of seven journalists covering protests in Delhi in October to a high-powered inquiry committee headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice R Subhash Reddy.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit relevant material before the five-member committee, which will examine the allegations and establish whether the journalists were subjected to police excesses.

The petitions were filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) and the Delhi Union of Journalists over alleged police action against media personnel covering protests on October 10 and 11, 2026.



The demonstrations were reportedly demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Justice Bagchi said the committee would ascertain whether the journalists were present at the protest sites, whether force was used against them and, if so, whether it was excessive in the circumstances.

"You will go back to the committee which we have constituted to factually demonstrate whether your petitioners were, in fact, present there.





If present, whether they were subjected to excessive force," he observed, as quoted by PTI.

The judge added that the committee should examine whether the force used was disproportionate to what was necessary for maintaining public order.

The bench also indicated that it would consider broader constitutional questions concerning the protection available to journalists covering protests and public events, including whether accredited journalists are entitled to greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters.

Justice Bagchi observed that self-proclaimed journalists may not enjoy the same protection as accredited media persons.

Appearing for the journalists, senior advocate PV Dinesh said the seven media personnel worked for established news organisations and were not social media reel-makers.

"We are just journalists, recognised journalists. Allow us to do our work," he submitted.

He also questioned whether journalists working for established media organisations could be taken into custody while performing their professional duties.

"The question is, when established journalists, who are recognised journalists, are covering events, can they be taken into custody?" Dinesh asked, as quoted by PTI.

The court indicated that it would examine the constitutional safeguards available to journalists, including their freedom of movement and right to practise their profession. It would also consider whether forcibly removing a journalist from a location amounts to custody and the legal consequences of such action.

The petitioners alleged that journalists were forcibly removed from reporting locations, prevented from recording events and subjected to physical force despite displaying their press credentials. The allegations also include an attempt to snatch a photographer's camera and the physical assault of a woman journalist while she was reporting live.

The seven journalists named in the petition are Suhail Muhammed and VS Rahul of 24 News, Sajin of Asianet News, Roshni Rajan and Farsana of Reporter TV, Vishnuprasad of Mathrubhumi and Miji P Jose of Manorama News.

The Delhi Police had earlier told the Supreme Court that social media influencers and reel-makers cannot claim the same protections as journalists covering protests.

In an affidavit, the police described journalists as a "distinct category" from social media content creators who use cameras and microphones to make reels for commercial gain. It argued that the latter cannot automatically claim the protections available to the press while reporting from protest sites.

World.title: 'Message to clean-shaven face & head': Owaisi's 'moustache' challenge to Yogi, Akhilesh over CM fight in UP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: AIMIM chief

on Thursday took a swipe at Uttar Pradesh chief minister

and Samajwadi Party chief

, saying neither would become the chief minister after the 2027 assembly elections.

Addressing the Samajik Parivartan Morcha's first joint rally in Lucknow, he said the next chief minister would be someone with a moustache, in an apparent reference to alliance partner Chandrashekhar Azad.

"Someone remarked that this is an alliance between the bearded and the moustachioed. And, in truth, it is. Now, I wish to address that clean-shaven face and the other clean-shaved head, you will not become the CM anymore; it will be someone with a moustache..,"



he said.

Owaisi accused the BJP and the Samajwadi Party of failing to protect the Constitution and ensure adequate political representation for Muslims.

Invoking Dr BR Ambedkar, he said the Constitution guaranteed liberty, fraternity, justice and equality. He accused the RSS and the Sangh Parivar of working against these principles.

"Justice will not come through bulldozers or encounters. Justice will come through Babasaheb Ambedkar's Constitution.





The rule of law will be restored," he said, targeting the BJP government.

He also criticised the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that it was being used to weaken the Constitution.

Targeting the Samajwadi Party, Owaisi accused its leadership of practising caste-based politics and seeking Muslim votes without ensuring adequate representation to the community.

"How many times will we be betrayed? Akhilesh Yadav, will you give a ticket to a Muslim from Karhal?" he asked.

Yadav had won the Karhal seat in the 2022 Assembly elections.

Owaisi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adityanath of promoting communal divisions while failing to address unemployment and concerns over education.

He said the Morcha, if voted to power, would focus on education and employment for young people.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"We will ensure education for young people and jobs after they complete their education. We will make doctors and engineers, and ensure that our students get opportunity to study in IITs," he said.

Referring to the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, Owaisi urged people to support the Morcha's candidates in the 2027 elections.

"The historic opportunity before us is that we should support neither the red cap (of Samajwadi Party) nor the RSS-BJP," he said.

Praising Azad, Owaisi said he could represent the poor, oppressed and deprived sections of society.

"If there can be a chief minister in Uttar Pradesh who represents the poor, the oppressed and the deprived, and whose government will be of the people rather than only a particular section, his name will be Chandrashekhar Azad," he said.

"I am confident that with our unity, prayers and hard work, we will make Chandrashekhar Azad the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh. Together, we will prevent the BJP from forming the government for a third time," Owaisi said.

World.title: Rs 5 canteen, 50% PDA quota in govt contracts: Akhilesh unveils SP's UP manifesto
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief

on Thursday released his party's "PDA manifesto" ahead of the UP assembly polls. The announcement comes on

.

The PDA, a political formulation promoted by Akhilesh Yadav, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).

The SP has indicated that releasing its manifesto months before the polls will allow it to take its proposals to the public ahead of the election campaign.

Here's what Akhliesh Yadav announced

PDA youth will be provided access to higher education through a special state education policy. The issue of paper leaks will be addressed, all examinations will be conducted on schedule, and results will be declared with complete transparency.

Graduate students will be provided employment opportunities. Those who remain unemployed will receive a monthly allowance of Rs 5,000.

The party will provide government jobs to 25 lakh youths and create employment opportunities across other sectors.

Will begin caste-survey across the state to frame policies for the targeted upliftment.

Samajwadi canteens will be set up, where meals will be available for Rs 5 per plate.

Elderly women will receive Rs 40,000 as pension, with the amount transferred directly to their bank accounts.

He said labourers, women workers, artisans to also receive Rs 40,000 annual pension.

Laptops to be distributed again to students passing Class-12 exam, 26,000 primary schools shut by current UP government to be reopened.

For government contracts worth up to Rs 50 crore, 50% reservation will be provided to members of the PDA community.

The party is expected to announce two more detailed manifesto, including district, city and women-centric.

In the party's election manifesto release, Akhilesh Yadav also attacked the rival BJP, saying: "When a few dominant, supremacists and selfish people want to keep their thousands of years of power intact and in that attempt want to not only amend and change but also erase the Constitution - all of us those who love the Constitution should take it up as our national and social duty to unite and thwart all conspiracies to amend the Constitution".



He further said: "Our country will be governed by 'Samvidhan' (Constitution) and not 'Manvidhan' (arbitrariness). There are a few powers who want to do this through 'Manvidhan' and not 'Samvidhan'. There is an ongoing war over Constitution. On one hand, there are those who want to misue the Constitution to come to power. One the other hand is PDA, who wants the rule of social justice of the Constitution, we want to erase all differences, uphold reservation and equality.





.."

Akhilesh Yadav's annoucement comes as relations between

Congress

and his party appeared to sour after the SP jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of candidates for the upcoming polls.

The list was released even as deliberations over a seat-sharing deal were still ongoing between the two parties. To make matters worse, the list included candidates on two constituencies that featured on Congress' wishlist.

Later, SP offered 26 seats to the Congress, which triggered unease on the second day of the seat-sharing talks for the 2027 UP polls between the two alliance partners in Delhi on Tuesday.

According to reports, SPâs offer of 26 seats came after the Congress tabled a list of 120 seats of its choice.

Unease was noticeable in the Congress camp over SPâs 26-seat offer as Saharanpur MP and member of Congressâs negotiating team Imran Masood objected to media claims of SPâs 36-seat offer.

The SP is expected to contest the 2027 assembly elections in alliance with the Congress against the BJP-led govt in UP. The BJP has been in power in the state since 2017, while the SP governed under Akhilesh from 2012 to 2017. The

Bahujan Samaj Party

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(BSP), led by Mayawati, was in power from 2007 to 2012.

The 403-member UP assembly is expected to witness a major contest between the BJP and the SP-led opposition, with alliances and the mobilisation of different social groups likely to play an important role in the campaign.

In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, while its ally Apna Dal (Sonelal) secured 12.

The SP won 111 seats, while its allies also won seats. The Congress secured two seats, and the BSP one. The SP received approximately 32% of the vote in the 2022 polls, emerging as the principal opposition party in the state.

By choosing to release its manifesto on the Constitution Day, the SP has linked the launch of its electoral programme to a day associated with constitutional values and democratic institutions.

World.title: History-sheeter held for brutal assault at eatery
World.content:
Kottiyam police have arrested a habitual offender in connection with the brutal attack on a roadside eatery near Kundara over a dispute regarding the lack of salt in parippuvada. The accused, identified as Kolli Niyas, was taken into custody based on statements from the shop owner and eyewitnesses.

The violent incident occurred on November 10 when Niyas, accompanied by his friend, visited the stall for evening snacks and ordered tea and parippuvada. After tasting the snack, the duo picked a heated argument with the staff, complaining that the snack lacked salt.

The verbal altercation quickly escalated into severe violence and Niyas assaulted the eatery’s employee, Mohanan. Later, the attackers poured boiling oil from the frying pan directly onto Mohanan’s body. When the shop owner, Nasim, rushed to intervene, Niyas stabbed him with a weapon. The assailants then brandished weapons to threaten local residents who tried to step in, before vandalizing the eatery and scattering food items and equipment onto the road.

Local residents rushed the injured victims to a nearby hospital. Mohanan sustained severe burn injuries across his body along with a fractured rib, while Nasim was treated for stab wounds.

The police confirmed that Niyas is a notorious history-sheeter involved in multiple criminal cases. Notably, Niyas is also facing a separate case registered at the Kundara police station for assault. While Niyas is now behind bars, police have intensified their search to apprehend his accomplice who remains at large.

World.title: Constitution is hard earned, we need to protect it, says Congress leader Balasaheb Thorat
World.content:
“Independence, democracy, and constitution is hard earned, we need to create awareness among people. We have to go from town to town, village to village, and create awareness,” said Senior Congress leader Balasaheb Thorat during ‘Samvidhan Bachao Rally’ in Thane.

Mr. Thorat pointed out the need to protect constitution, saying “The institutions of country that protect democracy have been sabotaged, Judiciary is pressured, Election Commission is no more independent.”

Maharashtra Congress on Thursday (November 26, 2026) staged a ‘Samvidhan Bachao Rally’ in Thane led by Harshwardhan Sapkal. During the rally he criticised Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis alleging corruption in preparations of Nashik Kumbh Mela and called him “Jhadkhau CM”.

Calling Mr. Fadnavis Jhadkhau CM (Tree-cutter CM), Mr. Sapkal said, “Jitney Jay tithe khau, Deva bhau (Wherever Deva Bhau go there is corruption).” He added, “What is happening in the state, Pune has become home of crime, farmers are in distress, Nashik Kumbh Mela city has now become a city of corruption, where graft worth ₹36,000 crore has taken place.“

Congress leaders including Satej Patil, Praniti Shinde and Naseem Khan also participated in the rally passing through Court Naka, Khartan Road, Bazar Peth, Tembhi Naka, Kharkar Ali, and Talao Pali.

Congress launched the initiative from Thane, claiming this was the first place where attempts have been made to distort values of constitution. “The previous unconstitutional Government in the State began from Thane itself, and the Supreme Court has also put its seal on that. So, no better place than Thane to sound the call for protecting the Constitution,” Mr. Sapkal stated.

Satej Patil, Congress leader from Kolhapur referred Gokul dairy incident, where his panel won 13 seats against 12 for the BJP-led Mahayuti panel but after the state cabinet approved an amendment to the Cooperative Societies Act allowing the Government to nominate five members to the managing committees, equation changed leading to Mahayuti’s victory.

“If constitution stayed then only the State will sustain. When running the country, constitution needs to be followed, if legacy and ideology of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, Chattrapati Shivaji Maharaj, and Shahu Phule are kept to be alive, then we must struggle and fight.”

World.title: Congress urges CEO to rectify discrepancies in graduates’ MLC draft electoral rolls
World.content:
The Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) has urged Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) C. Sudharshan Reddy to rectify discrepancies in the draft electoral rolls of the Graduates’ MLC constituencies, including the allotment of polling stations and duplicate voter entries.

A delegation comprising TPCC Election Commission Coordination Committee chairman Pulipati Rajesh Kumar, State Special Intensive Revision (SIR) coordinator Gampa Venu and Raghavender met the CEO on Thursday and submitted a representation seeking immediate corrective measures.

The delegation pointed out that several voters had been allotted polling stations 10 km to 14 km away from their residences, despite the availability of closer polling stations.

It urged the CEO to ensure that voters were allotted polling stations closer to their residences to avoid inconvenience and facilitate their participation in the electoral process.

The delegation also drew the CEO’s attention to alleged duplicate entries in the draft electoral rolls published on Wednesday.

It sought physical verification of the electoral rolls through the respective Booth Level Officers (BLOs) to identify and remove duplicate entries and rectify other discrepancies in accordance with the prescribed electoral procedures.

Mr. Rajesh Kumar urged the CEO to take immediate corrective measures to ensure error-free electoral rolls and safeguard the voting rights of all eligible graduates.

World.title: ‘Citizens must discharge fundamental duties to build a better society’
World.content:
Deputy Commissioner Snehal R. on Thursday stressed the need for citizens to discharge their fundamental duties along with exercising their rights guaranteed by the Constitution.

Inaugurating the Constitution Day celebrations organised jointly by the district administration, zilla panchayat and the Department of Social Welfare in Dharwad, she said that fundamental duties are essential for building responsible citizens and a better society.

Respecting the national flag, national anthem and other national symbols, upholding the spirit of nationalism, treating fellow citizens as brothers and sisters and protecting natural resources and maintaining cleanliness are among the responsibilities of every citizen, she said.

Referring to civic issues in the district and also, in the city, Ms. Snehal said that the efforts of the municipal corporation, district administration and zilla panchayat alone cannot bring about the desired improvements without public participation.

Citizens must recognise their responsibilities and contribute to building a clean and orderly society, she added.

The Deputy Commissiner also urged government officials to discharge their constitutional responsibilities with commitment and ensure that public services and welfare facilities reach people without discrimination or based on personal considerations.

Emphasising the values of justice, equality and fraternity enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution, she said that officials must treat everyone approaching government offices equally, irrespective of their social or economic background and ensure that their grievances are addressed in a fair manner.

Three students from Dharwad district, Ankita Putani, Sowmya Byathanala and Arun Sunagar, who secured third place at the State-level Youth Parliament in Mysuru, will be felicitated at a district-level programme, she added.

Earlier, Ms. Snehal, Hubballi-Dharwad Police Commissioner Bhushan Borase, Superintendent of Police Gunjan Arya and other officials and public representatives paid floral tributes to B.R. Ambedkar and Basavanna at Jubilee Circle.

Zilla Panchayat Deputy Secretary Mallikarjun Todalabagi administered the Preamble oath.

Head of the Department of Political Science at Karnataka Arts College Mahadevappa B. Dalapati delivered a lecture on Constitution Day.

Similar Constitution Day programmes were organised in various educational institutions across the district.

World.title: Kayalpattinam records 183.8 mm rainfall; Schools in Tiruchendur taluk closed following heavy rain
World.content:
Thoothukudi District Collector Vishu Mahajan had declared a holiday for schools in Tiruchendur taluk on Thursday, following heavy rain that lashed the region on Wednesday night. The downpour has reportedly caused water stagnation on the premises of several schools in the area. In the past 24 hours, Kayalpattinam recorded a maximum rainfall of 183.8 mm.

According to the Regional Meteorological Centre Chennai, “The trough in easterlies from Gulf of Mannar to the Southwest Bay of Bengal off Tamil Nadu coast now runs from Comorin area to South Interior Karnataka across Tamil Nadu and Keralam and extends up to 1.5 km above the mean sea level.”

In line with the prevailing weather conditions, widespread rainfall has been recorded across Thoothukudi district. Several southern parts of the district received heavy rainfall on Wednesday night particularly Kayalpattinam, Tiruchendur, Kulasekarapattinam, Udangudi and Sathankulam.

The rainwater accumulated in some low-lying areas of the district caused considerable inconvenience to motorists.

The coastal areas near Thoothukudi have also recorded widespread rainfall. As a precautionary measure, mechanised boat fishermen did not venture into the sea on Thursday.

Rainfall recorded in the district during the 24 hours ending at 6:30 a.m. on Thursday are as follows: Tiruchendur 120.3, Kulasekarapattinam 90, Sathankulam 55.8. Manappad 73.2, Ammanpuram 100, Pannamparai 73.2, Thattarmadam 102.4, Thoothukudi 32.4, Srivaikuntam 45.2, Vallanadu 16.8, Kovilpatti 2.4, Vembar 16.8 and Ottapidaram recorded 20.8 mm rainfall.

World.title: Mega job mela in Bukkapatnam on November 28
World.content:
A mega job mela will be held at Sri Sathya Sai Government Degree College in Bukkapatnam on November 28 to provide employment opportunities to unemployed youth in Sri Sathya Sai district.

District Collector A. Shyam Prasad said the recruitment drive, organised by the Andhra Pradesh State Skill Development and Training Department, would begin at 9 am. Several corporate and industrial companies are expected to participate and recruit candidates based on their qualifications and skills.

Interested candidates should register in advance through the Naipunyam portal (https://naipunyam.ap.gov.in/user-registration). They must attend in formal attire and carry their resumes, copies of educational certificates, Aadhaar card and a passport-size photograph.

The collector urged eligible youth to make use of the opportunity. For details, contact 79815 41994.

World.title: BMTC invites bids for 200 mini-buses to improve last-mile Bengaluru metro connectivity and serve narrow roads
World.content:
As proposed earlier, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) has finally invited bids to induct 200 mini-buses to operate as metro feeder services and navigate narrow roads.

The smaller buses are expected to improve last-mile connectivity and address commuter demand for better access to metro stations, particularly in areas with narrow roads that larger buses cannot easily access.

The Hindu first reported in September 2026 that BMTC had been inspecting seven-metre midi/mini-buses for induction into service. According to the tender document, BMTC has invited bids for the supply of 200 fully built seven-metre and 11-metre non-air-conditioned BS-VI diesel city buses.

The procurement is aimed at adding smaller vehicles to its fleet, which can be deployed on routes where operating conventional city buses is difficult.

Read | Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka

“The buses will be built in accordance with the AIS-052 bus body code and other applicable automotive standards. The seven-metre buses should have a minimum seating capacity of 16 passengers, in addition to the driver’s seat, and the 11-metre buses should have a minimum of 39 seats and one additional driver seat,” a senior official said.

Trial operation

The tender outlines a phased delivery schedule, beginning with the supply of one prototype bus within 30 days of the purchase order. This will be followed by nine buses within 15 days, allowing for the trial operation of 10 buses.

Read | BMTC to share real-time bus data with mobility platforms in Bengaluru

“We will conduct a 30-day trial run followed by a 15-day period for evaluation of its results. After the evaluation, the successful bidder will have to supply 40 buses within the next 30 days and the remaining buses within another 30 days. The entire procurement will comprise 200 buses,” official added.

The technical specifications prescribe several safety and passenger-information features. Each bus will have three cameras connected to a mobile network video recorder (mNVR), with cameras positioned to cover the road-facing area, driver and passenger doors, and the interior saloon.

Bus features

The camera system will be capable of transmitting footage to the control centre on demand. In the event of an emergency, pressing the panic button will trigger the transmission of video footage, including 30 seconds before and 30 seconds after the button is pressed, to the backend system.

Read | BMTC to introduce automatic passenger counting system on 30 buses in Bengaluru

The buses will also be equipped with an AIS-140-compliant vehicle location-tracking system and emergency buttons. The automatic tracking device will transmit location data every 10 seconds when the ignition is switched on and once every minute when the ignition is off. An emergency alert will be sent to the designated server, with an SMS alert provision in the absence of GPRS connectivity.

Further, the vehicles will have electronic LED destination boards at the front, rear, left-hand side, and inside the bus, along with a GPS-based next-stop voice announcement system. The specifications also provide for accessibility features, including designated seating arrangements and stop-request switches for passengers using mobility aids.

World.title: IFS probationers learn about Coimbatore Forest Division’s AI-based early warning system
World.content:
The AI-based early warning system for preventing elephant mortalities on railway tracks in Madukkarai forest range of the Coimbatore Forest Division continues to attract Forest Department officials and biologists from different parts of the country to learn about effective use of technology in conservation.

A total of 65 Indian Forest Service (IFS) probationers from the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy, Dehradun, had a field-level experience on the system on Wednesday.

District Forest Officer N. Vengatesh Prabhu explained to the probationers about the system, which has enabled hundreds of safe crossings of elephants and other animals after its introduction in February 2024. No accident involving wild elephants and moving trains has been reported in areas covered by the system since its launch on the Tamil Nadu side.

The probationers visited the control room of the facility in Madukkarai range and towers mounted with AI-enabled surveillance cameras along the railway tracks passing through forest.

The DFO and the staff in-charge of the early warning system also explained the use of three surveillance drones and three tethered drones, which are used as additional layers of surveillance to cover blind spots of camera-mounted towers.

The DFO said that the field level experience of the AI-based early warning system would help the IFS probationers in understanding the effective use of technology in conservation and replicate similar models in their respective areas during their service.

World.title: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen in Islamabad meeting, Khawaja Asif says
World.content:
The Makkah pact nations will discuss the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen when officials from the mutual defence agreement meet in Islamabad on Thursday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told AFP.

Asif said the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting and it is very important”, confirming that defence and foreign ministers from the Gulf kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan would attend.

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact in August, with the three Muslim nations pledging to come to each other’s aid in the event of an attack.

Saudi Arabia has faced repeated barrages by the Houthis in Yemen, with the group targeting cities, oil facilities and shipping since fighting in Yemen’s civil war intensified in July.

“Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear,” Khawaja said on Wednesday, praising Riyadh’s handling of the conflict with the Houthis, who hold swathes of territory in Yemen, including its capital Sanaa.

He said the pact, which was formed during the expansion of the war in the Middle East following US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, was still at a “nascent stage”.

“Initially, we need to have frequent meetings to steer what is being formulated, in a way that in the next couple of months we have everything in place so that we can move forward,” he added.

Khawaja declined to comment on how the pact would react to a direct attack by Iran on Saudi Arabia and identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

“The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and set a roadmap for further agreement on reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz and for negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme.

But the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy to resuscitate the ceasefire, led principally by mediators Qatar and Pakistan.

Khawaja said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”.

World.title: PTI a 'political reality' whose trust in system needs to be restored: Bilawal
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place.

Bilawal, who is on a visit to Punjab for the past few days, made the remarks while speaking at the Multan Press Club. He has made stops in Multan, Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh so far.

Responding to a query about him calling former premier Imran Khan a “political prisoner”, Bilawal explained that he made the “controversial” statement in a polarised political environment, where those terming him a political prisoner could not be convinced otherwise and those declaring him a convict and corrupt could not be convinced otherwise.

Bilawal stressed that in his speech, not the press queries, he made an observation that was not about Imran, but rather about Pakistan’s political history wherein elected premiers often end up going to jail later on or come to power after being imprisoned.

“Whatever opinion you may hold about Khan sahib, even if you think he is not a political prisoner, there is no denying the fact that PTI is a political reality,” the PPP chairman stressed.

He emphasised that even if Imran was considered a “convicted felon or terrorist or whatever”, prisoners in a respectable society were entitled to their rights.

Bilawal said that although the PTI founder “tried to deny my family those rights”, he would not want to continue the cycle of “repeating the same mistakes” in vengeance.

“Khan sahib is a convict, he is in jail, but PTI is a political reality. Until PTI’s trust is restored in this system […] and they are able to play their role in the Parliament, the reset that is being discussed cannot take place in that manner,” he maintained.

The PPP chairman’s latest remarks come amid a growing debate over a “system reset” in the country. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units , arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

In a similar vein, the Bhutto scion on Monday had called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system.

During Thursday’s address, Bilawal reiterated his call to regain the opposition’s “lost trust” in the system and for the government to undertake confidence-building measures to convince it that institutions such as the Parliament, the Election Commission, the courts, and the accountability system could be trusted again.

The PPP chairman highlighted a similar “lack of trust” in the opposition on the government’s part.

“In my opinion, if we truly want this system to serve the public, if we truly want our country, our Pakistan, to be capable of facing every problem, whether they are economic hardships or foreign difficulties, then we will have to take steps as soon as possible so we can establish unity, political stability, and restore trust in all institutions,” Bilawal stated.

“I believe this reset or reboot of our system — whatever words are used — should be in a democratic manner; it shouldn’t be non-political, it should be political,” Bilawal asserted.

He explained that a “political reset” would imply that all political stakeholders would have to be included in the conversation, including the ruling party, its allies and the opposition as well.

“If we want to make the Parliament functional, then all decisions have to be made in the Parliament alone,” he said, adding that decisions taken “outside the Parliament” will leave the system incapable of overcoming challenges.

Bilawal regretted that ongoing discussions in the Parliament, the federal cabinet, seminars, or even television talk shows did not pay attention to the fundamental issues faced by the public.

“People are distressed about managing two square meals. They’re worried whether they should educate their children or arrange medicines for their elders,” Bilawal said.

“Whether it’s a cultivator or a farmer, they are not getting the price for their crops. Labourers and hard workers are not being rewarded for their efforts,” the PPP chairman highlighted.

“I believe that governments, political parties, and political stakeholders across the world have a responsibility to draw attention to this crucial issue of how we can reduce the economic burden on the people.”

Bilawal noted there was “restlessness and distress” among Pakistan’s youth, who faced unemployment and, even if employed, their salaries were spent on just commuting to and from work.

During his address, the PPP chairman also highlighted the importance of a free press, adding that he wanted to restore the “power” previously held by press clubs across the country.

“With your voice, your columns, you used to make and topple governments,” the Bhutto scion remarked. “I don’t want to topple any government, nor do I want to form another one. But I believe your role is to hold up a mirror to those sitting in power,” he added.

The PPP chairman acknowledged that if the media was given space only to regurgitate what those in power talked about among themselves, then issues related to economic crises and difficulties faced by the people at the grassroots level would not come to the forefront.

Bilawal referred to his earlier address at the Karachi Press Club, saying that he did not deny the mistakes made by him over time.

“I am not backing away, I am not claiming that I am, you know, an angel and everyone else is dirty. I admit [we played a] role in this,” he said, adding that PPP’s intention was not to weaken the press.

Bilawal then referred to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), saying that whatever PPP’s intention was, the country had now arrived at a point where press freedom was nonexistent.

In January last year, the National Assembly had rushed the controversial amendments to the country’s cybercrime laws amid protests, with PTI lawmakers and journalists walking out of proceedings. PPP members had voiced their support during the voting.

More to follow

World.title: SBCA chief removed as CM Murad orders sweeping action over building collapse in Karachi's Baloch Colony
World.content:
KARACHI: Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) director general, was removed from both the posts on Thursday on Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah’s directives following the collapse of an under-construction building in Karachi’s Baloch Colony the previous day.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

Regarding Shamshad, the CM further directed that his services be surrendered to the federal government. Moreover, a recommendation should be made to the federal government to suspend Shamshad and order a formal inquiry against him, the CM instructed.

Following CM Murad’s directives, the Sindh government notified Shamshad’s transfer.

The Services, General Administration and Coordination Department’s notification, seen by Dawn, said the BS-21 officer had been transferred “with immediate effect” and directed to report to the same department.

Meanwhile, the chairperson of the Inspection, Enquiries and Implementation Team Department, Bilal Memon, was posted as the Sindh local government secretary with immediate effect and until further orders, another notification by the Services, General Administration and Coordination Department said.

Apart from the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

He further directed that a “comprehensive and transparent” probe be carried out and strict action be taken against any other SBCA employee found responsible.

The statement quoted him as saying that any negligence resulting in the loss of lives or causing suffering to people would not be tolerated.

He said public safety must remain the “foremost responsibility” of every government department and warned that negligence in enforcing building regulations would lead to strict action, the statement added.

Sindh Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hasan Lanjar, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah, Karachi Commissioner Hassan Naqvi and other senior officials attended the meeting.

Separately, CM Murad said during a press conference in Karachi that authorities had halted the construction of 123 buildings that were being built under stay orders.

At least 123 buildings in this city were being constructed under stay orders,” he reiterated.

He added that he had asked the provincial law minister to speak to the chief justice and the court had been requested to decide the cases of those 123 buildings in 15 days.

He said the building that collapsed in Baloch Colony was also being constructed under a stay order.

The chief minister said that the government had identified 16 to 17 SBCA officers and ordered their suspension over misconduct. He added that he had further instructed that a legal case be filed against those officials so that they could be terminated under law and an example could be set.

CM Murad said that he had also ordered the removal of the SBCA chief. He stated that the government had requested the federal government to suspend him.

“We are going to have a reset in the Sindh Building Control Authority,” he announced.

Death toll rises to 4

On Wednesday, a ground-plus-five-storey building with one penthouse, covering 600 square yards, collapsed in Karachi’s Baloch Colony — at a time when over 20 workers were reported to be present at the site.

Officials and witnesses said that the building collapsed when work to dig a borehole was under way. On the day of the collapse, authorities had confirmed three deaths and injuries to 14 others.

The search operation, which was halted on Wednesday night, was resumed on Thursday, and search teams had pulled out another body by evening.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaanul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that the deceased was a middle-aged man, and the death toll had risen to four following the recovery of his body.

The body was recovered hours after Khan told Dawn in the afternoon that an information desk had been set up in collaboration with the East district administration and yjr families of 17 missing individuals had approached it.

On Wednesday, the now-removed East DC told Dawn it had transpired during the initial probe that the SBCA had given the approval for constructing the ground-plus-one-storey building to its owner.

However, the owner allegedly violated the approved plan and constructed six storeys. When the SBCA tried to halt the construction, the owner approached the court and got an order against the SBCA, he said. But the SBCA did not take any action against him.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police five-day physical remand of the suspects.

Additional reporting by Sumair Abdullah

World.title: Govt to limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Thursday announced that it would limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit (kWh) through a forward-looking adjustment on a quarterly basis, instead of Rs2.88 per unit in additional fuel cost it was seeking for December billing.

The Power Division, in a statement, said it has “proposed a Forward-looking Fuel Cost Adjustment (FFCA) mechanism wherein the increase … would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026” over the September FCA.

The statement came while the public hearing was in progress at the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) for an additional FCA of Rs2.88 per unit for electricity consumed in September and its billing in December.

The petition for higher FCA was filed by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) of the Power Division for all distribution companies (Discos), including K-Electric.

During the public hearing, the Power Division Additional Secretary Mehfooz Bhatti said the government as well as the consumers were facing increasing price shocks due to volatility in fuel supplies, particularly in the winters when cheaper hydropower generation dropped substantially.

He said the government had been working hard since the war-related challenges emerged to manage additional FCA shocks within Rs2 to 2.5 per unit through the provision of scarce and expensive imports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) at local gas rates and other efforts.

“We are bringing up a tariff band that provides pricing predictability as always demanded by the industry”, he said, adding that a policy directive had been secured from the government’s appropriate forums.

“The policy guidelines under section 31(4) of the Nepra law would be placed before you latest by tomorrow (Friday) morning. The government has cleared the policy directive covering the October-December period.”

Bhatti requested the Nepra to call an early public hearing if it was necessary to ensure that consumers were insulated from a major price shock and take care of October FCA as well. “This is a government decision,” he said.

Nepra’s member tariff, Amina Ahmed, welcomed the decision and promised to complete regulatory “due diligence as soon as possible”.

“The concept is very welcome,” she said, but added that technical review would follow as soon as the regulator received the formal policy guidance from the government.

The Power Division, in its statement, said the national average electricity tariff inclusive of taxes stood at Rs53.04 per unit while industrial tariff was at Rs62.99 per unit when the current government assumed office in March 2024.

“Through concerted efforts and key policy and reform initiatives, the government successfully reduced the national average tariff by Rs8.76 per unit to Rs44.28 per unit by March 2026, prior to the onset of the Iran-US war and the ensuing energy crisis in the Middle East.

“The reduction in industrial tariffs was even more significant, declining by Rs18.49 per unit from Rs62.99 to Rs44.50 per unit over the same period.”

However, the Iran-US war triggered a sharp increase in international fuel prices, particularly RLNG and coal, exerting upward pressure on monthly FCAs, it said.

“The Power Division closely monitored the evolving situation and implemented a carefully planned and publicly announced load management strategy while optimising the utilisation of available fuel supplies to limit the impact of rising fuel costs on FCAs,” the statement said.

Consequently, during April–September 2026, consumers were protected from a potential additional FCA increase of Rs6–7 per unit, the Power Division claimed.

“The combined FCA and Quarterly Tariff Adjustment (QTA) increase during this period was restricted to an average of Rs2.38 per unit, inclusive of taxes.”

The Power Division said the onset of winter further intensified these challenges.

“A seasonal decline in hydropower generation increases reliance on thermal generation, with thermal fuels accounting for over 80pc of the generation mix during certain winter months. This seasonal shift traditionally results in higher fuel costs.

“In the prevailing circumstances, the elevated international fuel prices following the Iran-US war posed an additional risk of a substantial increase in monthly FCAs.”

Therefore, it came up with the FFCA mechanism wherein the increase due to the above situation would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026 over the September 2026 FCA, the statement added.

Following the requisite approvals, the Power Division will issue policy guidelines to Nepra for the implementation of the FFCA mechanism, it stated.

“These measures reflect the government’s continued commitment to maintaining tariff stability and minimising the impact of external fuel price shocks on electricity consumers,” the Power Division highlighted.

For the business community, in particular, greater predictability in electricity prices provided an improved basis for planning operational costs and business decisions, while reducing uncertainty arising from monthly tariff adjustments, it added.

“The government remains committed to protecting consumers and supporting economic activity during these challenging times.

“The Power Division will continue to closely monitor developments in international fuel markets and take all necessary measures to safeguard consumer interests,” the statement concluded.

World.title: PIA restores UK flight operations after Norse Atlantic disruption
World.content:
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Thursday that it had restored normal flight operations to and from the United Kingdom, a day after two flights were cancelled by wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic as passengers prepared to board.

Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations on Wednesday, saying its financial situation was “critical” and it needed new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

In a press release on Thursday, PIA said: “Flight operations between Pakistan and the United Kingdom have been restored following yesterday’s cancellations by our wet-lease partner.”

The airline said its teams assisted all passengers in both London and Manchester and that passengers affected by the flight cancellations had been re-accommodated on subsequent flights “in accordance with their individual travel preferences”.

“Passengers who opted to alter or defer their travel plans due to the disruption have been facilitated with full, penalty-free refunds,” it added.

The statement said that in line with the contingency plan activated last night, the airline had “transitioned its UK operations directly onto its own widebody Boeing 777 fleet”.

“Today’s scheduled UK services and operations are running on schedule,” the airline added.

In yesterday’s statement, PIA said flights PK786 from London Heathrow to Islamabad, scheduled for 7:55pm GMT, and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore, scheduled for 7pm GMT, were cancelled.

“Notice of this operational suspension was communicated to PIA without any prior warning just as passengers were preparing to board their respective flights in London and Manchester,” the airline’s spokesperson said.

It termed the abrupt suspension of Norse Atlantic’s operations without notice “deeply regrettable” and said it was pursuing the matter with the carrier at the “highest contractual and executive levels”.

PIA was privatised in December last year through an auction. A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for a 75 per cent stake in the airline, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion. The Arif Habib-led consortium had vowed to transform the loss-making airline through operational restructuring, fleet expansion, and improved customer service.

In October, the airline signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aims to meet rising demand.

Following Norse Atlantic’s announcement on Wednesday about its financial situation, its shares plummeted by 76 per cent at 1:03pm GMT. Most of the airline’s market value has already been wiped out this year.

The Norwegian company is now in talks to secure short-term financing, it said in a statement.

“However, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution,” Norse said. It did not say how long it could still operate without new financing.

The carrier, which does not hedge its jet fuel needs, cut capacity as costs skyrocketed following the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February. Many other airlines are faced with the same problem, filing for bankruptcy or initiating restructuring proceedings to survive.

World.title: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl among nine party leaders barred from Sargodha district for 30 days
World.content:
LAHORE: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman is among nine party leaders barred from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha district for 30 days, according to a notification issued by the deputy commissioner.

The development came as the party was scheduled to hold a rally in Sargodha on Nov 26 (Thursday).

The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, states that the restriction was imposed under Section 7(1) of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, read with the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008, and would remain in force for 30 days from Nov 25.

Besides Maulana Fazlur Rehman, whose district is listed as Dera Ismail Khan, the notification names eight other party leaders: Maulana Naseer Ahmad Abrar, Maulana Amjad Khan and Prof Ghazanfar Aziz, all from Lahore; Maulana Safi Ullah from Bhakkar; Maulana Muhammad Noor Khan Hans from Multan; Maulana Muhammad Zakria Shah from Faisalabad; Maulana Muhammad Yahya Abbasi from Muzaffargarh; and Maulana Jamal Abdul Nasir from Dera Ghazi Khan.

According to the notification, the deputy commissioner reviewed a report submitted by the Sargodha district police officer and expressed concerns that the individuals had a history of delivering provocative and objectionable speeches that could threaten public order.

It described them as “firebrand speakers” whose speeches were allegedly provocative and inflammatory, adding that they were likely to assemble crowds unlawfully and incite public sentiment against the state and its institutions.

The order further stated that their presence could create a law and order situation and pose a potential threat to peace and security.

Meanwhile, several senior JUI-F leaders were detained in Sargodha and served notices for allegedly violating Section 144, police said. Several local JUI-F leaders were also detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Khushab district.

Separately, the JUI-F chief, in a video message, said that despite the road restrictions and blockade, he was leaving for Sargodha.

He demanded that the government immediately remove all restrictions, release detained party leaders and workers and ensure that constitutional rights and civil liberties be protected.

JUI-F Punjab spokesperson, Hafiz Ghazanfar Aziz, said the government was continuing its “high-handed tactics” against the party.

Aziz claimed that a large number of party workers had been stranded on the road and that arrests were being made across Punjab, with cases registered against JUI-F activists.

Fazl-govt rift

On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

The JUI-F chief was scheduled to participate in a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association on Tuesday. However, he could not leave his residence in a private housing society on Multan Road due to the deployment of a heavy police contingent.

The development came after tensions persisted between JUI-F and the Centre. Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks .

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

A JUI-F spokesman had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

World.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad, Rawalpindi on Nov 27
World.content:
A local holiday has been declared in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi for Nov 27 (Friday).

A notification issued by the Islamabad deputy commissioner stated that Nov 27 “has been declared a local holiday within the revenue limits of ICT”.

It noted that all essential services would remain operational during the holiday, including the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad, the Capital Development Authority, the ICT administration, Islamabad police, the Islamabad Electric Supply Company, the Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited and hospitals.

Separately, the Rawalpindi deputy commissioner shared a notification on X stating that a local holiday had been declared in the district for Nov 27. He said that all schools, colleges and offices would remain closed.

The notification said that all “emergency dealing departments/institutions/authorities shall remain operational”.

“Moreover, all annual and supplementary examinations shall be conducted as per the approved schedule in all education institutes of Rawalpindi district,” it said.

Both notifications did not provide a reason for the holiday.

Meanwhile, a notice of expected partial closure was issued for the Rawalpindi-Islamabad metro system from Nov 26-28, as a result of expected “VIP movement”.

The notice warned of a possible suspension of the line from Kashmir Highway to the Pak Secretariat stations and said the closure of the last four stops was also under consideration.

The metro service from Saddar to Faiz Ahmed Faiz would remain operational, it added.

World.title: Meta battles political storm in India as Congress party sues, stages protests
World.content:
India’s main opposition party, the Indian National Congress, has sued Meta and the federal government, saying that an automated content-removal system is blocking political posts and images of ​opposition leader Rahul Gandhi ahead of state elections.

The filing takes a week-long Congress campaign against Meta from the streets to the courtroom, and highlights Prime Minister ‌Narendra Modi’s automated takedown mandate, under which the Facebook and Instagram parent has restricted more than 5.4 million posts in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025.

In a court filing dated Nov 25 in the Delhi High Court, seen by Reuters, Congress’s youth wing social media head Manu Jain said the rules have become “an instrument for the suppression of lawful political expression”.

The case leaves Meta’s operations ​in India, the company’s biggest market, caught between a government whose rules strip platforms of legal protection if they fail to comply, and an opposition demanding it ​push back.

Congress argues that Meta’s system is blocking posts that are not “exactly identical” copies of content previously ordered removed, including birthday greetings, tributes ⁠and a wedding invitation featuring Gandhi. Meta says it moderates content in India in accordance with the law.

Meta declined to comment. India’s IT and home ministries, which are named as co-respondents ​in the lawsuit, did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

Modi’s government has maintained that such laws are essential to prevent the proliferation of illegal and harmful content online in ​a market of over 1.1 billion internet users.

Congress is urging the court to strike down the mandate for automated takedowns and also order Meta to restore the posts, as well as disclose blocking criteria.

Hearings are expected to begin in the coming days.

‘Automated tools’ mandate

India amended its IT rules in February to require large platforms to use technical measures “including automated tools” to find and block any post “exactly identical” to content already removed ​under a court order or a written government notice. Before that, platforms were asked only to “endeavour” to use such tools.

To comply, Meta has been restricting “100 per cent identical copies of content, at ​scale and in country” under India’s amended IT rules, its transparency report shows. The company says it is still testing and refining the system given the “unprecedented nature of this effort”.

Meta says it is required ‌to automatically ⁠restrict content at scale in only a “limited” number of countries, which it says explains the higher volumes.

Congress says the automated system is catching far more than exact duplicates. It is blocking birthday greetings, tributes and even a wedding invitation because they carry the photograph or name of opposition leader Gandhi, while “no order, notice, reason or even a ‘legal request’ has been disclosed,” the petition said.

In one case cited in the petition, a Nov 8 birthday greeting from a youth wing leader to a colleague, showing the colleague standing beside Gandhi, was blocked the same day.

“We ​restricted access to this content through an automated ​system implemented pursuant to legal requirements,” ⁠the notice to the user read.

India is also one of seven markets, including Brazil and Hong Kong, where Meta does not tell users which government authority sought a restriction, citing “legal obligations and regulatory considerations”, its transparency report shows. Elsewhere, it does so in most cases.

Wider offensive by Congress

The automated takedown system “distorts the level playing field” needed for a free and fair election, especially as party workers rely on Meta’s ​platforms to reach voters ⁠ahead of state polls due early next year, the petition says.

Facebook and Instagram have 400m and 515m users respectively in India, according to research firm DataReportal.

Congress has put up large hoardings in several cities depicting Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg in the traditional uniform of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, the ideological parent of Modi’s party.

Congress’s youth wing has protested near Meta offices and clashed with ⁠police in ​several cities in recent days. The BJP has accused the protesters of vandalising the offices of private companies.

At ​a closed-door meeting this week reported by Reuters, Congress told Meta to push back against first-instance takedown orders, as Elon Musk’s X has done, a source told Reuters. X is currently engaged in a legal battle against the government over ​its content-removal system.

Meta told Congress at the meeting that it was neutral towards all political parties and bound by local laws.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.
